pages.title: Start your plan and add a card
pages.body:
# Start your plan and add a card

Your price is set by the number of wells on your account, so the only choice on this screen is monthly or annual. Add a card and your one month free trial starts. You are not charged today.

## Pick monthly or annual

1. On the **Your plan** screen, select **Monthly** or **Annual** at the top. **Annual** is 2 months free.
2. Check **Wells on platform**. That number, and nothing else, sets the price shown.
3. Select **Continue to payment**.

The card below the buttons lists what is included: your billing rate, your monthly AI credits, and **One month free, cancel any time**. Prices do not include sales tax.

## Add your card

1. On the **Add your payment method** screen, type your card number, expiry date, CVC and postal code.
2. Select **Start free trial**.

**Start free trial** becomes available once the card box has finished loading. Your card is held by Stripe, the payment company WildcatIQ uses. The box says **Saved securely with Stripe**.

### What happens after

Your subscription starts in its free trial and your setup is finished. The screen reads **You're all set**. Select **Continue to your workspace** to go into WildcatIQ.

No money is taken today. The first charge is when the free month ends, and **Cancel plan** in **Settings** stops it before then. See [Manage your subscription and card](../your-account/manage-your-subscription-and-card.md).

If you add or remove wells later, your plan follows the new count automatically. You do not have to change anything.

## Change monthly or annual after you reach the payment screen

Reload the page. Setup reopens on **Your plan**, where you can switch and continue again. Nothing you entered on the payment screen is kept.

## If billing is not connected yet

Some workspaces see a note saying billing is not connected and a single **Continue** button instead of **Continue to payment**. Select **Continue** to finish setup now and add a card later from **Settings**.

Next: [Find the screen you need](find-your-way-around.md).

pages.title: Find the screen you need
pages.body:
# Find the screen you need

Every screen in WildcatIQ is in one menu. On a phone, tap the button at the far left of the bar across the top to open it. On a computer the menu is already down the left side of the page.

## Open the menu on a phone

1. Tap the button at the far left of the bar across the top. It sits to the left of the trail showing which screen you are on.
2. Tap the screen you want.
3. Tap the page beside the menu to put the menu away.

The menu slides in over the page, and the bar across the top stays on screen wherever you are, so the menu is always one tap away.

## Open the menu on a computer

The menu is down the left side of every page, so there is nothing to open. Select the same button at the far left of the top bar to shrink the menu to icons, and select it again to bring the words back. **⌘B** on a Mac and **Ctrl+B** on Windows do the same thing. Rest the pointer on the button and its label reads **Toggle Sidebar**, which is what the menu is called in the app.

## What is in the menu

Four groups, in this order.

**Workspace**

- **Orion**: the assistant. Ask it questions about your operation in plain English.
- **Dashboard**: charts and totals for the whole operation.
- **Projects**: work you are tracking to a schedule.
- **Files**: documents and folders.
- **Notes**: written notes.
- **Agenda**: your calendar.
- **Messages**: chats with the rest of your team.

**Operations**

- **Leases**: your leases and what is on them.
- **Production**: wells, batteries, tanks and meters, and the readings entered against them.
- **Disposal**: saltwater disposal wells, tanks and meters.
- **Facilities**: a map of what flows into what.
- **Inventory**: equipment and parts.
- **Recon**: every well in the Texas record on a map, including other operators'.

**Finance**

- **Revenue**: revenue and purchaser settlement statements.
- **Invoices**: vendor invoices.
- **Prices**: posted and projected oil and gas prices.

**Admin**

- **People**: who is in the workspace and what each person can do.
- **Reports**: production and financial reports.

You see the screens your account has permission for, so your menu can be shorter than this list. See [A screen or button is missing](../getting-help/a-screen-or-button-is-missing.md).

## Settings, help and support

These sit in the account menu. Select your picture in the top right corner, on a phone as well as a computer. It holds:

- **AI Credits**, with **Buy more** to top them up.
- **Workspace**, with **Switch** if you belong to more than one. See [Switch between workspaces](switch-between-workspaces.md).
- **Help docs**.
- **Settings**.
- **Chat with support**.
- **Sign out**.

## The rest of the bar across the top

Left to right, after the menu button:

- The trail showing where you are, such as **Production** and then the well you have open. Select an earlier part of the trail to go back to it.
- The current oil and gas prices. These show on a wide screen when your account can view pricing.
- The microphone, to talk to Orion instead of typing.
- The Orion button, which opens the assistant in a panel beside whatever you are looking at.
- The bell, for your alerts.
- Your picture, which opens the account menu.

The microphone and the Orion button are there if your account can use the assistant.

pages.title: Import your wells from the Railroad Commission
pages.body:
# Import your wells from the Railroad Commission

WildcatIQ looks your company up in the Texas Railroad Commission's records and offers to create your leases and wells for you. Confirm which operator you are, check the list, and nothing is created until you select the import button at the bottom.

This happens once, during setup, right after you enter your company details.

## Confirm which operator you are

1. On the **Is this you?** screen, read the highlighted card at the top. It shows the operator name, the city and state, the P-5 status, the operator number, how many wells are on file, and the people listed on the filing under **Associated Persons**.
2. If that is your company, select the card. It reads **Yes, this is us →**.
3. If it is not, look under **Not you? These also came close.** and select the right one there.

The card you select reads **Bringing in your wells and leases…** while it loads. This is the longest wait in setup. Leave the page open.

## Search when nothing matched

If WildcatIQ could not find you, the screen reads **Let's find your company** and the search box is already open. From the **Is this you?** screen, select **None of these. Search for my company** to open it.

1. Type your company name in **Search by company name**. Type at least two letters.
2. If you know your P-5 number, type it in **RRC no. (optional)** instead. Type at least three digits. When both boxes are filled, the number is used and the name is ignored.
3. Select **Search**.
4. Select your company from the results.

## Review the wells before they are created

The **Here's what we found** screen lists your wells grouped by lease, as the Railroad Commission has them on file.

1. Select a lease row to open or close it and see its wells.
2. Correct any well name in the **Well** box, and any county in the **County** box.
3. Uncheck any well you do not want. Uncheck a lease row to uncheck all of its wells at once.
4. Select the trash icon at the end of a row to drop that well from the list entirely.
5. Select the button at the bottom. It reads **Import 42 wells across 9 leases**, with your own numbers.

Wells that are plugged start unchecked, because nothing is producing behind them. Check them if you want them on your books. Inactive wells start checked.

**API**, **Depth** and **Status** are shown so you can recognize a well. Correct them on the well's own page once setup is finished.

A **Multi** tag means the well is completed on more than one lease and WildcatIQ had to file it under one of them. On a computer, rest the pointer on the tag to see the others.

The button reads **Select at least one well** until something is checked. **Back** returns you to **Is this you?** to pick a different operator.

If the Railroad Commission has more wells on your P-5 than the list shows, a note at the top says how many there are in total and how many are listed. Import these now and add the rest yourself later, or contact support and they will bring in the rest.

### What happens after you import

Your leases and wells are created and appear under **Leases** and **Production**. Everyone in your workspace can see them. The number of wells you imported sets your subscription price, which you see on the next screen. See [Start your plan and add a card](choose-a-plan-and-add-a-card.md).

Nothing here is permanent. You can rename, add and remove wells afterwards, and your plan follows the well count automatically.

## Skip the import and type a count instead

1. On the **Is this you?** or **Let's find your company** screen, select **Skip, I'll add my wells myself**.
2. On **How many wells do you operate?**, type the number in **Wells**. Count every well you operate, including shut in and inactive ones. It must be at least 1.
3. Select **Continue**.

You land on the same question if the operator you confirmed has no wells on file. Your count sets your price, and you add the wells yourself later.

pages.title: Set up your company
pages.body:
# Set up your company

After you confirm your email, WildcatIQ asks for your name and phone, then for your company details. It uses those details to find your company in the Railroad Commission's records, so your wells can come in automatically.

Only the person who created the account does this. If someone invited you to their workspace, you skip setup and go straight into the app.

## Enter your own details

1. On the **Welcome, let's get you set up** screen, type your **First name**.
2. Type your **Last name**.
3. Type your **Phone number**.
4. Select **Continue**.

## Enter your company details

1. On the **Set up your workspace** screen, type your **Company name**.
2. Type your **Company address**. End it with your ZIP code, which helps match you to the right operator.
3. Type how many people work there in **Employees**. This one is optional.
4. If you know it, type your P-5 number in **RRC operator number (optional)**. Leave it blank and WildcatIQ searches by company name instead.
5. Select **Continue**.

The button keeps spinning for a few seconds while WildcatIQ searches the Railroad Commission's records, then shows you what it found. See [Import your wells from the Railroad Commission](import-your-wells-from-the-rrc.md).

Nobody else sees this screen and no one is emailed. Your company name and address can be changed later. See [Update your company details](../your-account/update-your-company-details.md).

## If you close the browser partway

Sign back in. Setup reopens at the last step you finished, with what you already saved filled in. If you had reached the company details, you land back there and select **Continue** again to redo the search.

pages.title: Sign in and confirm your email
pages.body:
# Sign in and confirm your email

Type your address and password on the WildcatIQ sign-in page and select **Sign in**. If you have just created an account, WildcatIQ holds you on a **Check your email** screen until you open the link it sent you.

## Sign in

1. Go to the WildcatIQ sign-in page. The heading reads **Welcome back**.
2. Type your address in **Email**.
3. Type your password in **Password**. Select the eye icon at the right of the box to see what you typed.
4. Select **Sign in**.

You land on your workspace, which for most people opens on Orion, the assistant screen. If you were sent to sign-in from somewhere else in WildcatIQ, you go back to that page instead.

To set a new password, select **Forgot password?** beside the **Password** label. See [Reset a password you forgot](../your-account/reset-a-password-you-forgot.md).

## Create an account

1. On the sign-in page, select **Sign up** at the bottom. The heading changes to **Join now**.
2. Type your address in **Email**.
3. Type a password in **Password**. Use at least 8 characters.
4. If someone referred you, select **Have a referral code?** and type it in **Referral code**. When the code is recognized, the screen names the company that referred you and the credit you both receive.
5. Select **Create account**.

You are signed in straight away and taken to the **Check your email** screen. The rest of WildcatIQ opens once your address is confirmed.

## Confirm your email address

1. Open the email WildcatIQ sent to the address you signed up with.
2. Select the link in it.

Open the link on the same device you signed up on and you go straight into setup. Open it on your phone or another computer and you land on the sign-in page with an **Email confirmed** banner and your address already filled in, so you only type your password.

The link is good for 7 days.

## Send the email again

1. On the **Check your email** screen, select **Resend the email**.
2. Wait for the button to stop counting down. It reads **Resend in 30s** until it is ready again.

The screen confirms the new link replaces the old one, so use the newest email. See [An email did not arrive](../getting-help/an-email-did-not-arrive.md).

Only you see any of this. Your teammates are not notified.

Next: [Set up your company](set-up-your-company.md).

pages.title: Switch between workspaces
pages.body:
# Switch between workspaces

Select your picture in the top right corner, then select **Switch** beside **Workspace**. WildcatIQ shows one workspace at a time, and everything on screen belongs to whichever one you are in.

**Switch** appears if your account belongs to more than one operator. Most people have one, and never see it.

## Switch

1. Select your picture in the top right corner.
2. Under **Workspace**, check the name shown. That is the one you are in now.
3. Select **Switch**.
4. In the **Switch workspace** panel, select the workspace you want.

Each row shows the workspace name and whether you are its **Owner** or a **Member**. The one you are in now has a check mark on the right.

### What happens after

The whole page reloads and you land on the same screen you get when you sign in to that workspace, which for most people is Orion. You do not come back to the page you were reading, so finish what you were doing first.

Your choice is remembered. It stays in place after you sign out, on your next visit, and on your other devices, until you switch again.

Nothing is shared between workspaces. Your teammates in either one are not notified.

## Choose a workspace when you sign in

If your account works with more than one operator and you have never picked one, signing in lands you on a **Choose a workspace** screen before the app opens.

1. Select the workspace you want to work in.

You go into that workspace. After this, WildcatIQ remembers and stops asking, and you use **Switch** in the account menu instead.

## Get into another workspace

You cannot create or join a workspace from the switcher. Someone in that workspace invites you, and it appears in your list once you accept.

pages.title: Add a well
pages.body:
# Add a well

Open the menu, select **Production**, and select **New Well** on the **Active Wells** tab. Type a name and select **Create well**. You need the **Add wells** permission to do this.

## Add the well

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the **Active Wells** tab. The page opens on it.
3. Select **New Well**.
4. Type the well's **Name**. This is the only box you have to fill in. **Create well** stays greyed out until it has a name.
5. Leave **Type** on **Production**. Choose **Disposal** for an injection well, which goes to the **Disposal** page instead of this list.
6. Fill in whatever else you know: **Formation**, **County**, **Wellbore profile**, **Depth (ft)**, **Date drilled**, **Perforations**, **Coordinates**, **API well #**. All of these are optional and all can be changed later.
7. Select **Create well**.

The well appears in **Active Wells** straight away, with its own page and its own folder in **Files**. Everyone in your workspace can see it. Nobody is emailed.

## If the well takes you past your plan

Before the well is created, a box may appear headed **Adding this well moves you to the next plan**. It says how many wells you have now, what the new price is, and how the difference is charged.

- Select **Upgrade and add well** to move up a plan and create the well in one step.
- Select **Cancel** to create nothing.

An owner or an admin gets the **Upgrade and add well** button. Everyone else sees **Ask an owner or admin to upgrade** and can only cancel.

## Setting the lease, the tanks and the meters

The **Lease**, **Oil tanks**, **Gas meters**, **Saltwater tanks** and **Disposal wells** boxes on this form offer **New lease**, **New tank**, **New meter** and **New disposal well**, which create a new one on the spot. To put the well on a lease, tank or meter you already have, create the well first and set it from the well's own page. See [Edit well details](edit-well-details.md) and [Assign wells, tanks and meters to a lease](assign-wells-tanks-and-meters-to-a-lease.md).

To let the state fill in the depth, formation, perforations and API number for you, see [Fill in well details from Railroad Commission records](fill-in-well-details-from-rrc-records.md).

pages.title: Assign wells, tanks and meters to a lease
pages.body:
# Assign wells, tanks and meters to a lease

A well or a tank goes on a lease from its own settings. A meter or a battery goes on a lease from the lease page's **Add** menu. Assigning only moves things: nothing is created and nothing is deleted. You need the **Manage leases** permission.

## Put a well on a lease

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the well's name, then the gear beside the name at the top of the page.
3. Set **Lease** to the lease you want. **Unassigned** takes it off every lease.
4. Select **Save**.

## Put a tank on a lease

1. Open the menu and select **Production**, then the **Tanks** tab.
2. Select the tank's name, then the gear beside the name at the top of the page.
3. Set **Lease**.
4. Select **Save**.

If the tank is in a battery that is on a lease, **Lease** is greyed out. The battery's lease decides it, so move the battery instead.

## Put a meter or a battery on a lease

1. Open the menu and select **Leases**, then select the lease.
2. Select **Add**, at the top right.
3. Select **Meter** or **Battery**.
4. In **Select**, choose one. Anything already on another lease reads **on another lease** after its name and can still be taken.
5. Select **Assign meter** or **Assign battery**.

Assigning a meter also pulls the wells that meter measures onto the lease. Assigning a battery brings its tanks onto the lease with it.

The **Add** menu holds **Note**, **File**, **Battery**, **Meter** and **Interest Owner**. Use the two sections above for a well or a tank.

## Take something off a lease

1. Open the lease.
2. Select the **Batteries**, **Tanks**, **Meters** or **Wells** tab.
3. At the right of the row, select the trash button.

The row comes off as soon as you select it. This only takes the item off the lease: the well, tank, meter or battery itself is kept, with all of its readings, and can be put on another lease afterwards. To put it back, assign it again.

Everyone in your workspace sees these changes. Nobody is emailed.

pages.title: Check what the state has on file for a lease
pages.body:
# Check what the state has on file for a lease

Open the lease and select **RRC record**, the small link under the lease name. It shows the Railroad Commission's own record: the operator, the field, the wells on file, and the production that has been filed.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Leases**, then select the lease. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **RRC record**, under the lease name beside the county.
3. If a record is already matched, **RRC lease record** opens straight onto it. Otherwise a search box opens with the lease's name in it.

## Match the lease to a state record

1. Correct the name in the box if you need to. The state files names its own way, so try the surname first, for example **YOUNG FANNIE**.
2. Select **Search**.
3. Read the results. Each one gives the name the state holds, then the commodity and number, the district, the operator and the field, for example **Oil 08440 · district 08 · operator 123456 · field 1234**. The same lease name can exist as both an oil and a gas record.
4. Select **This is it** on the right one.

The match is saved on the lease for everyone in your workspace. If nothing fits, **No RRC lease matches that name** appears; close the box and try a different spelling later.

To undo a match, open the box again and select **Remove match**, at the bottom right.

## If it says the record was derived

**Derived from a well on this lease, not confirmed here** means the record was found through one of the lease's wells rather than chosen by anyone. It is usually right. To pick a different one, select **Match a different lease** in that same line, then search and select **This is it**. **Back** returns you to the record.

## What the record shows

**Lease name**, **RRC key**, **District**, **Operator**, **Operator #**, **Field**, **Wells on file**, **Counties** and **Schedule**. A dash means the state has nothing in that box.

A red line saying the lease is flagged **SEVERANCE** appears when the Commission has severed it.

Under that, **Filed production** lists the last twelve months the state holds, with **Cycle**, **Oil (bbl)**, **Gas (mcf)** and **Filed**. The last two or three months normally read **not published**, because the Commission runs about three months behind. **not filed** means a report was never made for that month, which is not the same as a month that produced nothing, so those months show a dash rather than a zero.

These are the state's figures for the whole lease. They are not your own gauged production, and nothing here changes your readings or your revenue.

pages.title: Create a lease
pages.body:
# Create a lease

Open the menu, select **Leases**, then select **New Lease**. A name is all that is required. You need the **Manage leases** permission to create one.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Leases**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **New Lease**, at the top right.
3. Type the **Name**, for example **Smith A**. **Create lease** stays greyed out until it has one.
4. Type the **Lease number (optional)** if you have it, for example **12345**. Leaving it blank is fine, and blank leases do not clash with each other.
5. Type the **County**, for example **Reagan**.
6. Select **Create lease**.

The lease appears in the **List** tab and gets its own page and its own folder in **Files**. Everyone in your workspace can see it. Nobody is emailed.

The list puts your biggest earners first. A lease sits at the bottom until it has both estimated revenue and an operator interest recorded.

## What is not on the create form

**Status** and **Net revenue interest (NRI)** appear once the lease exists. To set them, select the gear beside the lease's name on its own page. That box, **Lease settings**, also carries **Sync with RRC**, which fills in **Lease number** and **County** from the state's record. Select **Save lease** when you are done.

## Deleting a lease

At the right of the lease's row on the **List** tab, select the trash button, then select **Delete lease**. The wells, tanks and meters on it are kept and simply stop being on that lease. The interest rows recorded against the lease are deleted with it, along with its comments. This cannot be undone.

## Next

- [Assign wells, tanks and meters to a lease](assign-wells-tanks-and-meters-to-a-lease.md)
- [Record interest owners and your net revenue interest](record-interest-owners-and-your-net-revenue-interest.md)
- [Check what the state has on file for a lease](check-what-the-state-has-on-file-for-a-lease.md)

pages.title: Delete a well
pages.body:
# Delete a well

Delete a well from the trash button on its row on the **Production** page. This cannot be undone, so retire the well instead if you only want it out of the way. You need the **Add wells** permission to delete a well.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Open the **Active Wells** or **Inactive Wells** tab, whichever holds the well.
3. At the right of the well's row, select the trash button.
4. Read the box, headed **Delete** followed by the well's name.
5. Select **Delete well**, or **Cancel** to keep it.

The row disappears at once and the well is gone from every list, every picker and the leases map, for everyone in your workspace. If the well counted towards your plan, your billed well count drops.

The tanks, meters and batteries the well ran to are kept, and anything that flowed through the well is joined back up around it. There is no undo in the app.

## A safer choice

If the well is shut in, plugged or sold but you want to keep its records where you can find them, set its status to **Inactive** instead. See [Retire or reactivate a well](retire-or-reactivate-a-well.md).

pages.title: Edit well details
pages.body:
# Edit well details

Open the well's own page and select the gear beside its name. Change what you need in the **Well settings** box and select **Save**. You need the **Add wells** permission to change a well.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the well's name in the **Active Wells** or **Inactive Wells** table.
3. Select the gear beside the well's name at the top of the page.
4. Change any of these: **Name**, **Lease**, **Type**, **Formation**, **County**, **Wellbore profile**, **Depth (ft)**, **Date drilled**, **Perforations**, **Coordinates**, **API well #**, **Oil tanks**, **Gas meters**, **Saltwater tanks**, **Disposal wells**, **Status**.
5. Select **Save**.

The change shows everywhere the well appears, for everyone in your workspace, as soon as you save. Nobody is emailed. To reverse an edit, open the box again and retype the old value.

## What some of these change

- **Name** also renames the well's folder in **Files**.
- **Oil tanks** sets which tank a gauge reading is converted with. Picking a tank copies that tank's barrels-per-inch onto the well, so oil entered in inches turns into the right number of barrels.
- **Type** moves the well between the **Production** and **Disposal** pages, and moves its files folder with it.
- **Status** takes the well off the **Active Wells** list. See [Retire or reactivate a well](retire-or-reactivate-a-well.md).

Set **Oil tanks**, **Gas meters**, **Saltwater tanks** and **Disposal wells** from the well's own page, which is where they are kept. The gear on a row in the **Active Wells** and **Inactive Wells** tables opens the same box for the boxes above it: **Name**, **Lease**, **Type**, **Status** and the well's details.

To have the state's record fill the boxes in for you, see [Fill in well details from Railroad Commission records](fill-in-well-details-from-rrc-records.md).

pages.title: Fill in well details from Railroad Commission records
pages.body:
# Fill in well details from Railroad Commission records

Open the well's settings and select **Sync with RRC**. It fills the boxes from the state's record, and the well is unchanged until you select **Save**.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the well's name, then the gear beside the name at the top of the page.
3. Check that **Name** or **API well #** has something in it. **Sync with RRC** stays greyed out until one of them does. The API number finds the right hole where a name may not.
4. Select **Sync with RRC**, at the bottom left of the box.
5. Read the small line that appears beside the button. It names the record that was used, for example **Matched Dollar 1 (API 42123456)**.
6. Check the boxes it filled. They are outlined in amber until you save.
7. Select **Save** to keep them, or **Cancel** to throw them all away.

Nothing is saved by the button itself. Once you save, the change shows everywhere the well appears, for everyone in your workspace.

## What it fills in

**Formation**, **County**, **Depth (ft)**, **Date drilled**, **Perforations**, **Coordinates**, **API well #** and **Wellbore profile**, plus **Lease** when the state's lease for that hole clearly matches one of your leases. Anything the state has not filed is left alone, so blanks can remain.

Typing in a box removes its amber outline. That is only the marking: the value stays as you left it.

## If it asks which well

**More than one well goes by that name. Which one?** appears with a button for each candidate, each reading like **Dollar 1 (API 42123456)**. Select one and the boxes refill from that record. This is common where a lease has two holes of the same name.

## Other messages

- **Enter a well name or API number first.** The box is empty.
- **The Railroad Commission has no record for that API number.** Check the digits.
- **No well matching "…" in your Railroad Commission records.** The state files names differently from the way you say them. Try the API number instead.
- **The Railroad Commission has no details on file for this well.** The state has the hole but nothing to fill the boxes with.
- **Could not tell which Railroad Commission operator this workspace is. Add your RRC operator number in Settings.** A name search needs your P-5 number. An API number search does not.
- **Railroad Commission records are unavailable right now. Try again shortly.**

## For a lease

A lease has the same button, in **Lease settings**: open a lease, select the gear beside its name, and select **Sync with RRC**. On a lease it fills only **Lease number** and **County**, and it works off the wells the state has under your operator number. Select **Save lease** to keep what it filled. See [Check what the state has on file for a lease](check-what-the-state-has-on-file-for-a-lease.md) for the full state record.

pages.title: Record interest owners and your net revenue interest
pages.body:
# Record interest owners and your net revenue interest

Open the lease, select **Add**, then **Interest Owner**. Your own share goes on the **Operator** row, and every net revenue figure on the lease is worked out from it. You need the **Manage leases** permission.

Interest is held per lease. Every well on the lease shares it.

## Add a holder

1. Open the menu and select **Leases**, then select the lease. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **Add**, at the top right, then **Interest Owner**.
3. In **Holder**, choose one of:
   - **+ Create new interest owner**,
   - **Operator (your own WI/NRI)**,
   - an owner already in your list.
4. If you chose to create one, type the **New owner name**, for example **Baldwin Family Trust**.
5. Choose the **Type**: **WI**, **RI**, **ORRI** or **NPRI**. The operator has no Type box, because the operator always holds a working interest.
6. Type the **Interest** as a decimal fraction. **0.125** is 12.5%. Anything above 1 is refused.
7. If the holder is the operator or a **WI** holder, type the **Net revenue** as a decimal fraction too. Royalty holders have no second figure: what they own is their revenue share.
8. Select **Save interest**.

An owner created here is added to your interest owners on the **People** page. Owners already on this lease are not offered again. Everyone in your workspace sees the holding. Nobody is emailed.

## Change a figure later

1. Open the lease and select the **Interest** tab.
2. Select the number in **Interest %** or **Net Rev %** and type the new one, as a percentage this time.
3. Press **Enter**, or select somewhere else, to save it.

Only a number you actually changed is saved. A figure that claims more than the whole lease is refused, a message says so, and the cell goes back to what it was. Royalty holders show a dash in **Net Rev %**, because their interest column is already their revenue share.

Selecting an owner's name opens their record, the same one the **People** page shows.

## Remove a holder

At the right of the row on the **Interest** tab, select the trash button. The holding comes off this lease as soon as you select it. The owner stays in **People**. To put it back, add it again.

## A shortcut for your own share

1. Open the lease and select the gear beside its name.
2. Type your share in **Net revenue interest (NRI)** as a decimal fraction, for example **0.78125**.
3. Select **Save lease**.

On a lease with no operator interest yet, that records you at 100% working interest with the NRI you typed. On a lease that already has one, only the net revenue figure changes and the working interest stays as it was. Either way it is the same row the **Operator (your own WI/NRI)** choice writes.

## Where the number shows up

Your operator NRI drives the **NRI** and **Net Rev. / mo** columns on the leases list, and the **Net Revenue Interest** and **Est. Net Monthly Rev.** cards on the lease page. Those read as a dash until an operator interest is recorded, because until then your share is unknown.

pages.title: Retire or reactivate a well
pages.body:
# Retire or reactivate a well

Set the well's **Status** to **Inactive**. It moves off **Active Wells** and onto the **Inactive Wells** tab, keeping all of its history. Setting it back to **Active** brings it back, and may ask you to move up a plan first.

## Retire a well

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the well's name on the **Active Wells** tab.
3. Select the gear beside the well's name at the top of the page.
4. In **Well settings**, set **Status** to **Inactive**.
5. Select **Save**.

The well leaves **Active Wells** and appears on **Inactive Wells**, where the **Last Active** column shows the last day it reported oil or gas. Everything it has is kept: production, tests, service, files and comments. A retired well no longer counts towards the number of wells your plan is billed for.

## Bring a well back

1. On the **Production** page, select the **Inactive Wells** tab.
2. Select the well's name, then the gear beside the name at the top of the page.
3. Set **Status** to **Active**.
4. Select **Save**.

Because a well coming back is a well your plan has to cover, a box headed **Adding this well moves you to the next plan** may appear before it is saved. It states your well count, the new price, and how the difference is charged. Select **Upgrade and add well** to accept, or **Cancel** to leave the well retired and keep the box as you set it. An owner or an admin gets that button. Everyone else sees **Ask an owner or admin to upgrade**.

Retiring and reactivating can be done as often as you like. Everyone in your workspace sees the change.

To take a well off the system altogether, see [Delete a well](delete-a-well.md).

pages.title: See your leases on the map
pages.body:
# See your leases on the map

Open the menu, select **Leases**, then select the **Map** tab. It draws your wells and the ground they sit on, using the state's own records.

## What you are looking at

- **Green dots** are producing wells, **blue dots** are injection wells, and **red dots** are wells marked inactive. An injection well stays blue whether it is active or not.
- **Amber outlines** are the survey tracts your wells sit in. The Railroad Commission publishes no lease boundaries, so these are the closest public record there is. A tract is usually bigger than the lease inside it, and one lease can cover several.
- Lease names appear on the tracts as you zoom in, and well names at closer zoom still.

## Using it

1. Select a tract or a well dot to open that lease's page.
2. Use **Map** and **Satellite**, at the bottom right, to change the background. It opens on **Satellite**.
3. Use the **−** and **+** buttons beside them to zoom.

On a computer, resting the pointer on a well dot shows its name, its API number, its lease, and its current oil and gas rate. Resting it on a tract lights up every tract belonging to that lease.

The map frames your wells when it loads and then leaves the view where you put it. Switching to **List** and back frames them again.

## Wells that do not appear

A well is placed by its **API well #** matched against the state's location records. A well with no API number, or one the state has no location for, is not drawn even though it is on the lease. Wells not on any lease are drawn.

To add API numbers, see [Fill in well details from Railroad Commission records](fill-in-well-details-from-rrc-records.md).

If the map says **Could not load well locations from the RRC**, the state records could not be reached. Try again later. Nothing is wrong with your wells.

pages.title: Call in a tank for pickup
pages.body:
# Call in a tank for pickup

Phone the purchaser yourself, then record the call: open the tank, select **Add**, then **Call-In**, and select **Record Call-In**. Wildcat keeps the record of the call. It does not place the call or notify the purchaser.

## Steps

1. Phone the purchaser and ask for the pickup.
2. Open the menu and select **Production**.
3. Select the **Tanks** tab.
4. Select the tank.
5. Select **Add**, then **Call-In**. The window names the gatherer this tank is set up with.
6. Check **Date** and **Time**. Both start at right now. Change them if you phoned earlier.
7. Type the number the purchaser read back in **Confirmation #**. Leave it empty if they did not give one.
8. Select **Record Call-In**.

## What happens next

An amber **Called in** badge appears under the tank name with the days waiting and the gatherer. A row is added to the **Call-Ins** tab showing **Waiting**, and the tank joins the **Tanks Called In** report under **Reports**, where everyone in your workspace can see it.

The badge stays until the crude is hauled. See [Mark a tank picked up](mark-a-tank-picked-up.md).

## If something looks wrong

- **The window names the wrong gatherer, or none.** Select the gear icon next to the tank name and set **Gatherer**. The gatherer is stored with the call as it stands at the moment you record it.
- **Call-In** is on the **Add** menu while the tank is not already called in. One open call at a time is enough to hold the tank's place in the queue.
- **You logged a call by mistake.** Open the **Call-Ins** tab and select the trash icon at the end of that row. It takes the tank back out of the pickup queue if that was its only open call, and it cannot be undone. The icon appears under the pointer, so remove a call-in from a computer.
- You need the **Manage oil production** permission to record a call-in. Ask whoever runs your workspace.

pages.title: Correct or delete a gauge reading
pages.body:
# Correct or delete a gauge reading

Open the tank's **Readings** tab, select the **⋯** at the end of the row, then **Edit** or **Delete**. Deleting cannot be undone.

## Correct a reading

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Tanks** tab.
3. Select the tank.
4. On the **Readings** tab, find the row by its **Timestamp**.
5. Select the **⋯** at the end of that row, then **Edit**. The window is headed **Edit Gauge Reading**.
6. Change **Date**, **Time** or **Gauge (in)**. **Derived volume** updates as you type.
7. Select **Save**.

## Delete a reading

1. Follow steps 1 to 5 above, and select **Delete** instead of **Edit**.
2. The row goes at once. You can also select **Delete** at the bottom left of the edit window.

## What happens next

Every figure built on the reading recalculates: the **Δ bbls** and **Impl bbl/day** on the rows around it, the **% Full** and **Current level** boxes, the chart, and the production on the wells this tank feeds. Everyone in your workspace sees the change.

A deleted reading is kept for the audit trail, so it still shows on the **Tank Measurement Audit** report under **Reports**. It counts toward no other figure.

## If something looks wrong

- **A row is tagged "at run time".** Its timestamp matches a haul exactly, so the run ticket's own open and close gauges are used instead of this reading. If you gauged before or after the truck, edit the row and correct the **Time**.
- **A tank holds one reading per date and time.** If another reading already sits on that exact minute, change the time on the one you are entering.
- You need the **Manage oil production** permission to change a reading. Ask whoever runs your workspace.

pages.title: Correct or delete a meter reading
pages.body:
# Correct or delete a meter reading

Open the meter, select the reading's row in the **Readings** tab, fix the numbers and select **Save**. To remove it instead, select **Delete** at the bottom left of the same box.

## Correct a reading

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Meters** tab.
3. Select the meter.
4. Stay on the **Readings** tab. Rows are newest first.
5. Select the row you need to fix. The box reads **Edit Meter Reading**.
6. Change **Date**, **Time**, **Gas (MCF)**, or any of **Orifice**, **Differential**, **Separator** and **Heater**.
7. Select **Save**.

The corrected row moves into date order in the table, and the cards above it recalculate. WildcatIQ records who made the change.

## Delete a reading

1. Open the reading the same way.
2. Select **Delete** at the bottom left.

The row goes at once. Deleting cannot be undone, so check the date before you select it. To put one back, add it again with the same date, time and volume.

## Who sees the change

Everyone in your company who can see this meter. Correcting or deleting a reading changes the gas figures on every well this meter is split across, and the revenue estimates that follow from them.

You need the **Manage gas production** permission to change a reading. Without it you can read the numbers.

pages.title: Enter daily production for a well
pages.body:
# Enter daily production for a well

You do not type a well's daily oil, gas and water on the well itself. WildcatIQ works them out from the tank you gauge, the gas meter you read, and the water the well is wired to, and shows the result on the well's **Production** tab.

## Where each number comes from

| Column on the well | Where you enter it |
| --- | --- |
| **Oil (bbl/d)** | Gauge the well's tank: [Record a tank gauge](record-a-tank-gauge.md). |
| **Gas (MCF/d)** | Read the well's gas meter: [Record a gas meter reading](record-a-gas-meter-reading.md). |
| **Salt Water (bbl/d)** | Read the saltwater tank or disposal meter the well runs to: [Record an injection reading](../saltwater-disposal/record-an-injection-reading.md). |

Gauge the tank and read the meter for the day, and the well's row for that day fills in on its own. Nothing else needs doing.

## See what a well made

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Stay on the **Active Wells** tab and select the well.
3. Stay on the **Production** tab. Days are newest first.
4. Select **Show more** at the bottom to load older days.

These rows are worked out from the tank and the meter rather than typed. To change one, correct the gauge or the meter reading and the row follows.

Below the daily rows is a band headed **Reported to the Railroad Commission · monthly average**. Those rows are what the state has on file for this well before your own records start, one per month. They are an estimate from the state's filings, not your measurements.

## If the numbers look wrong

- **Oil is missing or short.** The tank was not gauged that day, or the well is not on the tank. Check the tank's **Readings** tab first.
- **Gas is missing.** The meter has no reading for that day, or the well is not on that meter's split.
- **A day is down and should not be.** Check the **Downtime** tab: a shut-in day drops the well's share of the tank to nothing and hands it to the other wells. See [Record downtime or a shut-in](record-downtime-or-a-shut-in.md).
- **The last day looks like a part-day.** The most recent day is held back until the tank is gauged again, so a few hours of oil never shows as a whole day. The next gauge closes that day and the row returns in full.

pages.title: Fill in past readings from a document
pages.body:
# Fill in past readings from a document

Open the meter, select **Add**, then **History**, add the document and select **Upload & Parse**. WildcatIQ reads it and shows you the readings it found, and nothing reaches the meter until you select **Approve**.

Use this for a run of days you have on paper: a scanned gas chart, a month of daily MCF, a spreadsheet, a page of the pumper's book. For today's reading, [record it by hand](record-a-gas-meter-reading.md) instead.

## Send the document

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Meters** tab.
3. Select the meter the readings belong to.
4. Select **Add**, then **History**.
5. Select **Drag & drop files here** to take a photo or pick a file. You can add more than one, up to 100 MB in total.
6. Or, if the numbers are in an email or a text, copy them and paste them into the box. Pasted text counts as a document.
7. Select the X beside anything you added by mistake.
8. Select **Upload & Parse**.

Reading can take up to a minute. Leave the box open while it works.

## Check the readings before they save

When the reading finishes, a table of what was found opens over the page, headed **Add 30 meter readings?** or however many there are, and naming the file underneath.

1. Read down the rows. Every cell can be typed in, so correct anything that came through wrong.
2. Select the trash icon at the end of a row to drop that row.
3. A row tinted amber is one WildcatIQ was unsure about. Check it against the document before you approve.
4. Long documents come in pages of 25 rows. Use **Next** and **Previous** at the bottom to see the rest. Rows on the other pages are saved too.
5. Select **Approve**.

A line then tells you what happened, for example *Added 28 meter readings, skipped 2 as duplicates*. Days already on the meter are skipped rather than doubled up. Select **Done**.

## If nothing is found

The box says so and offers **Try another document**. Try a page that carries daily gas volumes, or a clearer photo. The file is stored either way.

If it says you are out of AI credits, select **Buy AI credits**. Your upload is not lost.

## Things worth knowing

- Nothing reaches the meter until you select **Approve**. Closing the box with the X throws the suggestions away, so review them while the box is open.
- Only the date, time and gas volume are saved. **Orifice**, **Differential**, **Separator** and **Heater** are not filled in from a document.
- Readings land on the meter you opened, never on another one, whatever name is printed on the page.
- Once approved, they behave like readings you typed: [correct or delete one](correct-or-delete-a-meter-reading.md) the same way.
- Reading a document uses your company's AI credits. Approving costs nothing more.
- You need the **Manage gas production** permission to approve meter readings.

## Documents about a well

On a well page, the **Add** menu has **File**, then **Upload document**. Select **Upload & scan** there and WildcatIQ suggests service jobs, downtime and equipment off the ticket instead. See [Log a service job](log-a-service-job.md) and [Record downtime or a shut-in](record-downtime-or-a-shut-in.md). Select **Just upload** to file the document without suggesting anything.

pages.title: Log a run ticket
pages.body:
# Log a run ticket

Open the tank, select **Add**, then **Run Ticket**. Fill in what the paper ticket says and select **Save 1** at the bottom right.

You can also photograph the ticket and let Wildcat fill the fields in for you: see [Read a run ticket from a photo](read-a-run-ticket-from-a-photo.md).

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Tanks** tab.
3. Select the tank.
4. Select **Add**, then **Run Ticket**.
5. Set **Date** to the day of the haul, and **Departure time** if the ticket shows one.
6. Type the printed number in **Ticket #**.
7. Leave **Type** on **Run (sale)** for oil sold to a purchaser. Use **Transfer** for a move between your own tanks, or **Disposition** for anything hauled off without a sale.
8. Enter the **Purchaser** and, if the trucking company is named separately, the **Transport company**.
9. Enter **Open gauge (in)** and **Close gauge (in)** from the ticket.
10. Enter **Gross barrels**.
11. Enter **BS&W (%)** and **API gravity (°)** if the ticket prints them.
12. Check **Net barrels (as printed)**. It fills itself from gross minus BS&W. If the ticket prints a different net figure, type that instead. The ticket always wins.
13. Select **Save 1** at the bottom right. The number is how many tickets it will write.

## Entering several tickets at once

Select **Add** in the row above the fields to start another ticket, and use the arrows to move between them. The line at the bottom left counts how many are ready, such as "3 tickets ready to save", and **Save 3** writes them all at once.

## What happens next

Each ticket appears on the **Runs** tab, and **Last run** at the top of the page updates. If both gauges are filled in, the **Barrels** column shows the drop between them rather than the gross figure you typed.

If the tank was called in and the ticket type is **Run (sale)**, the haul takes the tank out of the pickup queue and the amber **Called in** badge clears.

To fix a ticket later, select the **⋯** at the end of its row on the **Runs** tab, then **Edit** or **Delete**. Everyone in your workspace sees these rows.

## If something looks wrong

- **Save needs a volume.** A ticket needs **Gross barrels**, or both **Open gauge (in)** and **Close gauge (in)**. A ticket with neither is left out of the count.
- **BS&W warns about a fraction.** Enter it as a percent: `1.2` means 1.2%, not `0.012`.
- You need the **Manage oil production** permission to log a run ticket. Ask whoever runs your workspace.

pages.title: Log a service job
pages.body:
# Log a service job

Open the well, select **Add**, then **Service**, fill in **Job** and select **Add Service**. The job saves to the well's **Service** tab, and you can attach the vendor's ticket to it at the same time.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Stay on the **Active Wells** tab and select the well.
3. Select **Add**, then **Service**.
4. Type what was done in **Job**, for example *Pulled pump* or *Tubing test*. This is what names the row everywhere else.
5. Set **Date**.
6. Type what it cost in **Cost**. Dollar signs and commas are fine.
7. Pick who did it under **Vendor**. Select **Add new vendor** to type a name that is not in the list. If your company has no vendors saved yet, the box is already a plain typing box.
8. Add anything worth keeping in **Notes**.
9. Attach the ticket if you have it, using the steps below.
10. Select **Add Service**.

The page switches to the **Service** tab with the job in it.

## Attach the ticket or invoice

The attachment is optional. Under **Document** in the same box:

- Select **Upload the ticket or invoice** to take or pick a file from your phone.
- Or open **Or choose an existing well file** to use a document already on this well.

Select the X beside the file name to swap it for another.

The document is filed as it is. WildcatIQ does not read it or suggest records from it, because you are typing the job off it already.

## Open, change or delete a job

1. Open the well and select the **Service** tab.
2. Select the row.
3. Change **Job**, **Notes**, **Date**, **Vendor** or **Cost**.
4. Select **Save**.

**Delete** at the bottom left removes the job. Deleting cannot be undone. The attached document stays in the well's files.

Everyone in your company who can see the well sees the job, the cost and the ticket.

You need the **Manage well service** permission to log a job, and the **Files** permission to attach a document to it. Ask an admin in your company for them.

pages.title: Mark a tank picked up
pages.body:
# Mark a tank picked up

Open the tank and select **Mark Picked Up** at the top of the page. The tank leaves the pickup queue straight away, and the pickup is stamped as right now.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Tanks** tab.
3. Select the tank.
4. Select **Mark Picked Up**, next to the **Add** button.

## What happens next

The amber **Called in** badge disappears. On the **Call-Ins** tab, that row's **Picked Up** column fills in with the current date and time and **Waited** shows how many whole days the tank sat. The tank drops off the **Tanks Called In** report under **Reports**. Everyone in your workspace sees the change.

## If something looks wrong

- **Mark Picked Up** shows while the tank is called in. Once the badge is gone, the call is already cleared.
- **You cleared it too early.** Clearing cannot be undone. Record the call again with the original date and time: see [Call in a tank for pickup](call-in-a-tank-for-pickup.md). The closed row stays in the **Call-Ins** history.
- A run ticket of type **Run (sale)** on this tank also clears the badge. See [Log a run ticket](log-a-run-ticket.md).
- You need the **Manage oil production** permission. Ask whoever runs your workspace.

pages.title: Read a run ticket from a photo
pages.body:
# Read a run ticket from a photo

Open the **Add Run Ticket** window and select **Attach a picture of the ticket** at the top. Wildcat reads the photo and fills in the fields below, so you only have to check them and save.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Tanks** tab.
3. Select the tank.
4. Select **Add**, then **Run Ticket**.
5. Select **Attach a picture of the ticket** at the top of the window, then take or choose the photo. A PDF works too.
6. Wait while it says "Reading ticket…". This takes a few seconds.
7. Check every filled field against the paper ticket, especially **Gross barrels**, **Net barrels (as printed)** and **BS&W (%)**. Correct anything that is wrong by typing over it.
8. If the counter above the fields reads something like "1 of 3", the photo held more than one ticket. Use the arrows to check each one.
9. Select **Save** at the bottom right. It counts what it will write, so three tickets read **Save 3**.

## What happens next

The photo is stored with every ticket it produced. To see it again, open the **Runs** tab and select the paperclip at the end of the row.

Nothing is saved until you select **Save**. Selecting **Cancel** throws the photo away.

## If something looks wrong

- **It says no run tickets were found.** The fields stay blank and you can type the ticket in by hand. The photo still attaches when you save. See [Log a run ticket](log-a-run-ticket.md).
- **It says the file is too large, or that reading timed out.** Take the photo again at a lower size, or photograph one page at a time.
- **It reads the wrong numbers.** Type over them. What is in the field when you save is what gets stored.
- **The attach area is for new tickets.** When you are correcting an existing ticket, that ticket already has its own source document.

pages.title: Record a fluid shot
pages.body:
# Record a fluid shot

Open the well, select **Add**, then **Shot**, type the depths and select **Add shot**. The shot saves to the well's **Shots** tab and everyone in your company who can see the well sees it.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Stay on the **Active Wells** tab and select the well.
3. Select **Add**, then **Shot**.
4. Set **Date**. **Time** is optional.
5. Type feet from surface to fluid in **Fluid level (ft)**.
6. Type the pump setting in **Pump depth (ft)**.
7. **Fluid over pump** appears once both are filled in. Check it against what you expected before saving.
8. Add anything worth keeping in **Notes**.
9. Select **Add shot**.

The page switches to the **Shots** tab with the new shot in date order, newest first.

## Fix a shot

Change it straight in the table. There is no separate edit box.

1. Open the well and select the **Shots** tab.
2. Select the cell you need to change: **Date**, **Time**, **Fluid level (ft)**, **Pump depth (ft)** or **Notes**.
3. Type the new value.
4. Select outside the cell, or press Enter.

The change saves when you leave the cell. **Fluid over pump (ft)** recalculates on its own and cannot be typed in.

## Delete a shot

1. Open the well and select the **Shots** tab.
2. Move the pointer onto the row. An X appears at its right end.
3. Select the X.

The shot goes at once. Deleting cannot be undone. The X appears under the pointer, so delete a shot from a computer.

You need the **Manage well equipment** permission to add, change or delete a shot. Ask an admin in your company for it.

pages.title: Record a gas meter reading
pages.body:
# Record a gas meter reading

Open the meter, select **Add**, then **Reading**, fill in **Gas (MCF)**, **Cumulative**, or both, and select **Add Reading**. It saves straight away, and the wells this meter feeds pick it up.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Meters** tab.
3. Select the meter you are reading.
4. Select **Add**, then **Reading**.
5. Check **Date** and **Time**. They start at today and now. Change them if the reading is from an earlier day.
6. Type the day's gas in **Gas (MCF)**, the number on the meter in **Cumulative**, or both.
7. Fill in **Orifice**, **Differential**, **Separator** and **Heater** if you have them. They are optional.
8. Select **Add Reading**.

**Gas (MCF)** is the gas that meter made that day. **Cumulative** is the running total on the meter itself. They are two different numbers and neither one is worked out from the other, so fill in whichever you have.

## Why the cumulative number is worth writing down

The day's gas tells us what the meter was making when you looked at it. The cumulative number tells us how much gas has gone through in total, so the difference between two of them is the gas that actually passed the meter in between.

That matters on the days nobody reads the meter. With only the day's gas, a day you missed can do no better than hold the last number you wrote. With the cumulative number on either side of it, we know how much gas really went through and can share it out across those days.

It also catches drift. Daily numbers are estimates and run a little high or low; the meter's own total does not. When you record both, your day-to-day numbers are kept as they are and nudged so the month adds up to what the meter counted, which is the figure that shows up at settlement.

## Fill in from the previous reading

On a new reading, **Orifice**, **Differential**, **Separator** and **Heater** are already filled in from the reading before it, and a line under them reads *carried forward from* that date. Type over any of them to replace it.

**Gas (MCF)** and **Cumulative** are never filled in for you. If the volume is the same as last time, select **Same as previous** beside **Gas (MCF)** and it copies that number in. It works once the meter has an earlier reading with a day's gas on it to copy.

## Note a meter reset

1. Turn on **Meter reset** near the bottom of the form.
2. Set **Reset time**.

This marks the reading with an amber **reset** tag in the **Readings** tab. It applies to that reading only.

If you are recording **Cumulative**, a reset is picked up on its own: when the number is lower than the one before it, we treat it as a new meter rather than as gas going backwards, and start measuring again from the new reading.

## After you save

The reading appears in the **Readings** tab, which lists newest first, alongside the cumulative number if you entered one, and the cards above it update. Everyone in your company who can see this meter sees the reading, and it counts toward the gas on every well the meter is split across.

A meter holds one reading per date and time. To change a number you already saved, open that reading instead of adding a second one: [Correct or delete a meter reading](correct-or-delete-a-meter-reading.md).

You need the **Manage gas production** permission to add a reading. Ask an admin in your company for it.

pages.title: Record a tank gauge
pages.body:
# Record a tank gauge

Open the tank, select **Add**, then **Gauge Reading**. Enter the gauge in inches and select **Add Reading**. The barrels are worked out for you from the tank's strapping.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Tanks** tab.
3. Select the tank.
4. Select **Add**, then **Gauge Reading**. The window is headed **Add Gauge Reading**.
5. Check **Date** and **Time**. Both start at right now. Change them if you are entering a gauge you took earlier.
6. Type the gauge in **Gauge (in)**. Use inches as one number, with a decimal if you need it, such as `62.5`.
7. Check **Derived volume**. That is the barrels this reading stores.
8. Select **Add Reading**.

## What happens next

The reading appears at the top of the **Readings** tab with the change since the last one: **Δ in**, **Δ bbls**, **Hours since last** and **Impl bbl/day**. The **% Full**, **Current level** and **Est. bbl/day** boxes at the top of the page update, and the wells this tank is allocated to pick up the production.

Everyone in your workspace sees the reading. You can change or remove it later: see [Correct or delete a gauge reading](correct-or-delete-a-gauge-reading.md).

## If something looks wrong

- **Derived volume reads 0 bbl.** It is worked out from the tank's strapping. Select the gear icon next to the tank name and fill in **Strapping (bbl/in)**.
- **A tank holds one reading per date and time.** If you gauge the same tank twice in the same minute, change the **Time** on the second one.
- You need the **Manage oil production** permission to gauge a tank. Ask whoever runs your workspace.

pages.title: Record downtime or a shut-in
pages.body:
# Record downtime or a shut-in

Open the well, select **Add**, then **Downtime**, set **Start**, and select **Add Downtime**. The well's share of its tank and its gas meter drops to nothing for those days and goes to the other wells instead.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Stay on the **Active Wells** tab and select the well.
3. Select **Add**, then **Downtime**.
4. Choose **Type**. Use **Downtime** for a stoppage and **Shut-in** for a well that is off.
5. Set **Start**.
6. Set **End** if the well is back on. Leave **End** empty while it is still down.
7. **Days applied** fills in on its own once both dates are set, counting the first and last day. With no end date, type the number of days yourself.
8. Type why in **Reason**. This is what your team reads later.
9. Select **Add Downtime**.

## After you save

The page switches to the **Downtime** tab and the event joins the list, newest start date first. Everyone in your company who can see the well sees it.

Those days no longer count as producing days for this well. Where the well shares a tank or a meter with others, its volume for those days goes to the wells that were running, so the split changes for the period. Well tests and reports use the same figure.

## Remove an event

1. Open the well and select the **Downtime** tab.
2. Select the trash icon at the right of the row.

The row goes at once. Deleting cannot be undone. The days go back to counting as producing days.

## While a well is still down

Leave **End** empty. The event runs from **Start** to today and keeps growing until you set an end date. When the well comes back on, open the **Downtime** tab, delete the row, and add it again with both dates.

You need a production permission, such as **Manage oil production** or **Manage gas production**, to record downtime. Ask an admin in your company for it.

pages.title: Add a gas meter
pages.body:
# Add a gas meter

Open the menu and select **Production**, open the **Meters** tab, and select **New Meter**. Type a **Meter #**, tick the wells it measures, and select **Create meter**.

Water meters are added from the **Disposal** page. The **Meters** tab here lists gas meters.

## Add the meter

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the **Meters** tab.
3. Select **New Meter**.
4. Type the **Meter #**, the number the gatherer's statement uses. **Create meter** turns on once it has one.
5. Set **Lease**. The lease and the number together become the meter's name, for example **Dofflemeyer M1234**.
6. Under **Wells**, tick every well that sells through this meter.
7. Set **Gatherer** to the company that buys the gas, or leave it on **None**.
8. Select **Create meter**.

## What happens next

The meter is saved with its own page and its own folder under **Files**. The wells you ticked are split evenly across it, so two wells start at 50% each. To change the split, open the meter's page and select **Allocation**.

Everyone in your workspace can see the meter. Nobody is emailed.

## Add wells later

1. Open the **Meters** tab and select the meter's name.
2. Select the gear beside the meter's name.
3. Tick the wells under **Wells**.
4. Select **Save**.

A well joining a meter that already has wells starts at 0%, so set its share under **Allocation** afterwards.

## Water meters

1. Open the menu and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Meters** tab.
3. Select **New Meter** and type the **Meter #**.

A water meter reads a running total on the dial, and it feeds saltwater tanks and disposal wells instead of a gatherer.

You need a production permission such as **Manage gas production** to add or change a meter. Ask whoever runs your workspace if you do not have one.

pages.title: Add a tank
pages.body:
# Add a tank

Open the menu and select **Production**, open the **Tanks** tab, and select **New Tank**. Type a **Tank #** and select **Create tank**.

Saltwater tanks are added from the **Disposal** page. The **Tanks** tab here lists oil tanks.

## Add the tank

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the **Tanks** tab.
3. Select **New Tank**.
4. Type the **Tank #**, the number painted on the tank. **Create tank** turns on once it has one.
5. Leave **Product** on **Oil**.
6. Set **Battery** to the battery the tank sits on, or leave it on **Standalone**. Use **New battery** inside the box to make one on the spot.
7. Set **Lease**. If the battery you picked is already on a lease, this fills in and greys out, because a tank on a battery follows its battery's lease.
8. Set **Gatherer** if a hauler runs this tank, or leave it on **None**.
9. Fill in **Strapping (bbl/in)** and **Capacity (bbl)** if you know them. Both can be set later. See [Set a tank's strapping and capacity](set-a-tanks-strapping-and-capacity.md).
10. Select **Create tank**.

## What happens next

The tank is saved with a name built from its lease and its number, for example **Roach T123**. It gets its own page and its own folder under **Files**. Everyone in your workspace can see it. Nobody is emailed.

## Say which wells fill it

Oil is divided between wells at the battery, so put the wells on the battery the tank sits on. See [Group tanks into a battery](group-tanks-into-a-battery.md).

For a tank that stands on its own, open the tank's page, select the gear beside its name, and tick the wells under **Wells**.

## Saltwater tanks

1. Open the menu and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Tanks** tab.
3. Select **New Tank**.
4. Fill in **Tank #**, **Lease**, **Strapping (bbl/in)** and **Capacity (bbl)**.
5. Set **SWD Well (disposal)** to the disposal well the tank feeds.
6. Select **Create tank**.

You need a production permission such as **Manage oil production** or **Manage disposal** to add a tank. Ask whoever runs your workspace if you do not have one.

pages.title: Connect two pieces of equipment
pages.body:
# Connect two pieces of equipment

Open the menu and select **Facilities**, then drag one card onto another to say the first one feeds the second. The connection is made in the stream showing in the box at the top left, so set that to **Oil**, **Gas** or **Saltwater** first.

## Drag one card onto another

1. Open the menu and select **Facilities**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Choose the stream in the box at the top left.
3. Press and hold on the card the stream comes FROM, then drag it over the card it goes TO. The target card lights up.
4. Let go.

The line appears straight away, and the card you dragged returns to its place in the flow. The connection carries the whole stream, at 100%. To split it between several feeders, open the card it feeds and use its **Allocation** tab. Tanks, meters and batteries have one.

## Drag out of a port

The small dots on the left and right edge of a card are its ports. Point at the card to see all of them.

1. Press and hold on the dot on the RIGHT edge of a card. That side is what the facility feeds.
2. Drag the line onto another card and let go.

Pull from the dot on the LEFT edge instead and the connection runs the other way: whatever you drop on now feeds this card. To back out of a line you have started, let go over empty background.

## Put a facility in the middle of an existing line

Use this when a meter or a tank was always in the line and is only now being recorded.

1. Press and hold on the card you want to stand in the middle, and start dragging.
2. Circled **+** marks appear in the middle of the lines you can drop it into.
3. Drop the card on the **+** of the line it belongs in.

The two new legs are drawn first and the old line is taken out afterwards, so the stream stays connected the whole time. Single lines carry a **+**. A line that gathers three or more feeders into one junction does not, and neither does a line already touching the card you are dragging.

## Wire a whole chain at once

1. Select **New connection** at the top right.
2. Under **From**, select the facilities the stream starts at. Several is normal, for example six wells.
3. Under **To**, select what they feed.
4. To carry the chain further, select **Add step** and fill in the next stop, for example the disposal well the battery injects into.
5. Use the grip at the left of a step to drag it into a different position, and the **X** to remove a step you added.
6. If something you need does not exist yet, select **New facility** beside **Add step** and make it without leaving the box.
7. The line at the bottom left counts what you are about to draw, for example **6 connections**. Select **Connect**.

Every pairing between one step and the next becomes a connection. Where several facilities feed the same one, they are split evenly between them.

You can also start from one facility: select its card, and on the **Connections** tab select **Add** beside **Inflow** (things that feed it) or **Outflow** (things it feeds). That facility is filled in for you.

## Remove a connection

1. Select the card at either end.
2. On the **Connections** tab, find the row under **Inflow** or **Outflow**.
3. Select the trash icon on that row.

The line goes at once, for everyone. There is no undo, so draw it again if you remove the wrong one.

A row with no trash icon comes from a split that is set somewhere else, such as a tank's own allocation. Change it where that split lives.

## What happens next

The wiring you draw here is the wiring the rest of WildcatIQ allocates on, so a connection changes what the well, tank, meter and battery pages report. Everyone in your workspace sees it.

You need **Manage facilities** to draw or remove connections.

pages.title: Delete a tank, meter or battery
pages.body:
# Delete a tank, meter or battery

Point at the row on the **Production** page, select the trash icon at the right end, and confirm. The row leaves every list in WildcatIQ.

## Delete it

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the **Tanks**, **Meters** or **Batteries** tab.
3. Point at the row. A gear and a trash icon appear at its right end.
4. Select the trash icon.
5. Read the box that opens. It is headed **Delete Roach T123?** with the real name in it.
6. Select **Delete tank**, **Delete meter** or **Delete battery**.

The row disappears at once. Everyone in your workspace sees it go.

## What is kept and what is lost

The facility is hidden, and the record behind it is kept. Its gauge readings, run tickets, allocations, notes and files stay on that record. Contact support to bring a deleted facility back.

Deleting a battery keeps its tanks. They stay in the **Tanks** tab, and the confirmation says how many.

Where something fed the facility and the facility fed something else, the two ends are joined directly, so the stream stays whole on the **Facilities** map.

## Delete from the map instead

1. Open the menu and select **Facilities**.
2. Select the card.
3. Select the trash icon at the top right of the box that opens.
4. Select **Delete**.

A haul-off is a company shared by every facility that hauls to it, so haul-offs are deleted from the menu under **People**, on the **Purchasers** tab.

## Retiring instead of deleting

A tank you no longer use can be marked inactive: open the tank's own page, select the gear, set **Status** to **Inactive**, and select **Save**. A battery has an **Active** tick box in the same place on its own page.

You need a production permission such as **Manage oil production**, **Manage gas production** or **Manage disposal** to delete. Ask whoever runs your workspace if you do not have one.

pages.title: Group tanks into a battery
pages.body:
# Group tanks into a battery

Open the menu and select **Production**, open the **Batteries** tab, and select **New Battery**. Name it, tick the tanks that belong to it, and select **Create battery**.

A battery is the station its tanks sit on, and for oil it is where production is split between wells.

## Make the battery

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the **Batteries** tab.
3. Select **New Battery**.
4. Type the **Name**, for example **North Battery**. **Create battery** turns on once it has one.
5. Set **Lease**. Every tank on the battery follows this lease.
6. Under **Tanks**, tick each tank that belongs to the battery. A tank already on another battery shows that battery's name on its row.
7. To add a tank that does not exist yet, select **New tank** at the bottom of the list, type its **Tank #**, and select **New tank**. It joins the battery straight away.
8. Select **Create battery**.

The battery appears in the **Batteries** table at once, with its own page and its own folder under **Files**. Everyone in your workspace can see it.

## Move a tank onto a battery later

1. Open the **Batteries** tab and select the battery's name.
2. Select **Add**, then **Tank**.
3. Search for the tank and select it. A tick appears on the row, and the dialog stays open so you can add more.

Each tank you add moves onto the battery's lease, and its name changes to match. A tank sits on one battery at a time, so adding it here takes it off the one it was on.

## Put the wells on the battery

Oil is divided between wells at the battery, so this is the step that makes a well's oil appear.

1. Open the **Batteries** tab and select the battery's name.
2. Select **Add**, then **Well**.
3. Search for the well and select it.
4. Select **Allocation** at the top of the page to set each well's share of the battery.

A well added this way starts at 0%, so set its share before you rely on the figures.

## Rename a battery, or set its disposal well

Open the **Batteries** tab, select the battery's name, and select the gear beside the name at the top of that page. Change **Name** or **Disposal well**, then select **Save**.

You need a production permission such as **Manage oil production** to make a battery or change what is on it.

pages.title: Move equipment to a different lease
pages.body:
# Move equipment to a different lease

Open the facility's own page, select the gear beside its name, change **Lease**, and select **Save**. A tank and a meter take half of their name from their lease, so moving one renames it.

## Move a tank

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the **Tanks** tab, then the tank's name.
3. Select the gear beside the tank's name.
4. Change **Lease**.
5. Select **Save**.

If **Lease** is greyed out, the tank is on a battery and follows that battery's lease. Move the battery instead.

## Move a battery

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Batteries** tab, then the battery's name.
3. Select the gear beside the battery's name at the top of that page.
4. Change **Lease**.
5. Select **Save**.

Every tank on the battery moves with it.

## Move a meter

1. Open the menu and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Meters** tab, then the meter's name.
3. Select the gear beside the meter's name.
4. Change **Lease**.
5. Select **Save**.

## Or drag it on the map

1. Open the menu and select **Facilities**.
2. Press and hold on the card, and drag it into the grey panel of the lease you want it on. The panel lights up when the drop will take.
3. Let go.

A panel lights up when everything in it sits on one lease. Dragging a tank that sits on a battery moves the whole battery, and every other tank on it. Haul-off cards stay on the map where they are, because a haul-off is a company rather than something on a lease.

## What happens next

A tank or a meter is renamed from its new lease and its number, so **Roach T123** becomes **Dofflemeyer T123**. A battery keeps the name you gave it, and its tanks are the ones that get renamed. It moves to the new lease's panel on the map and to the new lease's page under **Leases**. Everyone in your workspace sees the change as soon as it saves.

Its readings, run tickets, wells and connections are untouched. There is no undo. To reverse it, set the old lease back the same way.

You need **Manage facilities** to drag a card between leases.

pages.title: See where your oil, gas and water go
pages.body:
# See where your oil, gas and water go

Open the menu and select **Facilities**. It draws one stream at a time as a map that runs left to right, from each producing well through every tank, meter and battery its stream passes on the way out.

## Read the map

1. Open the menu and select **Facilities**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Use the box at the top left to choose the stream: **Oil**, **Gas** or **Saltwater**. Green is oil, red is gas, blue is saltwater.
3. Use the box beside it to narrow the map to one lease, or leave it on **All leases**.
