4. Drag the background to move the map. Use the mouse wheel, or the **+** and **-** buttons at the bottom right, to zoom. The button beside them fits everything back on screen.

Each grey panel is a lease, named along its top. Cards inside it are the facilities, joined by lines that run in the direction the stream flows. A card with a dashed edge and **other lease** under its name sits on a different lease and is drawn because something on this one feeds it.

## What the number on a card means

- A well shows what it makes per day of the stream on screen, in **bbl/d** for oil and saltwater and **mcf/d** for gas.
- A tank shows how full it is, as a percentage. It needs a capacity to show one. See [Set a tank's strapping and capacity](set-a-tanks-strapping-and-capacity.md).
- A gas meter shows **mcf/d** and a water meter shows **bbl/d**. Both are a fourteen-day average.
- A number on a line is what that leg carries. The first leg out of a well has none, because the well's card beside it already carries that number.

On a wide screen, the card in the middle of the top bar totals the whole company: **Oil**, **Gas** and **Saltwater**. It covers every lease, whatever the lease box beside it is set to.

## Find one facility

1. Type into **Search facilities** at the top right.
2. Select a result. The map centres on that card and switches the lease box to **All leases** so the card is in view.

## Look at one facility

Select a card. Everything one step from it stays sharp and the rest of the map fades, and a box opens with its tabs:

- **Connections** lists what feeds it under **Inflow** and what it feeds under **Outflow**, for all three streams together.
- **Settings** is the same settings form the facility's own page uses.
- **Allocation** is the split its volume is divided by. Tanks, meters and batteries have this tab. Wells do not.

The arrow at the top right of that box opens the facility's own page in a new tab. Select the empty background to close the box and bring the whole map back.

## Bring the numbers up to date

Select the circular arrow at the bottom left. It re-reads the production figures behind the cards and keeps your stream, lease and zoom as they are.

## When a lease has nothing on it

A card reading **No oil facilities** means nothing on this lease carries that stream yet. Use **New facility** to add the wells, tanks and meters, and **New connection** to wire them together. See [Connect two pieces of equipment](connect-two-pieces-of-equipment.md).

Everyone who can view facilities sees the same map. **New facility**, **New connection** and the wiring gestures need **Manage facilities**.

pages.title: Set a tank's strapping and capacity
pages.body:
# Set a tank's strapping and capacity

Open the tank's own page, select the gear beside its name, and fill in **Strapping (bbl/in)** and **Capacity (bbl)**. Strapping is how many barrels one inch of gauge is worth, and it is what turns every gauge you record into barrels.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Production**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the **Tanks** tab.
3. Select the tank's name in the table.
4. Select the gear beside the tank's name at the top of the page.
5. In **Strapping (bbl/in)**, type the barrels per inch from the tank's strapping chart. A new tank starts at **1**, which means one barrel per inch.
6. In **Capacity (bbl)**, type the tank's shell capacity, for example **210** for a 210 barrel tank.
7. Select **Save**.

## What happens next

Every gauge on this tank is converted at the new rate, including the ones already recorded. Barrels on the tank's readings, its chart, and the production figures that come off it are all restated. If a well's oil is entered in inches and it runs to this tank, that well converts at the new rate too.

**Capacity (bbl)** drives the **% Full** column on the **Tanks** table, the fill bar on the tank's page, which turns red at 90% full, and the capacity line on its level chart. A battery draws its level line once every tank on it has a capacity.

Everyone in your workspace sees the new numbers as soon as you save. There is no undo. To reverse it, open the box again and type the old figure back in.

For a saltwater tank, open the menu and select **Disposal**, open the **SWD Tanks** tab, and select the tank's name.

pages.title: Finish an open well test
pages.body:
# Finish an open well test

Open the well, select the **Tests** tab, and select the card that reads **In progress**. Fill in the **Closing reading** block and select **Close test**.

Only an oil test can be left open. It waits on the closing gauges and starts counting once you enter them. Gas and saltwater cards on the **Tests** tab are already finished.

## Steps

1. Open the [menu](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md) and select **Production**.
2. Select the well's name on the **Active Wells** tab.
3. Select the **Tests** tab.
4. Select the card that reads **In progress**. Open cards sit first in the grid and have no colour behind them.
5. Under **Closing reading**, fill in the date, the time, **Feet** and **Inches** for the tank marked **Isolation**.
6. Fill in the same four boxes for every tank marked **Rest of the battery**.
7. Select **Close test**.

## What happens next

The card turns grey and swaps **In progress** for the well's oil rate in bbl/d and its share of the battery. The closing gauges are stored on each tank the same way a hand-entered gauge is, so they appear on the tank's **Readings** tab.

The battery's oil split gains a **Well test** period starting on the test's end date, and every period after it re-chains. Everyone in your workspace sees it. See [Understand why a well's numbers changed](understand-why-a-wells-numbers-changed.md).

## Read a finished test

The card is the record. An **Oil** or **Gas** card carries the rate, the share as a percentage, and the tank or meter the test was read against. A **Saltwater** card carries the rate and the barrels you caught.

The gauges behind an oil test live on the tank. Open the tank and select the **Readings** tab to see them at the times they were taken.

## Correct or delete a finished test

- **The gauges were wrong.** Correct them where they live, on the tank. Open the tank, select the **Readings** tab, and edit the reading at that date and time. Every test that covers the window follows the corrected reading.
- **The whole test was wrong.** Hover the card, select the trash icon, and record the test again. The card goes immediately, and there is no confirmation step.

Deleting a test leaves the gauges on the tank untouched. It removes the test's own record, and the splits that were built from it are worked out again the next time the page loads. That can change what other wells on the battery were credited with, so it is worth telling whoever handles your revenue.

## If something looks wrong

- **Close test is greyed out.** The closing block needs a date on the isolation tank's row.
- **The card you want is not there.** Tests are listed on the well they were recorded on. A test run on a sibling well shows on that well's page, and on the battery's **Well Tests** tab.
- **"Test saved. Some gauges were already recorded."** A reading already sat on that tank at that exact date and time. The test is saved. Select **Done**, then set the reading right on the tank's **Readings** tab.

pages.title: Run a gas well test
pages.body:
# Run a gas well test

Open the well, select **Add**, then **Well test**, then **Gas**. Enter the window you had the well shut in and what the meter read while it was off, then select **Save reading**.

A gas meter reads one total for every well on it, so a well's gas is the drop the meter takes when that well alone is shut in. Somebody has to open the test on the meter first with an all-wells-on baseline. See [Split gas production between wells](split-gas-production-between-wells.md).

## Steps

1. Open the [menu](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md) and select **Production**.
2. Select the well's name on the **Active Wells** tab.
3. Select **Add**, then **Well test**, then **Gas**.
4. Under **Meter**, pick the meter you tested against. If the well feeds only one, it is already selected.
5. Read **Baseline, all wells on (MCF/d)**. It carries the figure already on the open test. Type over it only if you measured a better one.
6. Fill in **Start date** and **Start time** for the moment you shut the well in.
7. Fill in **End date** and **End time** for the moment you brought it back.
8. Type what the meter was making with the well off in **Meter rate with this well shut in (MCF/d)**.
9. Read **This well's share**. That is the percentage this reading gives the well.
10. Select **Save reading**.

## What happens next

The reading is added to the open test on that meter. The well's **Tests** tab gets an orange **Gas** card holding the drop in mcf/d, the share, and the meter's name.

The split does not change yet. It changes when the test is published on the meter's page, which is also where the shut-ins for the other wells are gathered.

Everyone in your workspace sees the reading. To replace it, record another one for the same well: the message **This well already has a reading on the open test, so saving replaces it** tells you when that is what will happen.

## If something looks wrong

- **"This well isn't allocated to a gas meter, so there is nothing to test against."** Add the well to the meter first: open the meter, select **Add**, then **Add Well**.
- **"No gas test is open on this meter."** Open one from the meter's page: select **Allocation**, then **Add well test**, enter the baseline and select **Save draft**. Then come back here.
- **Save reading is greyed out.** It needs an open test on the meter, a baseline, an end that is after the start, and a rate.
- **The share reads 0%.** The meter read the same or more with the well off than with it on. Check that you typed the shut-in rate and not the baseline.

pages.title: Run a saltwater bucket test
pages.body:
# Run a saltwater bucket test

Open the well, select **Add**, then **Well test**, then **Saltwater**. Enter the day you caught the water, how many barrels you caught, and how long you held the bucket under it.

A bucket test is the whole procedure: a few minutes at the wellhead with a bucket and a watch. There is no second trip and no tank to gauge.

## Steps

1. Open the [menu](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md) and select **Production**.
2. Select the well's name on the **Active Wells** tab.
3. Select **Add**, then **Well test**, then **Saltwater**.
4. Set **Date** to the day you caught the water.
5. Type the barrels you caught in **Water caught (bbl)**.
6. Type how long you held the bucket in **Minutes** and **Seconds**. The seconds matter. On a three minute catch, thirty seconds out moves the answer by about a sixth.
7. Read **Water** and **Per hour** underneath. Those are the rates this test gives the well.
8. Select **Save in progress**.

The button reads **Save in progress**. A bucket test is complete the moment you save it, and the card it creates is a finished test.

## What happens next

The well's **Tests** tab opens with a blue **Saltwater** card holding the rate in bbl/d and the barrels you caught.

Every tank and meter the well is attached to re-splits its water from this test, from the test's date forward. Each well's share is its latest test rate against the total of its group's latest rates. See [Split water between wells](split-water-between-wells.md).

Everyone in your workspace sees the test, and the water splits move for everyone. To back a test out, hover its card and select the trash icon. The card goes immediately, and there is no confirmation step.

## If something looks wrong

- **Save in progress is greyed out.** It needs a date, a barrel figure, and a duration above zero. A blank **Minutes** with only **Seconds** filled in is fine.
- **The well's water share did not move.** The well has to be attached to the tank or meter first. Only wells on that facility's well list take a share.
- **You caught it in a bucket, not in barrels.** Convert before you type. The box takes barrels, and the test does no conversion of its own.

pages.title: Run an oil well test
pages.body:
# Run an oil well test

Open the well, select **Add**, then **Well test**, then **Oil**. Pick the tank you routed the well to, gauge every tank on the battery at the start, come back at the end and gauge them all again.

An oil test measures one well's share of its battery. The well goes to one tank on its own while the rest of the battery keeps producing into the other tanks, and the two sides are compared over the same window.

## Before you start

Route the well to one tank at the battery, and know which other tanks the battery is still producing into. Gauge all of them.

## Steps

1. Open the [menu](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md) and select **Production**.
2. Select the well's name on the **Active Wells** tab.
3. Select **Add**, then **Well test**, then **Oil**.
4. Select the tank you routed the well to under **Isolation tank**. The rest of the battery's tanks appear underneath as soon as you pick it.
5. Under **Start**, fill in the date, the time, **Feet** and **Inches** for the tank marked **Isolation**.
6. Fill in the same four boxes for every tank marked **Rest of the battery**. Use the time you actually read each tank, not one time for all of them.
7. Select **Save in progress**.
8. Come back at the end of the test and finish it from the **Tests** tab. See [Finish an open well test](finish-or-reopen-a-well-test.md).

To enter the whole test in one sitting, fill in the **End** block as well and select **Save test**.

## What happens next

The well's **Tests** tab opens with an **Oil** card. While the test is open the card has no colour behind it and reads **In progress**. Once you close it, the card turns grey and carries the well's rate in bbl/d, its share of the battery as a percentage, and the isolation tank's name.

Each gauge you typed is stored as a normal reading on that tank, so it shows up on the tank's **Readings** tab and counts toward that tank's production like any other gauge.

Once the test is closed, the battery's oil split picks up a **Well test** period starting on the test's end date. See [Split oil production between wells](split-oil-production-between-wells.md).

Everyone in your workspace sees the test and the gauges. To back a test out, delete its card. The gauges stay on the tank. See [Finish an open well test](finish-or-reopen-a-well-test.md).

## If something looks wrong

- **The tank list says "Pick an isolation tank to gauge its battery."** No isolation tank is selected yet. Choose one at the top.
- **The Oil figure at the bottom is blank.** It needs a start date and time, an end date and time, and feet or inches in both blocks on the isolation tank.
- **"Test saved. Some gauges were already recorded."** A reading already sat on that tank at that exact date and time. The test is saved. Select **Done**, then set the reading right on the tank's **Readings** tab.
- **Tapping outside the window saved the test.** That is deliberate, so a stray tap does not cost you a trip to the battery. Anything with a start date is saved on the way out. Use **Cancel** if you want to throw the entry away.

pages.title: Split gas production between wells
pages.body:
# Split gas production between wells

Open the meter, select **Allocation**, select **Add date range**, and give each well a percentage that totals 100. To split it by measurement instead, select **Add well test** and run a shut-in test.

A gas meter reads every well on it as one total, so the split decides how much of that gas each well is credited with.

## Split it by typed percentages

1. Open the [menu](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md) and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Meters** tab.
3. Select the meter's name.
4. Select **Allocation**.
5. Select **Add date range**.
6. Select the arrow beside the new range to open it.
7. Set **From** to the first day this split applies, and leave **To** blank while it is still in force.
8. Select a well under **Well** and type its share under **Split %**.
9. Select **Add well** and repeat for each well. **Even split** fills the period with every well on the meter at an equal share.
10. Check that the **Total** line reads 100%.
11. Select **Save allocation**.

## Split it by a shut-in test

The test takes one baseline with everything running, then one reading per well with that well alone shut in. Each well's share is the drop the meter takes when it goes off.

1. On the meter's page, select **Allocation**, then **Add well test**.
2. In the **Baseline (all wells on)** card, fill in **Start date**, **Start time**, **End date** and **End time** for the window you read with everything running.
3. Leave **Rate from** on **MCF/day** and type the rate. Switch it to **Meter reading** to enter an **Open reading** and a **Close reading** instead and have the rate worked out over the window.
4. Select **Save draft**. The test is now open, and shut-ins can be added to it.
5. Add each well's shut-in here with **Add shut-in**, or let whoever is at the wellhead add it from the well's page. See [Run a gas well test](run-a-gas-well-test.md).
6. When every well but one has a shut-in, read the **Resolved split** panel at the bottom.
7. Select **Publish**.

**Add well test** reopens the draft when one is already open on this meter, so a half-finished test can be picked up later rather than started again.

One well can be left untested. It takes whatever the others did not account for. Testing every well is also fine, and the shares are then scaled to 100%.

## What happens next

A published test becomes a read-only **Well test** period on the meter's allocation, starting on its date, and the meter's gas is divided by it from then on. Each well's **Production** tab and revenue follow.

Everyone in your workspace sees it. To back it out, select the trash icon on the **Well test** card. That deletes the test as well as the period, and the days it covered fall back to whatever manual range covers them.

A published test stays as it is. To correct one, remove it with the trash icon and run a new test.

## If something looks wrong

- **Publish is greyed out.** The test needs a baseline with a real window and rate, and a shut-in for all but one of the meter's wells. Each shut-in must name a different well.
- **A shut-in shows "clamped to 0" in red.** The meter read higher with that well off than with everything on. That well gets nothing from this test. Check the readings before you publish.
- **"No derivable split from this campaign (check the baseline and shut-ins)."** That published test cannot produce percentages. Remove it with the trash icon and run a new test, or add a manual date range to cover those days.
- **There is no Allocation button.** You need the **Manage gas production** permission. Ask whoever runs your workspace.

pages.title: Split oil production between wells
pages.body:
# Split oil production between wells

Open the battery, select **Allocation**, select **Add date range**, and give each well a percentage. The percentages have to total 100 before the panel saves.

A battery's tanks measure everybody's oil together, so the split is what decides how many of those barrels land on each well. Oil splits live on the battery, not on the individual tank.

## Steps

1. Open the [menu](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md) and select **Production**.
2. Select the **Batteries** tab.
3. Select the battery's name.
4. Select **Allocation**.
5. Select **Add date range**.
6. Set **From** to the first day this split applies. Leave it blank to run from the start of the battery's record.
7. Leave **To** blank for a split that is still in force, or set the last day it applied.
8. Select a well under **Well**, then type its share under **Split %**.
9. Select **Add well** and repeat for each well on the battery. **Even split** fills the period with every attached well at an equal share.
10. Check the **Total** line at the bottom of the card. It has to read 100%.
11. Select **Save allocation**.

## Change a split that is already there

The panel opens with the period in force today unfolded and the rest folded, and every card reads read-only so a stray tap cannot move a percentage.

1. Select the arrow beside the date range you want, if it is folded.
2. Select **Edit** on the card.
3. Change the dates or the percentages.
4. Select **Save allocation**.

To remove the whole range, select **Edit** first, then the trash icon beside its dates, then **Save allocation**.

## Periods marked Well test

A card labelled **Well test** was worked out from the well tests on that battery, so its percentages cannot be typed over. Its **Edit** button opens the test that produced it. To replace it with figures of your own, add a date range starting after the test's date: on any day two periods cover, the one that starts later governs. See [Understand why a well's numbers changed](understand-why-a-wells-numbers-changed.md).

To move a split with measurements instead of typed numbers, run [an oil well test](run-an-oil-well-test.md) on each well.

## What happens next

Every barrel the battery's tanks recorded is divided by the split in force on the day it was gauged. Each well's **Production** tab, its rate boxes and its revenue all follow, and so does the battery's **Wells** tab.

Everyone in your workspace sees the change, and it applies to history as well as to today. You can undo it by selecting **Edit** on the card, putting the old figures back and saving again.

## If something looks wrong

- **Save allocation is greyed out and a red bar is showing.** Two of your manual date ranges cover the same day, or one of them does not total 100%. The bar says which.
- **A well is missing from the picker.** Wells already used in that period are hidden from the other rows so nobody takes two shares. Wells on other batteries sit under **All wells**.
- **A card shows "No positive test rates on this date."** The tests behind that period gave no usable rate. Add a manual date range to cover those days.
- **There is no Allocation button.** You need the **Manage oil production** permission. Ask whoever runs your workspace.

pages.title: Split water between wells
pages.body:
# Split water between wells

Attach the producing wells to the saltwater tank, then record a saltwater bucket test on each of them. The wells split the tank's water by the ratio of their latest test rates, and the split moves on its own as new tests come in.

There is no percentage to type for a water tank. The tests decide it.

## Steps

1. Open the [menu](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md) and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Tanks** tab, then the tank's name.
3. Select **Add**, then **Add Well**, and attach each well whose water reaches this tank.
4. Run a bucket test on every one of those wells. See [Run a saltwater bucket test](run-a-saltwater-bucket-test.md).
5. Select the **Producing Wells** tab to read the shares the tests produced.

## How the shares come out

Every attached well is compared on its most recent test rate. A well making 40 bbl/d beside a well making 10 bbl/d takes 80% of the water.

A well with no test on record takes 0%, and the tested wells split the whole 100% between them. Test every well on the facility, so each one is credited with the water it made.

Re-testing one well moves the split from that test's date forward. The others keep the rates their last tests gave them, so you can work through a station a well at a time.

Tanks on the same battery are pooled. One set of shares covers the whole site, so a test recorded once moves the station rather than one tank of it. That is why the **Split %** on **Producing Wells** is read-only.

## Override the split on a water meter

1. Open the [menu](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md) and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Meters** tab, then the meter's name.
3. Select **Allocation**.
4. Select **Add date range**.
5. Select the arrow beside the new range to open it.
6. Set **From**, and leave **To** blank while the override is still in force.
7. Select a well under **Well**, type its share under **Split %**, and use **Add well** for the rest.
8. Check that the **Total** line reads 100%.
9. Select **Save allocation**.

A date range you enter here governs the days it covers, ahead of anything the tests say.

## What happens next

Water is attributed down the chain from wherever it was measured, so the shares reach each well's own figures, the facilities map and the disposal reports.

Everyone in your workspace sees the change, and it applies to history as well as to today. Removing a date range and saving hands those days back to the tests.

## If something looks wrong

- **A well shows 0%.** It has no bucket test on record, or its latest test came out at zero. Run one.
- **A well is not listed at all.** It is not attached to the tank. Add it with **Add**, then **Add Well**.
- **The percentages did not move after a test.** The split is worked out fresh each time the page loads. Reload the page.
- **There is no Add or Allocation button.** You need the **Manage disposal** permission. Ask whoever runs your workspace.

pages.title: Understand why a well's numbers changed
pages.body:
# Understand why a well's numbers changed

Three things move a well's oil, gas and water figures: a well test, a date range somebody entered on an **Allocation** panel, and downtime logged on a well. Nothing you measured changed. The gauge, the meter and the run ticket stand, and what moved is how their totals are divided.

## Start here

- **One well moved and the others moved the opposite way.** A split changed. Open the battery or meter, select **Allocation**, and read the period covering those dates.
- **A well went to zero for part of a month.** Check its **Downtime** tab.
- **Every well on the battery moved together.** The measurement changed, not the split. Check the tank's **Readings** tab or the meter's readings for a corrected or added entry.
- **The change starts on one exact date and runs to today.** That date is a period's start. It is either a test's end date or a **From** somebody typed.
- **Only the water moved.** Somebody recorded a saltwater bucket test, or entered a date range on a water meter's **Allocation** panel.

Everything on an **Allocation** panel is shared. Anyone in your workspace can change a split, and everyone sees the result.

## Splits are dated, and the later start wins

Allocation is a timeline of periods, each with a start date and an end date. Every day belongs to exactly one period, and every barrel is divided by the period in force on the day it was recorded.

Periods come in two kinds:

- **Manual** periods are the percentages somebody typed on the **Allocation** panel.
- **Well test** periods are worked out from tests, and their percentages are read-only.

For oil and gas, where a manual period and a well test period cover the same day, the one that **starts later** governs it. A test supersedes the split it was run against, and a date range entered for days after a test supersedes that test. When both start on the same day, the well test wins.

This is why entering a split for last month can change figures for months you did not touch. The period runs until the next one starts, and the periods after it re-chain around it.

Water works differently. On a saltwater tank or meter, a date range somebody entered governs every day it covers, whatever the test dates say, and the tests fill the days no date range covers.

## A well test re-cuts the timeline from its date

An oil test on one well starts a well test period on the day the test closed. Every other well on the battery keeps the share its own last test gave it, so testing a well at a time works, and each test moves the split forward from its own date.

A saltwater bucket test does the same for water. A gas test moves nothing until the test is published on the meter.

If more than one well on a battery has never been tested, no test period can be worked out for those days, and the manual split covers them instead. With exactly one untested well, that well takes whatever the tested wells did not account for.

Deleting a test removes its period, and the days it covered fall back to whatever else covers them.

## A well that is down takes 0%

Log downtime on a well with **Add**, then **Downtime**, and give it a **Start**, an **End** and a **Type** of **Downtime** or **Shut-in**.

For every day inside that window, the well's share of oil, gas and water drops to 0, and the wells still running absorb it in the proportions they already had. A group split 20 / 30 / 50 with the first well down becomes 0 / 37.5 / 62.5. The second and third keep their relative standing rather than splitting the missing share evenly.

The facility's total does not change. Only who gets credited with it does. If every well in the group is down on a day the facility still recorded production, the split is left as it was so the barrels are not lost.

Removing the downtime entry puts the shares back.

## Related

- [Split oil production between wells](split-oil-production-between-wells.md)
- [Split gas production between wells](split-gas-production-between-wells.md)
- [Split water between wells](split-water-between-wells.md)

pages.title: Add a disposal well
pages.body:
# Add a disposal well

Open the menu, select **Disposal**, then **New Well**, then **New disposal well**. Type the name and select **Create**.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Wells** tab.
3. Select **New Well**.
4. Select **New disposal well**.
5. Type the name in **Well name**, such as `SWD #1`.
6. Select **Create**.

## What happens next

The well appears in the **SWD Wells** table with no readings against it yet. Select its name to open its page, where you record readings, attach a meter and fill in the rest of its details.

A disposal well counts against the wells your plan covers, the same as a producing well. If it takes you past your plan's limit, a window explains the price change first. Select **Upgrade and add well** to go ahead, or **Cancel** to add nothing.

Everyone in your workspace sees the new well. It also gets its own folder under **Files**.

## Fill in the rest of its details

1. Open the well and select the gear icon next to its name.
2. Fill in **Lease**, **Formation**, **County**, **Depth (ft)** and **API well #** as you have them.
3. Select **Save**.

If you know the well's name or API number in the state record, select **Sync with RRC** in that window first. It fills the boxes from the Railroad Commission's record and names the record it took, so you can check it. Nothing is saved until you select **Save**.

The **API well #** is what lets Wildcat show the well's permitted injection limits. See [Watch injection pressure against your permit](watch-injection-pressure-against-your-permit.md).

## If something looks wrong

- **There is no New Well button.** You need the **Add injection wells** permission. Ask whoever runs your workspace.
- **The well already exists as a producer.** Do not create it twice. See [Turn a producing well into a disposal well](turn-a-producing-well-into-a-disposal-well.md).
- **You created it by mistake.** On the **SWD Wells** tab, move the pointer over the row and select the trash icon at the end of it, then select **Delete well**. This permanently removes the well and all of its injection readings, and it cannot be undone. The icons only appear when the pointer is over the row, so use a computer for this rather than a phone.

## Next

- [Connect a water meter to a disposal well](connect-a-water-meter-to-a-disposal-well.md)
- [Record an injection reading](record-an-injection-reading.md)

pages.title: Connect a water meter to a disposal well
pages.body:
# Connect a water meter to a disposal well

Open the disposal well, select **Add**, then **Meter**. Choose the meter, set **Measuring from**, and select **Attach**.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Wells** tab.
3. Select the well's name.
4. Select **Add**, then **Meter**.
5. Select the meter under **Water meter**. Only water meters that are not already wired into this well are listed.
6. Set **Measuring from** to the day the meter started measuring this well. It starts at today.
7. Select **Attach**.

## What happens next

The page opens its **Meters** tab with the meter listed, **Measuring from** showing your date and **Status** showing **Measuring**. From that date on, the well's barrels are the meter's throughput, and the well's **Latest rate**, **Total injected** and chart all come from the meter.

**Reading** and **History** leave the well's **Add** menu, because the meter is now the measurement. Record readings on the meter from now on: select the meter's row, then **Add**, then **Reading**.

Readings you entered by hand on days the meter now covers stop counting toward the well's totals. They stay on file and count again if the meter is detached.

If the meter was already counting before **Measuring from**, the first interval after that date carries no barrels. It measured water that went elsewhere, so it is used as the starting point. The interval after it is the first with volume.

Everyone in your workspace sees the change. To undo it, see [Stop a meter from measuring a well](stop-a-meter-from-measuring-a-well.md).

## If the meter is not in the list

Create it first:

1. Open the menu and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Meters** tab.
3. Select **New Meter**.
4. Type the number painted on the meter in **Meter #**.
5. Select **Create**.

Then attach it with the steps above. A meter already wired into this well is not offered a second time.

## If something looks wrong

- **There is no Meter in the Add menu.** You need the **Manage disposal** permission. Ask whoever runs your workspace.
- **The meter sits on the tank battery, not on the well itself.** That still counts. A water meter feeding the tanks or the battery that feed this hole measures the well, up to four connections upstream, and the well shows as metered.
- **The well shows no barrels after attaching.** The meter has no readings yet, or only one. Add a second reading on the meter and the barrels between the two appear.

## Next

- [See which wells your water came from](see-which-wells-your-water-came-from.md)

pages.title: Record a water haul
pages.body:
# Record a water haul

Open the tank the water was hauled from, select **Add**, then **Add Haul**. Enter the barrels, or the open and close gauges, and select **Add Haul**.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Tanks** tab.
3. Select the tank's name.
4. Select **Add**, then **Add Haul**.
5. Check **Date** and **Time**. Both start at right now. Change them if the truck came earlier.
6. Type the gauge before the haul in **Open (in)** and the gauge after it in **Close (in)**, both in inches.
7. Check **Bbls hauled**. With both gauges filled in, it shows the barrels worked out from the tank's strapping and cannot be typed into. If you have no gauges, leave **Open (in)** and **Close (in)** empty and type the barrels here instead.
8. Select **Add Haul**.

## What happens next

The haul appears in the **Hauls** tab with **Open (bbl)**, **Close (bbl)** and **Hauled (bbl)**, and it draws the tank down: **% Full** and **Current level** on the tank's page both drop by that many barrels. The **Last Haul** column on the **SWD Tanks** tab shows the date.

Everyone in your workspace sees it.

## Before the truck comes

To put the tank in the pickup queue, select **Add**, then **Call-In**. It works the same as it does for a crude tank: see [Call in a tank for pickup](../daily-production-entry/call-in-a-tank-for-pickup.md). The tank then shows a **Called in** badge, and **Mark Picked Up** appears at the top of its page. Select that once the water is gone.

## If something looks wrong

- **Bbls hauled is gray and will not accept typing.** Both gauges are filled in, so the barrels come from them. Clear **Open (in)** or **Close (in)** to type the figure yourself.
- **The barrels came out far too small or too large.** The tank's strapping is wrong. Select the gear icon next to the tank's name and correct **Strapping (bbl/in)**, then enter the haul again.
- **Add Haul is not in the menu.** You need the **Manage disposal** permission. Ask whoever runs your workspace.
- **You are looking for Run Ticket.** That is the crude side. A water tank records hauls instead.
- **Call-In is not in the menu.** The tank is already called in. Use **Mark Picked Up** at the top of the page when the truck has been.

pages.title: Record an injection reading
pages.body:
# Record an injection reading

Open the disposal well, select **Add**, then **Reading**. If **Reading** is not in that menu, a meter measures this well and the reading goes on the meter instead: see [If a meter measures this well](#if-a-meter-measures-this-well) below.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Wells** tab.
3. Select the well's name.
4. Select **Add**, then **Reading**.
5. Check **Date** and **Time**. Both start at right now. Change them if you took the reading earlier.
6. Type the number on the well's meter head in **Meter Reading (bbl, cumulative)**. This is the running total the counter shows, not the barrels for the day.
7. Leave **Water Transferred (bbl)** empty and the barrels are worked out for you, as this reading minus the one before it. Type a figure only when you want to override that, or when there is no counter to read.
8. Type **Tubing Pressure (psi)** and **Casing Pressure (psi)** if you took them. Both can be left empty.
9. Select **Add Reading**.

## What happens next

The reading appears in the **Readings** tab showing **Meter (bbl)**, **Δ Water (bbl)** for the barrels since the last reading, **Norm. (bbl/d)**, **Tubing psi** and **Casing psi**. The **Latest rate**, **Total injected**, **Avg inj. pressure** and **Max inj. pressure** boxes at the top of the page update, and so does the well's row on the **SWD Wells** tab.

Everyone in your workspace sees the reading.

## If a meter measures this well

The barrels come from the meter, so the reading goes there.

1. Open the well and select the **Meters** tab.
2. Select the meter's row.
3. Select **Add**, then **Reading**.
4. Set **Date** and **Time** to when you took the reading. Both start empty.
5. Type the counter's running total in **Meter reading (bbl, cumulative)**. **Water transferred (bbl)** fills in by itself as the barrels since the last reading, and once the meter has a reading on file you can type into either box.
6. Type **Tubing psi (optional)** and **Casing psi (optional)** if you took them. These feed the disposal well's pressure figures.
7. Select **Add reading**.

If the number you type is lower than the last one, the box shows **Reset** instead of a volume. That is how a meter change or a rollover is recorded, and no barrels are counted for that interval.

## Change or remove a reading

1. Open the well and select the row in the **Readings** tab.
2. Change what is wrong, or select **Delete** at the bottom left.
3. Select **Save**.

A row that came from a meter opens the meter's page instead of this window. Correct it there.

## Enter a stack of old readings

On a well no meter measures, select **Add**, then **History**, then upload the injection log and select **Upload & Parse**. Wildcat reads the document and proposes the readings it found, and nothing is written until you approve each one. Uploading the same log again does not double the readings: any already on file are left out of the proposal.

## If something looks wrong

- **There is no Reading in the Add menu.** A water meter measures this well, so the barrels come from the meter. Record them on the meter, or [detach the meter](stop-a-meter-from-measuring-a-well.md) if it no longer measures this well.
- **There is no Add button at all.** You need the **Manage disposal** permission. Ask whoever runs your workspace.
- **Δ Water reads nothing on the first reading.** There is no earlier reading to subtract from. The second one fills it in.
- **A reading you already entered stopped counting.** A meter was attached covering that date. Readings entered by hand count on days no meter measured the well, so the meter's figure is used instead. The reading stays on file, and it counts again for any day after the meter is detached.

pages.title: See which wells your water came from
pages.body:
# See which wells your water came from

Open the disposal well and select the **Source Wells** tab. It lists each producing well that fed this hole, its **Share** of the total, and the **Disposed (bbl)** that came from it.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Wells** tab.
3. Select the well's name.
4. Select the **Source Wells** tab.

The shares are worked out reading by reading, from the plumbing as it stood on each reading's date, so a split you changed in March does not rewrite what February reported. Each reading is traced back from whatever measured it, so with two meters on one hole, each meter's barrels go to its own wells.

## If the tab is empty

Check two things, in this order.

**The well has taken no water yet.** The tab fills in once the well has barrels on it. See [Record an injection reading](record-an-injection-reading.md).

**Nothing has said whose water this is.** Set the split on the meter that measures the well:

1. Open the well and select the **Meters** tab.
2. Select the meter's row.
3. Select **Allocation**.
4. Select **Add date range**.
5. Set **From** to the day this split started. Leave **To** empty while it is still the current arrangement.
6. Select **Add well**, choose the well under **Well**, and type its share in **Split %**. **Even split** fills them in equally for you.
7. Repeat for each well feeding the meter. The total should read 100%.
8. Select **Save allocation**.

The **Source Wells** tab fills in the next time the well's page loads. To change the split later, add a second date range starting the day the arrangement changed, rather than editing the old one. That keeps last month's figures as they were reported.

Your date ranges are what Wildcat uses first. On dates no date range covers, the split follows the wells' published water tests instead.

## Wells with no meter

A well with no meter is traced from the well itself, so its water has to reach it through the tanks:

1. Open the tank under the **SWD Tanks** tab.
2. Select the gear icon next to the tank's name, set **SWD Well (disposal)** to this well, and select **Save**.
3. Select **Add**, then **Add Well**, and add the producing wells that fill the tank.

The tank's split across those wells then comes from their water well tests. See [Split water between wells](../well-tests-and-allocation/split-water-between-wells.md).

## If something looks wrong

- **The shares do not add up to 100%.** That is deliberate. Each share is that well's slice of everything this hole took, so a gap is barrels the plumbing could not account for.
- **A well you expected is missing.** It is not on the meter's split for the dates in question, or it was added with a **From** date later than those readings.
- **There is no Allocation button on the meter.** You need the **Manage disposal** permission. Ask whoever runs your workspace.

pages.title: Stop a meter from measuring a well
pages.body:
# Stop a meter from measuring a well

Open the disposal well, select the **Meters** tab, then select the trash icon at the end of the meter's row. The barrels it already measured stay in the well's history.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Wells** tab.
3. Select the well's name.
4. Select the **Meters** tab.
5. Select the trash icon at the end of the meter's row.

It takes effect straight away, as of today. There is no confirmation step.

## What happens next

The meter stays in the list with **Status** showing **Detached** and an **Until** date of today. Nothing is erased.

Everything the meter measured while it was wired in still counts. The well's **Total injected**, its readings and its charts are unchanged for those dates, and a note under the table says so. Detaching never rewrites past volume.

For days after today, the well is no longer metered. If this was its last measuring meter, **Reading** and **History** come back in the well's **Add** menu, and you record barrels by hand again. See [Record an injection reading](record-an-injection-reading.md).

The meter itself is untouched. Its own page, its readings and its history all stay where they are, and you can wire it into another disposal well.

Everyone in your workspace sees the change.

## Put it back

1. Select **Add**, then **Meter**.
2. Select the same meter under **Water meter**.
3. Set **Measuring from** to the day it starts measuring this well again.
4. Select **Attach**.

The meter keeps one row in the **Meters** tab, with **Status** back to **Measuring**.

## If something looks wrong

- **There is no trash icon on the row.** You need the **Manage disposal** permission, or the row is already detached. A detached row has no icon because there is nothing left to detach.
- **Reading did not come back in the Add menu.** Another meter still measures this well. Check the **Meters** tab for a second row showing **Measuring**, including one wired to the tank or battery that feeds the well.
- **You detached the wrong meter.** Attach it again with **Measuring from** set to today. Today is covered either way, so no barrels are lost.

pages.title: Turn a producing well into a disposal well
pages.body:
# Turn a producing well into a disposal well

Open the menu, select **Disposal**, then **New Well**, then **Designate existing well…**. Pick the well and select **Convert**.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Disposal**.
2. Select the **SWD Wells** tab.
3. Select **New Well**.
4. Select **Designate existing well…**.
5. Select the well under **Well**. Only producing wells are listed.
6. Select **Convert**.

## What happens next

The well moves from **Production** to **Disposal**. It leaves the wells list under **Production** and appears in the **SWD Wells** table here, where selecting its name opens the disposal version of its page: injection readings, meters, source wells and its permit limits.

Nothing is deleted. The oil and gas readings, well tests, equipment, comments, notes and files it already had stay exactly as they were, and they come back if you convert it back. No new well is added to your plan, so nothing changes on your bill.

Everyone in your workspace sees the change.

## Change it back

1. Open the well from the **SWD Wells** tab.
2. Select the gear icon next to the well's name.
3. Set **Type** to **Production**.
4. Select **Save**.

The well returns to **Production**.

## If something looks wrong

- **Designate existing well… is gray and will not open.** Your workspace has no producing wells to convert. Add one under **Production** first, or use [Add a disposal well](add-a-disposal-well.md) instead.
- **There is no New Well button.** You need the **Add injection wells** permission. Ask whoever runs your workspace.
- **The well still shows old oil or gas readings.** That is on purpose. Its history is kept whole when it changes duty.

pages.title: Watch injection pressure against your permit
pages.body:
# Watch injection pressure against your permit

Open the disposal well. **Max inj. pressure** at the top of the page turns red when the well's highest recorded pressure is over the permit's limit, and **Latest rate** turns red when the well is taking more barrels a day than the permit allows.

To get there: open the menu, select **Disposal**, select the **SWD Wells** tab, then select the well's name.

## What each number means

On the **SWD Wells** tab, every well shows a row:

- **Injection (psi)**: the tubing pressure from the most recent reading that recorded one.
- **Casing (psi)**: the casing pressure from the most recent reading that recorded one.
- **Max (psi)**: the maximum surface injection pressure on the well's permit. This is the state's number, not yours.

On the well's own page:

- **Avg inj. pressure** is the average of the readings that recorded a tubing pressure. Use it to spot a formation slowly plugging off.
- **Max inj. pressure** is the highest pressure on record. This is the one held against the permit, because the permit limits any single moment rather than an average.
- **Latest rate** is the barrels a day the well is taking now.

## See it against the limit on the chart

1. Open the well.
2. Select the chart's title, **Disposal rate**, to open the list of views.
3. Select **Injection pressure**.

The permitted pressure is drawn as a red dashed line marked **permitted**. The line under the chart title reads `psi · 1,500 permitted`, with your well's own figure in place of 1,500.

Select the title again and choose **Disposal rate** to see the barrels a day against the permitted rate the same way.

## Turn the permit limits on

The limits come from the Railroad Commission's record of the well, matched by its API number.

1. Open the well and select the gear icon next to its name.
2. Type the well's API number in **API well #**, or select **Sync with RRC** to look it up and fill the boxes for you.
3. Select **Save**.

The limits appear the next time the page loads. Wildcat only counts permits that are live, and where a hole has two live permits the barrels are added together while the pressure limit stays the higher of the two.

## Record the pressures

Pressure appears once someone writes it down. On an unmetered well, fill in **Tubing Pressure (psi)** and **Casing Pressure (psi)** when you [record a reading](record-an-injection-reading.md). On a metered well, fill in **Tubing psi (optional)** and **Casing psi (optional)** on the meter's reading.

## If something looks wrong

- **Max (psi) is blank.** The well has no **API well #** on file, or the Railroad Commission has no live injection permit for it.
- **The permit line is missing from the chart and the subtitle says (off scale).** The limit is more than four times the highest figure on screen. Drawing it would flatten the well's own line into the axis. The tiles at the top still turn red if the well goes over.
- **The pressure chart says to log injection pressure on at least two readings.** Two readings with a tubing pressure are needed to draw a line. Add them with your next readings.
- **Every psi column shows a dash.** Nobody has recorded a pressure with a reading. Add them with the next reading.

pages.title: Add a purchaser statement
pages.body:
# Add a purchaser statement

Open the menu, select **Revenue**, stay on the **Statements** tab, and select **Add Statement**. Pick the settlement document, select **Read statement**, check what WildcatIQ read off the page, then select **Save statement**.

Nothing is saved until you select **Save statement**, and saving a statement does not put any money in your ledger. Posting is a separate step you take afterwards. See [Post a statement to revenue](post-a-statement-to-revenue.md).

## Add the statement

1. Open the menu and select **Revenue**. The **Statements** tab is already showing.
2. Select **Add Statement** at the top right.
3. In the **Upload Statement** window, select **Drop a statement or click to upload** and choose the file. One file at a time. It can be a PDF, a photo, a CSV, or an XLSX.
4. If you chose a photo, a **Check the crop** window opens. Drag the corners so the outline covers the page, then select **Upload**. Use **Whole image** if you would rather send the whole photo, and **Rotate** if it came in sideways.
5. Select **Read statement**. This is the step that uses AI credits, so nothing is spent if you picked the wrong file and select **Cancel** instead.
6. Wait while the button reads **Reading…**. A long settlement document can take a couple of minutes.

If you cannot find **Revenue** in the menu, see [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).

## Check it before you save

The window retitles to **Review Statements** and splits in two: the document on the left, what WildcatIQ read on the right.

1. Read the **Purchaser**, **Statement #**, **Check #**, **Commodity**, **Period start**, and **Period end** against the page. Correct anything wrong by typing over it.
2. Check each settlement line: its **Lease**, its **Tank** or **Meter**, and the money columns.
3. If a line is tinted amber, read the note under it. The arithmetic on that line does not close. See [Check and correct a statement](check-and-correct-a-statement.md).
4. If a line points at the wrong lease or tank, fix it now. See [Match a statement line to the right lease, tank, or meter](match-a-statement-line-to-the-right-tank-or-lease.md).
5. Select **Save statement**.

To throw the whole read away and start from a different file, select **Start over**.

## When one upload holds several statements

A row of tabs appears at the top of the window, one per statement, and a blue dot marks the ones you have not opened yet. The first tab counts as opened because it is already on screen. An amber triangle on a tab means that statement has a warning or looks like a duplicate.

The save button reads **Save 3 statements** instead of **Save statement**, and the number matches what was read.

Open each tab before saving. If you save with tabs still unopened, WildcatIQ asks first: **They'll be saved as Extracted so you can review them later. The ones you did open are saved as Reviewed.** Select **Save anyway** to go ahead. The status is how you tell later which ones nobody checked.

## What happens next

The window closes and the new row appears on the **Statements** tab with a status of **Reviewed**, or **Extracted** if you never opened it.

No revenue has been recorded yet. The **Transactions** tab is unchanged until you post the statement.

If the statement named a lease, tank, meter, or purchaser that is not on file yet, WildcatIQ offers to add them as approval cards over the page. Select **Approve** to add them or **Dismiss** to skip. Dismissing costs you nothing on the statement itself.

Everyone in your workspace who can see revenue sees the statement. Nobody is emailed. To undo the whole thing, delete the row. See [Handle a duplicate statement](handle-a-duplicate-statement.md) for what deleting does and does not remove.

## Messages you may see

- **You're out of AI credits** appears as soon as you pick the file, and **Read statement** stays greyed out. Select **Buy AI credits**, or ask your workspace owner to. Your file was not uploaded.
- **Document scanning is turned off for your organization. Enable it in AI settings.** An admin can switch **Use AI to scan uploaded documents** back on in **Settings**. Your file was not uploaded.
- **No settlement statements were found in this document.** The file read fine but held no settlement. Check you picked the right file.
- **That file is too large to process. Try a smaller or compressed PDF.** Send a smaller file.
- **Reading the document timed out. Try a smaller file.** Split a long packet and send it in parts.

You need the **Manage statements** permission to add a statement. With **View revenue** alone you get the list and can open a statement to read it.

pages.title: Add a vendor invoice
pages.body:
# Add a vendor invoice

Every invoice starts from the bill itself. Open the menu, select **Invoices** under **Finance**, select **Invoice**, upload the document, and file what comes back. There is no form for typing an invoice in by hand.

## Add one

1. Open the menu and select **Invoices** under **Finance**.
2. Select **Invoice** at the top right. It is the button with a plus sign on it.
3. In the **Upload Invoice** window, select **Drop an invoice or click to upload** and pick the file. PDF, image, CSV, and XLSX all work.
4. If you picked a photo, a **Check the crop** window opens first. Drag the corners around the page and select **Upload**.
5. Select **Read invoice**. The button reads **Reading…** while it works.
6. Check the panels on the right against the scan on the left.
7. Select **File 1 invoice**. If the document held several, the button says how many.

If you cannot find **Invoices** in the menu, see [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).

The window closes and the invoice appears in the list, sorted by invoice date with the newest first.

Everyone in your company with **View invoices** sees it straight away. Nobody is emailed. It also appears on the **Invoices** tab of any well, lease, tank, meter, or battery it turns out to be billed against.

## After you file it

WildcatIQ may offer you a card or two: the vendor if that company is not in **People** yet, the lease or well the bill names if it is not on file, and any equipment the charge lines show going into a well. Select **Approve** or **Dismiss** on each card. Nothing on a card changes the invoice you just filed.

## Messages you may see

- **That invoice is already on file, so nothing was added.** The same document was filed before, and nothing is duplicated.
- **Could not file …** followed by a reason. That document was not saved. If the file held several invoices, the message says how many of the others went in. Select **Start over** and try again.

## Other ways an invoice arrives

A document you upload somewhere else in WildcatIQ, on a well page or in Data Entry, is offered to you as an approval card if it reads as an invoice. Approving that card files it here.

You need **Manage invoices** to add one. With **View invoices** alone you get the list.

Next: [Read an invoice from a photo or PDF](read-an-invoice-from-a-photo-or-pdf.md), [See what an invoice was billed against](see-what-an-invoice-was-billed-against.md).

pages.title: Change what an invoice is billed against
pages.body:
# Change what an invoice is billed against

Open the invoice, then use the **Wells**, **Tanks**, **Meters**, **Batteries**, and **Leases** buttons in the **Billed against** panel to tick what it belongs to. There is no Save button. The change is saved when you close the window.

## Change it

1. Open the menu and select **Invoices** under **Finance**.
2. Select the invoice you want.
3. In the **Billed against** panel, select the button for the kind of facility you want, for example **Wells**.
4. Type in the search box to narrow the list, then select a name. A tick appears beside it and a chip appears above.
5. Select the same name again to untick it, or select the small x on its chip to remove it.
6. Repeat for any other kind.
7. Close the window with the x at its top right.

You can also open the invoice from a facility's **Invoices** tab and change it there.

## What happens next

The invoice appears on the **Invoices** tab of every facility you ticked and comes off the tabs of any you removed. If you made the change from a facility tab, the invoice can vanish off the tab in front of you. That is the change working.

Everyone in your company with **View invoices** sees the new filing. Nobody is emailed.

To undo it, open the invoice again and put the chips back the way they were.

## When a facility stays on the tab

A well or lease named on the invoice's own charge lines stays on that page's **Invoices** tab even after you remove its chip. The chips are one of two ways an invoice reaches a facility page, and the charge lines are the other. Tanks, meters, and batteries reach a page by chip alone.

You need **Manage invoices** to change the filing. With **View invoices** alone the panel shows the chips and nothing to change them with.

See also: [See what an invoice was billed against](see-what-an-invoice-was-billed-against.md).

pages.title: Check and correct a statement
pages.body:
# Check and correct a statement

Open the menu, select **Revenue**, select the statement's row on the **Statements** tab, correct any field, then select **Save changes**. The same editor you used when the statement went in is the one you get back, so a wrong purchaser, period, price, or lease can be fixed at any time.

Correcting a statement does not change revenue you have already posted from it. If the money was wrong too, undo the posting, fix the numbers, and post again. See [Undo a posting](undo-a-posting.md).

## Correct it

1. Open the menu and select **Revenue**.
2. Select the row you want on the **Statements** tab. The whole row opens the statement.
3. The document sits on the left and its fields on the right. Compare the two.
4. Type over anything wrong: **Purchaser**, **Statement #**, **Check #**, and any figure on a settlement line.
5. Use the lists for **Commodity**, **Period start**, and **Period end**.
6. Select **Save changes** at the bottom right.

**Save changes** stays greyed out until you actually change something.

To take a copy of the source document, select **Download** at the top of the window.

## Read the amber warnings

WildcatIQ checks the arithmetic itself and flags what does not close. The warnings are advice. They never block a save and they never change a number for you.

- A warning box at the top of the fields means the period is impossible, or the lines do not add up to the total the document itself printed.
- An amber tint on a line, with the reason written underneath it, means that line's own numbers disagree. For example, **Net $4,200.00 doesn't match gross − deducts − taxes ($4,180.00).**, or **Volume × price is $4,150.00 but gross is $4,200.00.**
- **This line carries value but no volume.** usually means a column was misread.
- **Part of this line was unreadable on the page — check it against the document.** means the scan was too poor to be sure.

The warnings recalculate as you type, so a correct fix clears the tint straight away without saving first.

A line pointing at no lease is not flagged amber. That is normal the first time a lease appears. See [Match a statement line to the right lease, tank, or meter](match-a-statement-line-to-the-right-tank-or-lease.md).

## Add or remove a line

1. Select **Add line** at the bottom of the fields to add an empty settlement line.
2. Select **Remove line 2** (the number matches the line) to take one out. The button only appears when there is more than one line.
3. Select **Save changes**.

## What happens next

The window closes and the list re-reads, so the **Oil (bbl)**, **Gas (MCF)**, and **Value** columns update to your corrected figures. Everyone in your workspace who can see revenue sees the corrected statement. Nobody is emailed.

Saving keeps the statement's current status. It does not post anything, and it does not undo anything already posted.

One field on the gas lines is deliberately not typeable. **$/MCF** is worked out from that line's **Net** and **MCF**, because no gas settlement prints a price per MCF. Correct the volume or the money and the rate follows. On an oil statement **$/BBL** is what the purchaser printed, so you can type over it.

You need the **Manage statements** permission to edit. With **View revenue** alone you can open a statement and read it.

pages.title: Check oil and gas prices
pages.body:
# Check oil and gas prices

Open the menu and select **Prices** under **Finance**. The table at the bottom of the page is your own price, month by month, newest first. The chart above it puts that price next to the market benchmark.

Nothing on this page can be edited, and nothing you do here is visible to anyone else.

## Find the price you were paid

1. Open the menu and select **Prices**.
2. At the top, select **Oil** or **Gas**. The page opens on **Oil**.
3. Read the table under the chart. The left column is **Month**, for example **January 2026**. The right column is headed **Posted Price ($/bbl)** for oil and **Posted Price ($/MMBtu)** for gas.

One row per month, newest first, with no page buttons.

Each figure is the average price your revenue worked out to for that month, weighted by volume. It is calculated from the rows on the **Transactions** tab of **Revenue**, so a month with no revenue in the ledger has no row. If the table reads **No posted prices yet for oil.**, posting a statement is what fills it. See [Post a statement to revenue](post-a-statement-to-revenue.md).

## Compare it to the market

The chart above the table is headed **WTI vs posted price** for oil and **Henry Hub vs posted price** for gas, with **WTI benchmark against the price you received.** underneath. The key below the plot names three lines:

- **WTI ($/bbl)**, or **Henry Hub ($/MMBtu)** for gas: the daily market close.
- **Posted ($/bbl)**, or **Posted ($/MMBtu)**: the price you actually received.
- **Projected**: a dashed estimate.

Select a period above the chart to change how far back the benchmark goes: **1M**, **3M**, **12M**, **5Y**, or **10Y**. It opens on **3M**.

The period buttons move the benchmark line only. Your **Posted** and **Projected** lines always cover your whole history, so a short period still shows them stretched across the plot.

## Read the dashed Projected line

**Projected** fills the gap between your last month of revenue and today, because accounting arrives about a month late while the market is live. It starts at the end of your last posted month, holds flat within each month, and is an estimate rather than money received.

It is left off the chart entirely when there is nothing to base it on.

## If you cannot find Prices in the menu

You need **View pricing** to open this page. Ask an admin to grant it in **Settings**.

See also: [Understand the prices in the top bar](understand-the-prices-in-the-top-bar.md).

pages.title: Delete an invoice
pages.body:
# Delete an invoice

Open the menu, select **Invoices** under **Finance**, put your mouse over the invoice's row, select the trash icon at the right end, then select **Delete invoice**. It comes off the list at once.

The trash icon appears when your mouse is over the row, and also when you reach it with the Tab key.

## Delete one

1. Open the menu and select **Invoices** under **Finance**.
2. Move your mouse over the row. A trash icon appears at the right end.
3. Select the trash icon.
4. The window asks **Delete invoice 12345?**, or names the vendor when the document had no number. Underneath it reads **It comes off the invoice list and every facility tab it was billed against.**
5. Select **Delete invoice**.

The row disappears straight away, and the invoice comes off the **Invoices** tab of every well, lease, tank, meter, and battery it was filed against. Everyone in your company sees it go. Nobody is emailed.

## It cannot be undone from the screen

There is no undo and no trash to restore it from. If you deleted the wrong one, upload the document again and file it. See [Add a vendor invoice](add-a-vendor-invoice.md). WildcatIQ will not call it a duplicate, because the deleted one no longer counts.

## Where you can delete from

Only the **Invoices** page. The **Invoices** tab on a well, lease, tank, meter, or battery page has no trash icon. To take an invoice off one of those tabs without deleting it, see [Change what an invoice is billed against](change-what-an-invoice-is-billed-against.md).

You need **Manage invoices** to delete an invoice. Ask whoever runs your workspace if you do not have it.

pages.title: Handle a duplicate statement
pages.body:
# Handle a duplicate statement

A duplicate warning is advice, never a block. WildcatIQ tells you when a statement or a line looks like one you already have, and you decide whether to save it, post it, or delete the extra copy.

There are two separate warnings: one when you upload a statement that matches one on file, and one when a line you are about to post matches money already in the ledger.

## When the upload says it is already on file

An amber banner appears above the fields: **A statement matching Plains Marketing · 2026-07-01 → 2026-07-31 · #44182 is already on file. Saving this creates a second one.**

It matches on the purchaser, the statement number, and the period, all three. It is right to save anyway when the purchaser has reissued a corrected statement under the same number.

- To keep only what you already have, select **Cancel** or **Start over**. Nothing is saved.
- To file this one as well, select **Save statement**. You now have two rows, and you can delete either one afterwards.

## When a line looks like money you already have

In **Post to revenue**, the **Status** column shows **Likely duplicate** or **Possible duplicate** on any line that matches an existing revenue transaction on the same lease, the same product, inside the same period, for about the same amount. A note under the table counts them: **2 selected lines look like an existing entry. Uncheck any you do not want to post.**

Flagged lines stay ticked. Nothing is excluded for you.

1. Rest the pointer on the badge to read what it matched, for example **Matches manual entry · 2026-07-31 · $12,400**. On a phone, go by the lease, the amount, and the date in the row.
2. Open the **Transactions** tab and find the row it means.
3. If it is the same money, untick the line before you post, or delete the older row from the ledger and post this one.
4. If it is genuinely different money, leave it ticked and select **Post 3 selected**.

**Likely duplicate** means the purchaser matched too. **Possible duplicate** means the amount is close but the purchaser differs, or the amount is only roughly the same.

## Delete the extra statement

1. Open the menu and select **Revenue**.
2. Find the row you want gone on the **Statements** tab. Check the **Period**, **Purchaser**, and **Value** columns so you delete the right one.
3. Select the trash icon in the **Actions** column at the right of that row.
4. The dialog reads **Delete the Plains Marketing statement?** Read it, then select **Delete**.

## What deleting removes, and what it leaves

Deleting removes the statement, all of its line items, and the source document. This cannot be undone.

Revenue you already posted from that statement stays in the ledger. It is kept and simply unlinked from the statement. If you want that money gone as well, unpost it first, then delete. See [Undo a posting](undo-a-posting.md).

Everyone in your workspace who can see revenue sees the row disappear. Nobody is emailed.

You need the **Manage statements** permission to delete. It is what puts the **Actions** column on the list.

pages.title: Match a statement line to the right lease, tank, or meter
pages.body:
# Match a statement line to the right lease, tank, or meter

Open the statement, find the line, and pick the right entry from its **Lease** list and its **Tank** or **Meter** list. Then select **Save changes**, or **Save statement** if you are still on the upload.

A line has to be matched before it can post. WildcatIQ posts revenue against a lease, so a line with nothing picked never reaches the posting table.

## Match a line

1. Open the menu and select **Revenue**.
2. Select the statement's row on the **Statements** tab.
3. Find the line on the right-hand side. Each one starts with **Lease** and then **Tank** or **Meter**.
4. Open the **Lease** list and choose the lease. Leases are listed as the name, then the lease number, for example **Roach · 12345**.
5. Open the **Tank** list (oil) or the **Meter** list (gas) and choose the measurement point.
6. Select **Save changes**. The window closes.

Whether the second box says **Tank** or **Meter** is decided by the **Commodity** field at the top of the statement, not by the line. **Gas** shows meters. **Oil** and **Mixed** both show tanks. If every line is showing the wrong one, change **Commodity**.

## What the greyed-out text in the box means

When a box shows dimmed text instead of a name, that line is unmatched and the dimmed text is what the purchaser printed on the page, for example **ROACH LSE 3**.

This is normal the first time a lease, tank, or meter appears on a statement. It is not an error, and it is not flagged amber.

Open the list and you get one extra choice at the top:

- **ROACH LSE 3 (new)** leaves the line unmatched and keeps the printed reference.
- **— Unmatched —** appears instead when the purchaser printed nothing there.

During the upload, leaving a line on **(new)** is what tells WildcatIQ to offer that lease or meter as an approval card once you select **Save statement**. Select **Approve** on the card to add it, then come back and match the line to it. Editing a statement that is already saved does not offer those cards, so add the lease or tank yourself first and then match the line.

A line left unmatched loses nothing. The printed reference stays on it.

## Getting a line to post

A line reaches the **Post to revenue** table when its **Net** is not zero and it has either:

- a lease picked in **Lease**, or
- a tank or meter picked in **Tank** or **Meter**.

Picking a tank or meter that belongs to a lease is what puts the lease on the posted transaction, so pick both where you can.

If the panel says **No postable lines. A line needs a value and a matched lease (or tank/meter) before it can post to revenue**, match the lines and save. Open the statement again and the posting table is filled in.

## What happens next

The corrected match saves against the statement and shows in the **Lease** column of the posting table.

Re-matching a line that is already posted does not move the revenue transaction it created. Unpost it, fix the match, then post again. See [Undo a posting](undo-a-posting.md).

The **Tank** or **Meter** you pick is also what puts the sale on the **Revenue** tab of the wells that measurement point feeds, whether or not you have posted the line. Everyone in your workspace who can see revenue sees it there.

You need the **Manage statements** permission to change a match.

pages.title: Post a statement to revenue
pages.body:
# Post a statement to revenue

Open the statement from **Revenue**, scroll to **Post to revenue**, leave the lines you want checked, then select **Post 4 selected** (the number matches your ticks). Each checked line becomes one revenue transaction on the **Transactions** tab.

Posting can be undone. Nothing about the statement or the document changes, and you can post the rest of the lines later. See [Undo a posting](undo-a-posting.md).

## Post the lines

1. Open the menu and select **Revenue**.
2. Select the statement's row on the **Statements** tab.
3. Scroll the right-hand side down to **Post to revenue**.
4. Read the table. Every line that has not been posted is already ticked. Untick any line you do not want to post.
5. Select **Post 4 selected** at the bottom right.

The message under the table tells you what happened, for example **Posted 4 transactions, 1 excluded.**

On a phone the table is wider than the screen, so drag it sideways to reach the **Amount** and **Status** columns.

## What each line becomes

One row on the **Transactions** tab, carrying:

- **Date**: the statement's **Period end**, not the day you posted.
- **Type**: revenue.
- **Counterparty**: the purchaser.
- **Category**: your workspace's oil or gas revenue category.
- **Lease**: the lease on the line, or the lease its tank or meter belongs to.
- **Amount**: the line's net value.

The price, the volume, and the taxes plus fees ride along on the row as well, and the statement number is stored against it.

## What the table is telling you

- **New** in the **Status** column means WildcatIQ found nothing like this line in the ledger.
- **Likely duplicate** or **Possible duplicate** means it did. The line stays ticked and posting is not blocked. See [Handle a duplicate statement](handle-a-duplicate-statement.md).
- Lines already posted are listed underneath in grey with a **Posted** badge.

If the panel reads **No postable lines. A line needs a value and a matched lease (or tank/meter) before it can post to revenue**, no line on this statement has both. See [Match a statement line to the right lease, tank, or meter](match-a-statement-line-to-the-right-tank-or-lease.md).

## What happens next

The statement's status changes to **Posted** once every postable line is linked, and stays **Reviewed** while some are still outstanding.

The new rows appear on the **Transactions** tab and count toward lease revenue for everyone in your workspace who can see revenue. Nobody is emailed.

Posting the same statement twice does not double anything. A line that is already posted is skipped, so you can safely come back and post the lines you left out the first time.

You need the **Manage statements** permission to post. **Post to revenue** is on the statement for anyone who has it.

pages.title: Read an invoice from a photo or PDF
pages.body:
# Read an invoice from a photo or PDF

Upload the document on the **Invoices** page and select **Read invoice**. WildcatIQ pulls out the vendor, the dates, the charge lines and the totals, and shows them beside the scan so you can check them before anything is saved.

## Read one

1. Open the menu and select **Invoices** under **Finance**.
2. Select **Invoice** at the top right.
3. Select **Drop an invoice or click to upload** and pick the file, or drag the file onto the box.
4. For a photo, the **Check the crop** window opens. WildcatIQ reads only what is inside the outline, so drag the corners onto the page. Select **Rotate** if it is sideways, or **Whole image** to keep the whole photo. Then select **Upload**.
5. Select **Read invoice**.
6. Wait. A single bill takes seconds. A thick packet can take a couple of minutes.

The window changes to **Review Invoices** and tells you how many invoices were read from the file. Nothing is saved yet.

## Check what came back

Each invoice found gets its own panel on the right: the vendor and number in the heading, then **Invoice date**, **Due**, **Terms**, **Charged to**, **Subtotal**, the tax line under the vendor's own wording, **Total**, and every charge line.

A field ticket stapled behind the invoice that bills it is folded into that invoice, so a packet can show fewer panels than it has pieces of paper. This is deliberate. Reading the ticket as a second bill would ask you to pay the same work twice.

Watch for the amber line: **The charge lines read here add to … but the invoice prints a subtotal of … Check the lines against the scan before filing.** That means a line was missed or counted twice. Compare against the scan on the left before you file.

## If a figure is wrong

You cannot correct a field on this screen. Select **Start over**, then upload a clearer scan or a different copy of the document.

## Then file it

Select **File 1 invoice** at the bottom right. See [Add a vendor invoice](add-a-vendor-invoice.md) for what happens next.

## Messages you may see

- **That document was read, but nothing in it looked like an invoice. It is stored in Files, and Data Entry will give it a broader read.** The file is kept. Nothing was added to the invoice list.
- **This file couldn't be read — try a clearer scan or another format.** Photograph the page again in better light, flat and square, or ask the vendor for a PDF. The file is still stored in Files.
- **Document scanning is turned off for your organization. Enable it in AI settings.** An admin turns it back on in **Settings**. Your file was not uploaded.
