- **You're out of AI credits.** This appears as soon as you pick the file, and **Read invoice** stays greyed out. Select **Buy AI credits**, or ask your workspace owner to. Your file was not uploaded.
- **Something went wrong while scanning. Please try again.** The file is stored. Try again.

You need **Manage invoices** to read an invoice.

pages.title: See what an invoice was billed against
pages.body:
# See what an invoice was billed against

Open the invoice from the **Invoices** page and read the **Billed against** panel. The chips in that panel are the wells, tanks, meters, batteries, and leases the bill is filed against.

## Open an invoice

1. Open the menu and select **Invoices** under **Finance**.
2. Select the row you want. You can also move to it with the Tab key and press Enter.

The document opens with the scan on the left and what WildcatIQ read off it on the right. The heading is the file name, with the vendor underneath.

## Read the panel

**Billed against** sits between the **Invoice** panel and **Totals**. Each chip carries the kind in small letters (**Well**, **Tank**, **Meter**, **Battery**, **Lease**) and the name.

If it is not filed against anything, the panel reads **Not billed against any facility.**

The same invoice also shows on the **Invoices** tab of each facility in that panel.

## Charged To is a different thing

The **Charged To** column in the table, and the **Charged to** row in the **Invoice** panel, are what the vendor printed on the page, word for word. **Billed against** is what WildcatIQ has it filed under. The two sit on screen together on purpose, and they do not have to match.

To change the filing, see [Change what an invoice is billed against](change-what-an-invoice-is-billed-against.md).

## A warning triangle next to the amount

An amber triangle beside the amount in the table means the vendor's tax label does not match the work described. Open the invoice and read under **Totals**, where the reason is spelled out: the tax line is labelled as sales tax, but the work described is an oil-well service under Texas Tax Code ch. 191, which is taxed at 2.42% and is mutually exclusive with sales tax on that labor.

Nothing was recalculated. The label and the amount are recorded exactly as printed, and the total you see is the total the vendor asked for. Check it against the scan, and take it up with the vendor if it is wrong. Nothing on this screen clears the triangle.

## Other things in the window

- **Download** at the top right saves the original document.
- **No source document attached to this invoice.** means the record was filed without a file.
- A field left blank on the document is left out of the panel rather than shown empty.
- **Charges** lists every line with its quantity, rate, and dates. **No charge** on a line means the vendor declined to bill it, which is different from $0.00.

Looking at an invoice changes nothing and notifies nobody. You need **View invoices**.

pages.title: Understand the prices in the top bar
pages.body:
# Understand the prices in the top bar

The two prices at the top right of the screen are live market prices, **WTI** for crude oil and **Nat Gas** for natural gas. They are the market, not what you were paid.

## What each part means

- The name of the contract, **WTI** or **Nat Gas**.
- The latest price in dollars.
- A green triangle pointing up, or a red one pointing down, and the percentage the price has moved over the last 24 hours.

On a computer, rest your mouse on a price and a label spells it out, for example **WTI: $80.69/bbl, up 1.23% over 24h (Yahoo, delayed)**.

The prices come from Yahoo Finance and run roughly ten minutes behind the market. They refresh on their own about once a minute. There is nothing to select and nothing to set up.

## Why you may not see them

- On a phone, or in a narrow window, the prices are hidden to keep the top bar clear. Widen the window on a computer to bring them back.
- You need **View pricing** for them to appear. Ask an admin to grant it in **Settings**.

## These are not your prices

What you received for your own oil and gas is a different number, and it lives on the **Prices** page under **Finance**. See [Check oil and gas prices](check-oil-and-gas-prices.md).

pages.title: Undo a posting
pages.body:
# Undo a posting

Open the statement from **Revenue**, scroll to **Post to revenue**, tick the grey lines marked **Posted**, then select **Unpost 3 selected** (the number matches your ticks). The revenue transactions those lines created are removed from the **Transactions** tab.

Posting is meant to be reversible. Unposting takes nothing away from the statement itself, and you can post the same lines again afterwards.

## Unpost

1. Open the menu and select **Revenue**.
2. Select the statement's row on the **Statements** tab.
3. Scroll the right-hand side down to **Post to revenue**.
4. The posted lines are the grey ones at the bottom of the table with a **Posted** badge. They start unticked.
5. Tick the ones you want to reverse.
6. Select **Unpost 3 selected** at the bottom left.

The message under the table confirms it, for example **Unposted 3 transactions.**

## What happens next

The transactions are deleted from the **Transactions** tab, and from the lease totals they were counting toward. Everyone in your workspace who can see revenue sees them go. Nobody is emailed.

The statement's status returns to **Reviewed**, and the lines you unposted move back up into the top half of the table, ticked and ready to post again.

The statement, its lines, and its document are untouched. So are the lines you left showing **Posted**.

## Fix the numbers, then post again

If you unposted because the money was wrong:

1. Correct the figures in the fields above. See [Check and correct a statement](check-and-correct-a-statement.md).
2. Select **Save changes**. The window closes.
3. Open the statement again, scroll to **Post to revenue**, and select **Post 1 selected**.

## The other way a posting comes undone

Deleting a revenue row directly on the **Transactions** tab also removes that money, and the statement line it came from goes back to being unposted. Unposting from the statement is the cleaner route, because it also puts the statement's status back. See [Work with the Transactions ledger](work-with-the-transactions-ledger.md).

Deleting the whole statement does **not** remove revenue you posted from it. That money stays in the ledger, no longer tied to a statement. Unpost first if you want it gone. See [Handle a duplicate statement](handle-a-duplicate-statement.md).

You need the **Manage statements** permission to unpost.

pages.title: Work with the Transactions ledger
pages.body:
# Work with the Transactions ledger

Open the menu, select **Revenue**, then select **Transactions** at the top of the page. Every revenue transaction in your workspace is listed here, oldest first, and most cells are edited in place: select the cell, change it, and it saves when you move away or press Enter.

There is no separate save button and no undo. An edit is written as soon as you leave the cell, and deleting rows is permanent.

## Correct a row

1. Open the menu and select **Revenue**, then select **Transactions**.
2. Select the cell you want to change.
3. Type the new value, or pick from the list for **Type**, **Category**, and **Lease**.
4. Press Enter, or select somewhere else on the page, to save it.

These cells can be changed: **Date**, **Type**, **Counterparty**, **Category**, **Lease**, and **Amount**.

These cells are shown for reading only: **Oil Price**, **Gas Price**, and **Added**. **Oil Price** and **Gas Price** come from the statement the row was posted from, and a dash means the row carries no price for that product. To change a price, correct it on the statement, unpost, and post again. See [Check and correct a statement](check-and-correct-a-statement.md).

**Added** is the day the row entered the ledger, which is not the same as **Date**. A posted statement line is dated the statement's period end.

## Delete rows

1. Tick the box at the left of each row you want gone. The box in the header ticks every row, and clears them all again if they are already ticked.
2. Select **Delete selected** in the bar that appears above the table.
3. The bar asks **Delete 3? This can't be undone.** Select **Confirm delete**, or **Cancel** to back out.

If the row came from a statement, deleting it also leaves that statement line unposted, so you can post it again later from the statement. The cleaner way to reverse a posting is [Undo a posting](undo-a-posting.md), because that also puts the statement's status back.

## Two cautions before you edit

Changing **Type** from **Revenue** to **Expense** clears that row's lease, volume, price, production tax, and category, and the row leaves this tab the next time the page loads. Only do it if the row was never revenue.

Editing a row that came from a statement does not change the statement. The ledger and the statement then disagree, and the statement is the record of what the purchaser sent you. Correct the statement instead and re-post.

## Who sees it

Everyone in your workspace who can see revenue sees this ledger and every change you make to it. Nobody is emailed. Rows feed lease and well revenue totals elsewhere in WildcatIQ, so a wrong amount here shows up in your reports too.

You need the **Manage statements** permission to change or delete a row.

New revenue rows are created by posting a purchaser statement. See [Add a purchaser statement](add-a-purchaser-statement.md) and [Post a statement to revenue](post-a-statement-to-revenue.md).

pages.title: Download a report
pages.body:
# Download a report

Open the report, select **Download** at its top right, then select **PDF**, **Excel (.xlsx)** or **CSV**. The file holds the same numbers as the screen, because both are built from the same figures.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Reports**.
2. Select the report you want. See [Find and read a report](find-and-read-a-report.md).
3. Select **Download**, at the top right of the report.
4. Select **PDF**, **Excel (.xlsx)** or **CSV**.

The file saves the way any download does. On a phone, look in your Files or Downloads app.

## Which format to pick

- **PDF** is the one to print, forward, or send to a bank or a partner. It is laid out as a document.
- **Excel (.xlsx)** is the one to work in. Some reports arrive as several sheets: **Production Overview (Daily) (last 30 days)** gives one sheet per well, and **Production Variance** gives one sheet each for **Company**, **Leases** and **Wells**.
- **CSV** is the plain rows, for loading into other software.

When the menu says **CSV (.zip)**, that report has more than one table, so the CSV arrives as a zip folder holding one file per table. That is the case for the three **Company Digest** reports and the **Pumper Report**.

## What happens next

Nothing in the workspace changes and nobody is notified. The file is a copy taken at the moment you selected it, so a download from last week does not update itself.

The file carries the rows the report shows on screen, over the same stretch of time.

**View in new tab**, beside **Download**, opens the same PDF in a browser tab instead of saving it. That is usually the quickest way to print.

## What you need

**Download** is on every report you can open, so the **View reports** permission that puts **Reports** in the menu is all it takes.

pages.title: Find and read a report
pages.body:
# Find and read a report

Open the menu and select **Reports**, then select a report's name in the list. It opens as a finished document, with its headline numbers, charts and tables already worked out.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Reports**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select a group heading to open it. The groups are **Company**, **Production**, **Tanks**, **Wells**, **RRC** and **Pumper**.
3. Select the report's name.
4. Wait for the grey blocks to fill in. Most reports take a moment, and the digests take a few seconds.
5. Scroll down to read it.

**Company** is already open when the page loads, and the page opens on **Daily Company Digest** until you pick something else. On a phone the list sits above the report, so the report is below it.

To read the same thing as a printable page, select **View in new tab**. That opens the report's PDF in a new browser tab.

## What happens next

Nothing changes and nobody is told. Opening a report only reads your data.

The web address now carries the report you are on. Bookmark it to come straight back, or send it to a coworker, who sees the same report if their permissions allow it.

The list holds the reports you are allowed to open, so two people can see different lists.

## How current the numbers are

- The three **Company Digest** reports are compiled overnight. What you see is what that morning's email carried.
- Every other report is worked out from current data and held for up to an hour, so opening it twice in a row is instant.
- A name ending in "(last 30 days)" or "(last 7 days)" covers that stretch and no more. So does the **Pumper Report**.
- **Simplified Production**, **Tanks Called In** and **Gross vs Net Production** cover the month so far. The rest cover everything you have entered.

## What you need

**Reports** needs the **View reports** permission, which in turn needs production and revenue viewing. Ask whoever runs your workspace.

The **Wells** group carries one entry per well, built from your well list, so a well appears there the day it is added.

## Next

- [What each report shows](what-each-report-shows.md)
- [Download a report](download-a-report.md)
- [Have reports emailed to you](have-reports-emailed-to-you.md)
- [Listen to a report read aloud](listen-to-a-report-read-aloud.md)

pages.title: Have reports emailed to you
pages.body:
# Have reports emailed to you

Open **Reports**, select the gear beside the **Reports** heading, then switch on **Daily**, **Weekly** or **Monthly** on the report's row. The **Company Digest** and the production reports can be emailed, and every other row's **Section** column ends in "not emailable yet".

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Reports**.
2. Select the gear icon beside the **Reports** heading. The **Report delivery** panel opens.
3. Find the report's row in the grid. The rows that can be sent are **Company Digest**, **Company Daily Summary**, **Production Overview (last 30 days)**, **Production Overview (Daily) (last 30 days)**, **Production Variance** and **Exception Report (last 30 days)**.
4. Switch on **Daily**, **Weekly** or **Monthly**. Each switch saves on its own as you flip it.
5. Set **Arrives at**, at the top of the panel, to the hour you want.
6. Pick **Central**, **Eastern**, **Mountain** or **Pacific** beside it.
7. Close the panel.

**Arrives at** is one setting shared by every scheduled report. Changing it moves all of them, and there is no separate time per report.

## What happens next

Reports go to the address on your account, starting with the next send that frequency is due.

- **Daily** arrives every day and covers yesterday.
- **Weekly** arrives on Friday and covers the seven full days ending Thursday.
- **Monthly** arrives on the 1st and covers the month just ended.

**Company Digest**, **Company Daily Summary** and the two **Production Overview** reports cover the stretch the frequency names. **Production Variance** and the **Exception Report** keep their own lookback, so for those the frequency sets how often you get one rather than what it covers.

Everything due on the same day arrives as one email, not one per report, with the subject "*Your company* Daily Reports" (or Weekly, or Monthly). Each report is attached as a PDF, whatever format you download it in on screen. The body carries a short summary of what stands out, a button into the app, and a link that opens this same panel.

## Who else this affects

The schedule belongs to the workspace, not to you. Anyone who can manage reports sees the same switches, and switching one off stops that report for everyone it was going to.

The address a report goes to is fixed when its row is first switched on. If a coworker switched a row on before you, it goes to them, and switching it off and on again does not change who is on it.

## Turning it off

Switch the same cell off. That stops the sends and keeps the recipient list, so switching it back on later resumes to the same people.

## What you need

- One of **Admin**, **Manage oil production**, **Manage gas production**, **Manage disposal** or **Manage statements** to work the switches and the hour. Ask whoever runs your workspace.
- An email address on your account, under **Settings**, for the reports to go to.
- A row whose **Section** column does not end in "not emailable yet". The rest can still be read and downloaded. See [Download a report](download-a-report.md).

The same grid is at **Settings**, then the **Reports** tab, if you would rather set it up there.

pages.title: Listen to a report read aloud
pages.body:
# Listen to a report read aloud

Open the report and select **Narrate**, next to the report's title. Orion reads it out loud, starting a second or two after you select it.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Reports**.
2. Select the report you want. See [Find and read a report](find-and-read-a-report.md).
3. Wait until the report has finished loading. **Narrate** appears beside its title.
4. Select **Narrate**.
5. To stop it, select **Stop**. That is the same button, which changes while Orion is talking.

## What happens next

Orion reads a spoken version of the report rather than the page word for word. Written passages come across as they stand, charts are summed up as the point you would have taken from looking at one, and tables are framed: what the table covers, who leads and by how much, and what is missing.

Figures and units are said the way a person would say them, so "MCF" comes out spelled letter by letter and "bbl" comes out as barrels.

Orion reads whichever report is on screen, always from the start. Leaving the page stops the narration. Nothing is changed by narrating a report, and nobody else hears it or is told.

## What you need

- The **Use AI** permission.
- AI credits in your workspace. Narration draws on the same pool as Orion's answers, and **Buy more** in the menu under your name tops them up. See [Buy AI credits](../orion-ai/buy-ai-credits.md).
- Sound on your device. On a phone, check the volume and the silent switch.

## Related

- [Talk to Orion out loud](../orion-ai/talk-to-orion-out-loud.md)

pages.title: What each report shows
pages.body:
# What each report shows

Use this to pick the report that answers your question, then open it from the list in **Reports**. The list is grouped the same way this page is, in the same order, and it holds the reports your permissions allow.

To open one, see [Find and read a report](find-and-read-a-report.md). To take one away with you, see [Download a report](download-a-report.md).

## Company

### Daily Company Digest

The whole company on one page for yesterday: headline barrels and dollars, anything flagged as out of line, what the pumpers reported, and the production trend. For an owner or manager who wants one look each morning. It is the same document the daily email carries.

### Weekly Company Digest

The same document over the last seven full days, ending Thursday. For a Friday review, when a single day is too noisy to judge anything by.

### Monthly Company Digest

The month just ended, with revenue on settled statement dollars rather than estimates. For closing the month and seeing what actually came in by lease.

## Production

### Company Daily Summary

One row per date for the whole company: oil, oil in stock, oil sold, water and gas. For anyone who needs the company's day-by-day history in one table, back as far as your entries go.

### Production Overview (last 30 days)

One row per well with its oil, gas and water totals for the last 30 days. For a quick ranking of which wells carried the month.

### Production Overview (Daily) (last 30 days)

One row per well per day for the last 30 days, including oil sold. For chasing a specific day on a specific well. In Excel it arrives as one sheet per well.

### Production Variance

Every scope from company down to lease and well, showing how oil, gas and water moved over 1 day, 7 days and 30 days as percentages. For spotting a decline early, and for telling a real fall from a slow day.

### Exception Report (last 30 days)

Only the facilities that have drifted from their own 30-day average, plus streams that have stopped being measured at all. For a morning check when you want the short list rather than every well.

## Tanks

### Water Disposed (last 30 days) and Water Disposed (last 7 days)

Water put away down each saltwater disposal well, with injection and casing pressures, the meter reading and the date it was last read. For anyone watching disposal volumes and pressures against a permit.

### Simplified Production

Stock reconciliation for the month so far, tank by tank: opening barrels, sales, dispositions, transfers, closing barrels and the production that accounts for the difference. For proving that what came out of the ground matches what is in the tanks and what left on a truck.

### Battery Capacity

Every tank with its capacity, what is in it now, and how full it is as a percentage, in both barrels and inches. For deciding what needs a truck before it runs over.

### Tanks Called In

The tanks called in this month, with the gatherer, the stock at the time, and how many days it has been. For chasing a pickup that has not come. See [Call in a tank for pickup](../daily-production-entry/call-in-a-tank-for-pickup.md).

### Tank Measurement Audit

Every gauge reading with who entered it, who changed it, who deleted it, and when. For settling an argument about a number, and for an auditor who asks how a figure was arrived at.

### Gauge History

Every gauge reading in plain rows: tank, date, time, inches, barrels and the change since the reading before. For working through a tank's history without the audit columns in the way.

### Transport Tickets

Every run ticket you have recorded: opening and closing gauge, gross and corrected barrels, gravity, BS&W, purchaser and transport company. For checking a hauler's paperwork against your own. See [Log a run ticket](../daily-production-entry/log-a-run-ticket.md).

## Wells

### Well Test Report

The latest test on each well: oil, gas and water rates per day, gas-oil ratio, oil and water cut, the volumes those rates extrapolate to, and days online against days down. For an engineer or a consultant judging how each well is performing.

### Gross vs Net Production

This month's volumes for each facility split by interest: gross, your working interest, your net working interest, and the royalty share. For working out what is yours before the money arrives.

### One entry per well

Below those two, the list carries an entry for each of your wells, titled with the well's name. Each is that well's own production history, day by day: oil, gas and water. For looking at a single well without everything else around it.

## RRC

### RRC Monthly Reconciliation

Each producing well and month with your oil sales runs against the purchaser's oil, your gas production against the purchaser's gas and lease use, and the difference each way in volume and percent. For anyone filing with the Railroad Commission who needs the two sides to agree first.

### RRC Monthly Well Detail

The same months in full: opening stock, oil production, sales, dispositions, closing stock, gas produced and sold, water, and days online. For backing up a filing line by line when a number is questioned.

## Pumper

### Pumper Report

How many of the last 30 days each facility was actually visited, as a coverage percentage, with a daily chart and a rate per facility. For a supervisor checking that the route is being run. It counts visits rather than volumes.

## Getting a report sent to you

The **Company Digest** and the production reports can be emailed on a schedule. See [Have reports emailed to you](have-reports-emailed-to-you.md).

pages.title: Approve or deny an action Orion wants to take
pages.body:
# Approve or deny an action Orion wants to take

When Orion wants to write something to your records, it stops and shows you a card headed with what it is about to do, such as **Record a tank gauge reading**, under the line **Orion needs your OK before this is saved.** Select **Approve** to let it through, or **Deny** to stop it.

## Steps

1. Read the title of the card. It says in plain words what Orion wants to do.
2. Check the details listed underneath. Each row shows a field and the value Orion intends to save. A batch of rows appears as a small table.
3. Select **Approve** to save it, or **Deny** to refuse it.

## What happens next

**Approve** writes the record immediately, exactly as shown on the card, and Orion carries on with the rest of your question. The record is now part of your company's data, so everyone with permission to see that area sees it.

**Deny** writes nothing. Orion is told you declined and continues the conversation, usually by asking what you would rather do.

If you close the chat or leave without answering, nothing is written. The request is dropped, and it does not come back when you reopen the chat later.

## Can it be undone

Not from the chat. Once approved, a record is corrected the same way any other record is: on the well, tank, meter or lease page it belongs to. This is why the card shows every value before it is written.

## What Orion can never do

- Every write to your records goes through this card. The software enforces the stop, so no request can talk Orion past it.
- Orion has no delete tools of any kind. It cannot remove a well, a reading, a person or a document, even if you approve it.
- Reading your records needs no approval. Anything Orion only looks at happens without asking.

Orion's own notes on how you like to work sit outside this. Orion keeps those on its own, and you can read and change them in **Settings**: see [Teach Orion about your operation](teach-orion-about-your-operation.md).

Administrators can switch off whole areas so Orion cannot even ask. See [Control what Orion is allowed to do](control-what-orion-is-allowed-to-do.md).

## In voice mode

The same card appears on the voice screen once Orion has finished speaking. Select **Approve** or **Deny** on it to carry on. See [Talk to Orion out loud](talk-to-orion-out-loud.md).

pages.title: Ask Orion a question
pages.body:
# Ask Orion a question

Open the menu and select **Orion**, type your question, and press Enter. Orion answers in the same window, using your own wells, tanks, meters, leases and documents.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Orion**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md) if the menu is not on screen.
2. Type your question in the box that reads **How can I help you today?**
3. Press Enter to send. To start a new line instead, hold Shift and press Enter.

Once a chat is going, the box at the bottom reads **Ask Orion…** and works the same way.

## What happens next

Orion thinks for a moment, then the answer writes itself onto the screen. Some answers include a chart.

- To stop an answer part-way, select the round button with the square in it, labelled **Stop generating**.
- To copy an answer, select the copy icon under it.
- To hear it read out loud, select the speaker icon under it. Select the square to stop.

## What Orion can and cannot change

Orion reads your records on its own. To add or change anything in them, it shows you a card first and waits for you to press **Approve**. See [Approve or deny an action Orion wants to take](approve-or-deny-an-action-orion-wants-to-take.md).

Orion has no way to delete anything at all, with or without your approval.

Orion also keeps its own notes on how you like to work, and it can update those without asking. They are yours to read and change: see [Teach Orion about your operation](teach-orion-about-your-operation.md).

## Who else sees it

Nobody. Your chats are yours alone. Other people in your workspace cannot open them, and administrators cannot either.

The chat saves itself a moment after you send your first message, and takes its title from what you typed. Find it again in the **Chats** panel: see [Find an old conversation](find-an-old-conversation.md).

## What you need

To use Orion your account needs the **Use AI** permission, which is what puts **Orion** in the menu. An administrator grants it in **Settings**, on the **Organization** tab, under **Members**.

Your workspace also needs AI credits. See [Get Orion working again after running out of credits](what-to-do-when-you-run-out-of-credits.md).

pages.title: Attach a document to your question
pages.body:
# Attach a document to your question

Select the paperclip button beside the message box, pick the file off your device, then type your question and send it. The file goes to Orion with that message.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Orion**.
2. Select the paperclip button to the right of the message box, labelled **Upload from disk**.
3. Choose one or more files. On a phone this opens your photos and files.
4. Check the chips that appear above the message box. Each one names a file you attached.
5. Type your question, such as "what does this run sheet say about the Smith 1?", and press Enter.

To take a file back off before sending, select the small **x** on its chip.

## What to attach

Attach photos, PDF files and plain text files. A photo of a paper ticket works, and so does a scan.

For a spreadsheet, upload it in **Files** first and then ask Orion about it by name. Orion can open anything in **Files** on its own.

## Attach something already in Files

1. Select the **+** button beside the paperclip, labelled **Attach from knowledge base**.
2. Browse the folders and tick the files you want.
3. Select **Add files**.

This points Orion at a document already in your workspace rather than sending a new copy.

## What happens next

A file off your device goes with that one message only, and the chips above your sent message show what went with it. It is not filed anywhere and it does not appear in **Files**. To keep a document in the system, upload it in **Files** instead.

Asking about a file is a read, so nothing is saved and no approval is needed. If Orion offers to record something it found in the file, it asks first: see [Approve or deny an action Orion wants to take](approve-or-deny-an-action-orion-wants-to-take.md).

## Who else sees it

Nobody. The file goes into your private chat and is not added to your company's records.

pages.title: Buy AI credits
pages.body:
# Buy AI credits

Select your picture at the top right, then select **Buy more** beside **AI Credits**. You need to be an administrator or the owner, and the credits go to the whole workspace rather than to one person.

## Steps

1. Select your picture at the top right of any screen.
2. Select **Buy more**, beside the **AI Credits** number. The menu closes and the **Buy AI credits** window opens.
3. Type a whole dollar amount into **Amount to spend**. It starts at 50.
4. Check **Payment method**. It fills in with your organization's card.
5. Check the breakdown: **Subtotal**, **Sales tax**, and **Total**.
6. Select the button reading **Pay** and the total, such as **Pay $54.13**.

**Cancel** closes the window without charging anything.

## What happens next

The card is charged straight away and **Payment received** appears with the number of credits added. Select **Done** to close it. The balance in your picture menu updates without a reload.

The charge cannot be undone from inside WildcatIQ. To reverse one, [contact support](../getting-help/contact-support.md).

## Who else sees it

The balance is shared. Everyone in the workspace draws Orion from the same pot and sees the same number in their own menu.

Every member can see the balance. Completing the purchase needs an administrator or the owner.

## If there is no card

**No cards on file** in **Payment method**, with **Add a card on the Billing tab to buy credits.** underneath, means the workspace has no card saved.

1. Open **Settings** from your picture menu.
2. Select **Billing**. This opens your card details with our payment provider in a new browser tab.
3. Add a card there, then come back to WildcatIQ and buy again.

## If you have referral credit

When your workspace has platform credit from a referral, it is spent before the card. A **Platform credit** line appears in the breakdown, and if it covers the whole amount, **Payment method** reads **Platform credit** and the button reads **Use $50.00 credit**. No card is charged in that case.

## Buying from Settings instead

Administrators can also open **Settings**, select the **AI** tab, then the **Credits** subtab. That page shows **Credits remaining** in large type and buttons for **$25**, **$50**, **$100**, **$250** and **$1,000**. Picking one and selecting **Buy $50 of credits** opens the same window as above, with the amount already filled in.

pages.title: Control what Orion is allowed to do
pages.body:
# Control what Orion is allowed to do

Open **Settings** from your picture menu, select the **AI** tab, then the **Permissions** subtab. The grid there lists the parts of your business, and a switch turns Orion's access to each one on or off. You need to be an administrator or the owner.

## Steps

1. Select your picture at the top right and select **Settings**.
2. Select the **AI** tab.
3. Select the **Permissions** subtab.
4. Find the row for the area you care about, such as **Wells**, **Oil & tanks**, **Leases & owners** or **Inventory**.
5. Switch off the column you want to block: **Read**, **Add** or **Edit**.

## What happens next

The change saves as soon as you flip the switch, and applies straight away to everyone in the workspace. Switching it back on restores it just as quickly.

A switch that is off stops the underlying tools from running at all. The software enforces it, so no request can talk Orion round it.

## Reading the grid

- **Read** is looking at records. **Add** is creating new ones. **Edit** is changing ones that exist.
- A dash instead of a switch means there is nothing to allow or block: Orion has no way to do that action in that area.
- There is no **Delete** column because Orion has no way to delete anything, anywhere.
- **Team messages** and **Support** start switched off, because both send something out under your name. Switch them on if you want Orion to be able to message a coworker or open a support ticket for you.

## Rows that are not in the grid

Six things stay on and are left out of the grid:

- **Public records (RRC)**, **Geology library** and **Web search** reach nothing of your company's.
- **Memory** is Orion's own notes about how you like to work. See [Teach Orion about your operation](teach-orion-about-your-operation.md).
- **Data layer** and **Analysis** are how Orion reads and does arithmetic over the records the rows above already govern. They reach nothing the per-area switches do not already cover.

## What this does not replace

Switching **Add** or **Edit** on does not let Orion write on its own. Every write still stops and asks you first. See [Approve or deny an action Orion wants to take](approve-or-deny-an-action-orion-wants-to-take.md).

## Related controls

To stop someone using Orion at all, remove the **Use AI** permission from their account in **Settings**, on the **Organization** tab, under **Members**.

To stop Orion reading documents as they are uploaded, select the **Documents** subtab and switch off **Scan uploaded documents**. Anything it finds there is still only a suggestion you approve one at a time.

pages.title: Find an old conversation
pages.body:
# Find an old conversation

Every chat you have sent a message in is listed in the **Chats** panel on the left of the **Orion** page, newest first. Select a row to reopen it exactly as you left it.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Orion**.
2. Look at the **Chats** panel on the left. Each row shows the chat's title, how long ago it was used, and the last thing said, with **You:** in front of it when the last word was yours.
3. Select the row to open it.

## To search instead of scroll

1. Select the magnifying glass at the top of the **Chats** panel, labelled **Search chats**.
2. Type a word you remember into the box that reads **Search chats by topic…**. The list narrows as you type and puts the closest matches first.
3. Press Esc to close the search and get the full list back.

**No chats mention that.** means nothing in any chat contains that word.

## If the panel is not there

Select the clock icon in the top left of the chat, labelled **Show chat history**, to bring it back. The double arrow at the top of the panel, labelled **Collapse**, is what hides it.

## Why a chat might be missing

A chat earns a row once you have sent a message in it. An empty chat you opened and left is never saved and never listed.

**No conversations yet.** means you have not sent a message in any chat.

## Deleting one

On a computer, point at the row and select the bin icon on its right, labelled **Delete conversation**. There is no confirmation, it happens at once, and it cannot be undone. If you delete the chat you are reading, you are left on a fresh empty chat.

## Who else sees them

Nobody. Your chats are private to your own account. Nobody else in the workspace can open, search or delete them, and administrators cannot either.

pages.title: Print or save a conversation
pages.body:
# Print or save a conversation

Open the chat, then select the printer button at the top of the **Chats** panel. Your usual print window opens, where you can send it to a printer or choose **Save as PDF**.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Orion**, then open the chat you want.
2. Select the printer button at the top of the **Chats** panel, labelled **Print conversation**. If the panel is collapsed, the same button sits in the small stack of icons at the top left of the chat.
3. Wait for the print window to appear. Building the document takes a moment and the button shows a spinner while it works.
4. Choose your printer, or choose **Save as PDF** to keep a copy on your device.

## What you get

A typeset document with WildcatIQ letterhead, readable type, page numbers, and any charts redrawn at full size. Every message in the chat is included, including the parts you have scrolled past.

## What you need

- A chat with at least one message in it. The button stays greyed out on an empty chat.
- A chat that has finished saving. Give it a moment after your first message. **This conversation has not been saved yet.** means it is not stored yet, so send a message, wait a moment, and select the button again.
- The **Use AI** permission on your account. **You do not have permission to print this conversation.** means your account no longer has it. An administrator grants it in **Settings**, on the **Organization** tab, under **Members**.

If **Could not build the document. Please try again.** appears, select the button once more.

## Who else sees it

Nobody, until you hand out the printout or the PDF yourself. Printing does not share the chat inside WildcatIQ.

pages.title: Talk to Orion out loud
pages.body:
# Talk to Orion out loud

Select the microphone button in the bar across the top, then speak. The screen turns into a full-page listening view and Orion answers out loud, so you can use it with your hands full.

## Steps

1. Select the microphone button in the bar across the top, labelled **Talk to Orion**.
2. If your browser asks for permission to use the microphone, allow it.
3. Wait until the screen says **Listening…**, then say what you want.
4. Speak over Orion at any time to interrupt it. You do not have to wait for it to finish.
5. To leave, press Esc or select the **X** at the top right. Selecting the microphone button again also ends it.

## What you see while it runs

- **Start talking. Talk over me to interrupt.** is the resting screen, before anything is said.
- **Listening…** means it is your turn.
- **Orion is thinking…** means it is working on the answer.
- **Orion is speaking (talk to interrupt)** means it is reading the answer to you.

Your words appear in blue as they are heard, and Orion's reply appears underneath in large type. Charts appear on the same screen, because a spoken answer never describes one.

## Approving something by voice

If Orion wants to write a record, it finishes speaking and then shows the same **Approve** and **Deny** card you get in a typed chat. Nothing is written until you select **Approve**, and the microphone waits until you choose one. See [Approve or deny an action Orion wants to take](approve-or-deny-an-action-orion-wants-to-take.md).

## Whether it is kept

On the **Orion** page, everything said in voice mode is written into the chat you have open, so turning voice off leaves you with the whole conversation in writing.

Anywhere else in the app, a voice conversation is held in memory only. Leaving the page or reloading the browser loses it.

## What you need

- The **Use AI** permission, which is what puts the microphone in the top bar.
- A browser that can record. The button is greyed out and reads **Voice not supported in this browser** where it cannot. Try Chrome or Safari, or use the typed chat instead.
- AI credits on the workspace. Voice needs them the same as typing does: see [Get Orion working again after running out of credits](what-to-do-when-you-run-out-of-credits.md).

pages.title: Teach Orion about your operation
pages.body:
# Teach Orion about your operation

Open **Settings** from your picture menu, select the **AI** tab, then the **Orion** subtab. Two boxes there hold what Orion carries into every chat: how you want to be spoken to, and the facts about your operation it should always keep in mind.

## Steps

1. Select your picture at the top right and select **Settings**.
2. Select the **AI** tab.
3. Select the **Orion** subtab.
4. Type into **How Orion should work with you** for things like "keep answers short", "always confirm before writing", "I run the pumping unit myself".
5. Type into **What Orion remembers about your operation** for durable facts, such as what you call the Smith lease, which wells you watch daily, and what matters most to you.
6. Select **Save** under the box you changed.

**Unsaved changes** appears beside the buttons until you save. **Cancel** throws your edits away and puts back what was stored.

## What happens next

Your next question uses the new text, in a new chat or in one you already have open.

## Who else sees it

Nobody. Both boxes belong to your own account rather than to the company. Everyone in the workspace has their own pair, and yours never changes anyone else's Orion. This is why the **Orion** subtab is there for every member, not only administrators.

## Orion edits these boxes on its own

After a conversation, Orion may rewrite either box with what it learned. Every version is kept, so an edit you did not make is one click to put back.

## Undo a change, yours or Orion's

1. Select **History** under the box.
2. Read the list. Each line shows the version number, who wrote it, marked **you** or **Orion**, the reason, and the start of the text.
3. Select the circular arrow at the right of the version you want back.

The old text is restored as a new version, and the box on screen updates to match. Nothing in the list is lost, so you can go back again. **No history yet.** means the box has only ever been saved once.

pages.title: Get Orion working again after running out of credits
pages.body:
# Get Orion working again after running out of credits

Orion stops answering when the workspace's AI credit balance reaches zero. An administrator or the owner tops it up, and Orion works again at once: see [Buy AI credits](buy-ai-credits.md).

## How to tell that this is the problem

Open your picture menu at the top right and read the **AI Credits** number. Zero, or a number below zero, is the cause.

You may also have seen one of these:

- In the Orion side panel: **You're out of AI credits**, with a **Buy AI credits** button.
- The send button in the side panel turned into a star. Selecting it opens the top-up window instead of sending.
- Voice mode ended the moment you turned it on, and the **Buy AI credits** window opened.
- On the full **Orion** page, a red box saying Orion is having trouble responding. Check the balance in your picture menu.

## Steps to fix it

1. Select your picture at the top right.
2. Select **Buy more**.
3. Follow [Buy AI credits](buy-ai-credits.md).

Orion answers again as soon as the payment goes through. You do not have to reload the page or start a new chat.

## If you are not an administrator

You can see the balance in your picture menu. Topping it up needs an administrator or the owner, so ask whoever administers your workspace.

## If the balance is below zero

A long piece of work can run past the last credit, which leaves the balance negative. The message then reads **Your AI credit balance is negative** and names how far overdrawn you are. Buying credits settles it and Orion resumes.

## Nothing is lost while you are out

- Files you uploaded are still stored. Once credits are back, Orion can read them without you uploading them again.
- Your chats are untouched and still in the **Chats** panel.
- Records already saved are unaffected. This only stops Orion answering.

## Waiting instead of buying

A paid subscription includes an allowance of credits that renews each month, and the number in the menu is that allowance and any purchased credit added together. If your renewal is close, the balance comes back on its own.

pages.title: Find a document
pages.body:
# Find a document

Open the menu, select **Files**, and type part of the name into the **Search files…** box at the top right. It looks through every folder at once, including folders you do not have open.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Files**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the **Search files…** box at the top right.
3. Type any part of the file or folder name. Results appear as you type.

Capital letters do not matter. Any part of the name works, so typing `corbett` finds `Roy Corbett 2-2 ticket.pdf`.

## Reading the results

Every result shows the folder it lives in beside its name, written as a trail such as **Files / Wells / Production / Roy Corbett 2-2**. That is how you tell two files with the same name apart.

Both files and folders are matched. Select a file to open it. Select a folder to go into it, which also clears the search.

When nothing matches, the list reads **No files or folders matching "corbett".**

## Clear the search

Press Esc, or delete what you typed. You go back to the folder you were browsing.

## Search inside a document

This box matches names. To find a document by the words inside it, ask Orion. Orion reads every uploaded file, so it can answer from what is inside them.

Related: [Open and read a file](open-and-read-a-file.md).

pages.title: Open and read a file
pages.body:
# Open and read a file

Select the file's row in **Files** and it opens in a viewer built for that kind of file. Select the back arrow at the top left to return to the folder it lives in.

## Open a file

1. Open the menu and select **Files**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Find the file. See [Find a document](find-a-document.md).
3. Select anywhere on its row.

Orion's panel opens beside the file, so you can ask questions about what you are looking at.

Each file has its own web address, so you can bookmark an open file or send the link to a colleague. They need permission to open **Files** to see it.

## PDFs

The bar across the top of the viewer shows the page count, for example **8 pages**. Scroll down through the document to move between pages.

On the right of that bar:

- The rotate arrow turns the page 90 degrees.
- The minus and plus buttons zoom out and in, 20 percent at a time.
- The percentage between them shows the current zoom. Select it to go back to 100 percent.

## Photos and images

The same rotate and zoom controls, with the file name instead of a page count.

## Spreadsheets

`.xlsx`, `.xls` and `.csv` files open as a grid, with lettered columns across the top and numbered rows down the side, like a spreadsheet. The first row of the file is shown as the header.

Scroll sideways to reach columns that do not fit. If a cell is cut off, point at it to see the whole value.

If the file holds more than one sheet, tabs appear along the bottom. Select a tab to switch sheets. A `.zip` of CSV files opens the same way, one tab per CSV inside it.

## Well logs

`.las` files open as a well log: depth running down the left, and the curves plotted in tracks beside it in the usual colors.

A bar above the plot names what the file says about the well, including **Well**, **Field**, **API/UWI**, **Interval** and the number of **Curves**.

A file that carries header information but no readings has nothing to plot. Download it to inspect it.

## Documents you can edit

A note or a `.md` document opens in the editor, ready to type in. See [Write a note](write-a-note.md).

## Everything else

Other file types show a summary page with the file's type, name, size and date. To read the document itself, use **Download** on the file's row in **Files** and it opens in the program on your device that handles it. See [Rename, move or delete a file](rename-move-or-delete-a-file.md).

## Going back

The back arrow at the top left returns you to the folder the file lives in, even if you arrived from a search or a link.

pages.title: Organize files into folders
pages.body:
# Organize files into folders

Open the menu, select **Files**, select **Add**, then select **New folder**, type a name and press Enter. New folders are created inside whichever folder you have open.

## Make a folder

1. Open the menu and select **Files**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Open the folder you want the new folder to sit inside. To work at the top level, select **Files** in the trail of names at the top of the page.
3. Select **Add** at the top right.
4. Select **New folder**. A new row appears with the box **Folder name** ready for typing.
5. Type the name and press Enter.

Selecting away from the box also creates the folder. Press Esc to cancel, or leave the name blank.

The name you type is the name it keeps, so choose it carefully. Folders are renamed, moved, pinned and deleted elsewhere, not from this page.

## Move around

The row of names at the top of the page is your trail, starting at **Files**. Select any name in it to go back to that folder. Select a folder row in the list to go into it.

Folders are listed above files and sorted by name. Each folder shows the word **Folder** in the **Type** column and the date it was created under **Modified**.

An empty folder reads **This folder is empty.**

## Folders you did not make

Some folders are created for you and are always there: **Wells**, **Leases**, **Tanks**, **Meters**, **Batteries**, **Projects**, **Data Entry** and **Chat Attachments**.

Folders for your wells, tanks, meters, batteries and leases are kept up to date automatically inside them. Three of those are split one level deeper by what the equipment is for:

- **Wells** holds **Production** and **Disposal**.
- **Tanks** holds **Oil** and **Saltwater**.
- **Meters** holds **Gas** and **Saltwater**.

So a producing well's folder sits at **Files / Wells / Production**. Batteries and leases sit directly under their own folder.

## Put a file in a folder

Upload it while that folder is open, or move an existing file into it. See [Upload a document](upload-a-document.md) and [Rename, move or delete a file](rename-move-or-delete-a-file.md).

## Who else sees it

Everyone in your company who can open **Files** sees the folder and everything in it.

pages.title: Rename, move or delete a file
pages.body:
# Rename, move or delete a file

Point at the file's row in **Files** with your mouse and five buttons appear at the right end of the row: **Download**, **Move to folder**, **Rename**, **Pin** and **Delete**.

Pointing at a row is what brings the buttons out, so use a computer with a mouse for everything on this page.

## Rename a file

1. Open the menu and select **Files**, then find the file. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Point at its row and select the pencil, **Rename**.
3. The name is selected ready to be replaced. Type the new name.
4. Press Enter.

Press Esc instead to cancel. The old name stays if you leave the box blank.

The name changes everywhere at once, including inside every folder the file sits in. There is no separate undo, so rename it again to put it back.

## Move a file to another folder

1. Point at the file's row and select the folder-with-arrow icon, **Move to folder**.
2. A panel headed **Move "Roy Corbett ticket.pdf"** opens with your folders listed.
3. Select the small arrow beside a folder to open it and see the folders inside.
4. Select the folder you want. It highlights.
5. Select **Move here**.

The folder the file is already in is greyed out and cannot be picked. Select **Cancel** to close without moving.

The file leaves the folder you moved it from. To put it back, move it again.

## Pin a file to the top of its folder

Point at the row and select the pin. The file jumps to the top of that folder's list and shows a small pin beside its name.

Pinning applies to one folder. A file pinned in one folder is not pinned in another. Select the pin again to unpin it.

## Download a file

Point at the row and select the downward arrow, **Download**. The file opens in a new tab, using a link that is good for one hour.

**Download** is for files you uploaded or scanned. To keep a copy of a document written inside WildcatIQ with **New doc**, select the text in the editor and copy it.

## Delete a file

1. Point at the file's row and select the trash icon, **Delete**.
2. A message asks **Delete "Roy Corbett ticket.pdf"?** and warns that this permanently deletes the file and removes it from every folder, and that it cannot be undone.
3. Select **Delete** to confirm, or **Cancel** to keep the file.

The row disappears straight away. The file is gone from every folder it was in, and it can no longer be searched or read by Orion. There is no way to get it back, so download a copy first if you are unsure.

## Who else sees these changes

Everyone in your company who can open **Files**. Renames, moves and deletions apply to the shared file, not to your own copy of it.

## Folders

Folders are renamed, moved, pinned and deleted elsewhere, not from this page. See [Organize files into folders](organize-files-into-folders.md).

pages.title: Scan a document with your phone camera
pages.body:
# Scan a document with your phone camera

Open the menu, select **Files**, select **Add**, then select **Scan**. Your camera opens, you photograph each page, and WildcatIQ combines them into one PDF and files it for you.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Files**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Open the folder you want the scan in.
3. Select **Add** at the top right.
4. Select **Scan**. A panel headed **Scan document** opens and reads **Preparing camera…** while it starts.
5. Allow camera access if your phone asks.
6. Hold the page flat and steady. A green outline traces the edges of the page when WildcatIQ can see them.
7. Tap the round white button at the bottom of the picture to capture the page.
8. Repeat for each page. A thumbnail of every captured page appears in a strip below, numbered in order.
9. Select **Done**.

## Fixing pages before you finish

Each thumbnail has three small controls:

- The trash icon at its top right deletes that page.
- The arrows at its bottom corners move the page earlier or later in the order.

The counter at the bottom left reads **No pages yet** until you capture one, then **1 page**, **2 pages** and so on. **Done** stays greyed out until there is at least one page.

## Use photos instead of the camera

Where the panel offers **Take / choose photos**, select it to use your phone's own camera app or your photo library. You can pick several photos at once, and they are handled exactly like captured pages.

## What happens next

**Done** changes to **Building…** while the pages are combined. The finished PDF is uploaded to the folder you had open, named for today's date, for example `scan-2026-08-25.pdf`.

From there it behaves like any other upload: Orion reads it and may propose records for you to approve. See [What happens when you scan a document](what-happens-when-you-scan-a-document.md).

## Who else sees it

Everyone in your company who can open **Files**.

## Undo

Select **Cancel** before selecting **Done** to discard the scan. After it is filed, delete it like any other file. See [Rename, move or delete a file](rename-move-or-delete-a-file.md).

pages.title: Tag a note to a well or lease
pages.body:
# Tag a note to a well or lease

Open the note and select **Wells** or **Leases** in the row of buttons under the title, then tick the ones the note is about. The note then appears on that well's or lease's **Notes** tab as well as in **Notes**.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Notes**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Open the note, or select **New note** to start one.
3. Under the title, select **Wells** or **Leases**.
4. Type in the search box at the top of the list to narrow it, or scroll it.
5. Select each one the note is about. A tick appears beside it and a count appears on the button.
6. Select outside the list, or press Esc, to close it.

The buttons are **Wells**, **Tanks**, **Meters**, **Batteries**, **Leases**, **People** and **Projects**. A note can carry as many tags as you like, of any mix of kinds.

## Remove a tag

Each tag sits above the buttons as a small chip showing its kind and its name, for example **WELL Roy Corbett 2-2**. Select the X on the chip to remove it.

## What happens next

Tags on a saved note are written immediately. **Saving…** appears beside the title and changes to **Saved**.

On a brand new note, tags are held until the note has a title or some text. Type something and the tags are saved along with it.

## Where the note then appears

Open the well, tank, meter, battery, lease or project you tagged and select its **Notes** tab. The note is listed there, and selecting it opens the same note you would open from **Notes**.

Tagging a person files the note against them for searching and for Orion. It does not add a tab anywhere.

## Starting from the well instead

If you are already looking at a well or lease, it is quicker to start there: select **Add** at the top right and select **Note**. The note opens already tagged to that well or lease.

## The name on a tag

The name shown on a tag is copied at the moment you add it. If the well is renamed later, the tag keeps the old name until you remove it and add it again. The note still appears on the right well's **Notes** tab either way.

## Who else sees it

Everyone in your company who can see notes. The lists you tag from hold the wells, tanks, meters, batteries, leases, people and projects in your company.

Related: [Write a note](write-a-note.md).

pages.title: Upload a document
pages.body:
# Upload a document

Open the menu, select **Files**, select **Add**, then select **Upload file** and pick the file from your device. It lands in the folder you have open, and Orion starts reading it in the background.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Files**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Open the folder you want the document in. The folder name is the heading at the top of the page. See [Organize files into folders](organize-files-into-folders.md).
3. Select **Add** at the top right.
4. Select **Upload file**.
5. Choose one file, or pick several at once.

## What happens next

The **Add** button changes to **Uploading…** and waits until the upload finishes. A row appears for each file with the words **Uploading & indexing…** beside its name.

When the rows are replaced by real file rows, the documents are stored. They show their **Type**, **Size** and **Modified** date, and Orion can search them.

Orion also reads each document to see whether it holds records worth adding, such as production readings, run tickets, invoices or people. Nothing is written to your records without your approval. See [What happens when you scan a document](what-happens-when-you-scan-a-document.md).

## Who else sees it

Everyone in your company who can open **Files** sees the document as soon as it is uploaded. Every document here is shared with your company.

## Limits

Everything you pick in one go is sent together, and the combined size must be at most 100 MB. Send a larger set in more than one batch.

## Undo

Delete the file. See [Rename, move or delete a file](rename-move-or-delete-a-file.md).

Related: [Scan a document with your phone camera](scan-a-document-with-your-phone-camera.md).

pages.title: What happens when you scan a document
pages.body:
# What happens when you scan a document

Orion reads every document you upload or scan, and where it recognizes records it offers them to you as a card you can edit and approve. Nothing is written to your wells, tanks, invoices or people until you select **Approve** on that card.

## What Orion does with the document

1. The file is stored in the folder you uploaded it to and indexed so it can be searched.
2. Orion reads the pages, including handwriting and photographs of paper.
3. Where it finds records it can recognize, such as tank gauge readings, run tickets, well tests, vendor invoices, inventory items or people, it writes them down as a proposal.
4. The proposal waits for you. It is never applied on its own.

## The approval card

When a proposal is ready you get a card headed like **Add 12 tank gauge readings?**, with the file name underneath, for example **From scan-2026-08-25.pdf.**

- Every value sits in its own box. Select a box and type to correct it.
- The trash icon at the end of a row removes that row.
- **Add row** at the bottom left adds a blank row.
- A row Orion was unsure about is tinted and carries an amber warning triangle. Point at the triangle to read why.
- For records that belong to a well, a **Well** box sits at the top. Pick the right well from **Choose a well…**. **Approve** stays greyed out until a well is chosen.
- Long extractions are paged 25 rows at a time, with **Previous** and **Next** at the bottom.

Select **Approve** to write the records, or **Dismiss** to throw the proposal away. Closing the card with the X, or by selecting outside it, dismisses it the same way.

## After you approve

The card reports what it did, for example **Added 12 tank gauge readings, updated 2 already on file, skipped 1 as duplicate.** Select **Done** to close it.

Records that were already on file are skipped or updated instead of being duplicated. Approving is not reversible from the card, so correct the values before you approve. To change a record afterwards, edit it where it lives.

## Where the card appears

The card opens on the page the records belong to:

- a producing well's page, for that well's records
- **Invoices**
- **Revenue**, and a statement's own page

Stay in the app after uploading and go to that page in the same sitting, and the card opens there. To have the records offered to you straight away, upload the document from the page it belongs to instead of from **Files**.

## Turning the reading off

An admin can turn this off for the whole company in **Settings**, under **AI**, on the **Documents** tab, with the **Scan uploaded documents** switch. With it off, documents are still stored and searchable, and no proposals are made.

Reading a document uses AI credits. Your company needs credits for Orion to read a document. Without them, documents are still stored and searchable.

## Who else sees it

The document is visible to everyone in your company who can open **Files**. The approval card is yours: it belongs to the upload you made, and nobody else sees it.

Related: [Upload a document](upload-a-document.md), [Scan a document with your phone camera](scan-a-document-with-your-phone-camera.md).

pages.title: Write a note
pages.body:
# Write a note

Open the menu, select **Notes**, then select **New note**. The note opens ready to type, and it saves itself as you write.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Notes**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **New note** at the top right.
3. Type a title over the word **Untitled** at the top, then press Enter or select below it.
4. Type the note in the large area underneath.
5. Close the note with the X at the top right, or by selecting outside it.

## Saving

There is no save button. The word **Saving…** appears beside the title while a change is being written, and changes to **Saved** when it is done. Wait for **Saved** before closing if you have just finished typing.

A note is kept once it has a title or some text.

## Formatting

The row of buttons above the writing area formats the text. Select some text first, then select a button.

Undo, Redo, Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 3, Bullet list, Numbered list, Blockquote, and Link.

**Link** asks you for the address in a small box, already filled in with `https://`. Type the web address and select OK. To remove a link, put the cursor in the linked words, select **Link** again, clear the box and select OK.

## Finding a note again

Notes are shown as cards, newest changes first. Each card shows the title, the first few lines, up to three tags and the date. Type into the **Search notes…** box at the top to narrow the list.

The search looks at the title, the tags, and roughly the first 200 characters of the note. Put anything you will search for near the top of the note or in its title.

## Delete a note

Open the note and select the trash icon at the top right, beside the title. The note is removed immediately with no confirmation, so be sure before you select it.

## Who else sees it

Everyone in your company who can see notes. Every note is shared with your company, and anyone allowed to manage notes can edit or delete one you wrote.

Related: [Tag a note to a well or lease](tag-a-note-to-a-well-or-lease.md).

pages.title: Add files to a project
pages.body:
# Add files to a project

Open the project, select **Add File** at the top right, and choose **Upload from computer** for a file on your device or **Select from files** for one already in Files. Either way the file lands in the project and Orion can read it.

## Upload a file from your computer or phone

1. Open the menu and select **Projects**.
2. Select the project's name.
3. Select **Add File** at the top right.
4. Select **Upload from computer**.
5. Pick one or more files. On a phone this opens your camera roll or file picker.

The button reads **Uploading…** while the file transfers, and the view switches to the **Files** tab. You can open and read the file straight away. Text inside a PDF or a photo is pulled out in the background, so Orion may take another minute to quote from it.

## Add a file that is already in Files

1. Open the project and select **Add File**.
2. Select **Select from files**.
3. Browse to the folder you want. Select a folder's row to open it, and select an earlier folder in the trail at the top to go back.
4. Select the rows you want. The count at the bottom left reads "2 selected". A file already in this project is greyed out and marked **Added**.
5. Select **Add 1 file** at the bottom right. The button counts what you picked: **Add 2 files**, and so on.

The file is now in both places at once. It stays where it was in Files, and it is not copied. Renaming, editing, or deleting it in one place does the same in the other.

## Open a file in the project

Select the **Files** tab, then select a file's name. On a computer, rest the mouse pointer on a row to show its buttons at the right: download, move, rename, pin, and delete.

Moving a file here moves it between folders inside this project. To take a file out of a project without deleting it, open **Files**, then **Projects**, then the project, and move the file to another folder there. See [Rename, move, or delete a file](../documents-and-notes/rename-move-or-delete-a-file.md).

## Can this be undone

Deleting a file cannot be undone. The confirmation says so: it permanently deletes the file and removes it from every folder, including the folder it came from before you added it to the project. To take a file out of the project only, move it rather than delete it.

## Who can see it

Anyone the project is shared with, plus the workspace Owner. See [Share a project with a coworker](share-a-project-with-a-coworker.md).

A file you upload straight into the project is private to those people. A file you added with **Select from files** stays visible to everyone who could already see it in its original folder, because it is still sitting in that folder too. Putting a file into a private project does not hide it.

pages.title: Ask Orion about a project
pages.body:
# Ask Orion about a project

Open the project and type your question in the box on the **Orion** tab. Orion answers from that project's files, tasks, and notes.

## Ask a question

1. Open the menu and select **Projects**.
2. Select the project's name. It opens on the **Orion** tab with a fresh chat.
3. Type your question in the box that reads "How can I help you today?".
4. Press Enter, or select the send button at the right of the box.

Press Shift and Enter together to start a new line instead of sending.

## What Orion answers from here

- Every file in the project, by name. Ask it to read one and it reads the whole file, including a full LAS log or a spreadsheet.
- The project's tasks, and the budget and spend figures on them.
- The project's notes.
- Your earlier chats in this project.

When it searches for wording inside documents, it searches this project's files. If Orion needs a document, add it to the project first. See [Add files to a project](add-files-to-a-project.md).

## Attach a file to one question

- Select the **+** button at the right of the message box to pick a file already in the workspace.
- Select the paperclip button to send a file from your device.

## Ask Orion to write something down

Ask it to write, draft, or save a summary as a document and it saves the document into this project's **Files** tab. You approve the write before anything is saved, so nothing appears without your say-so.

Ask it to save a note and it writes a note on the project. It writes one only when you ask.

## Start a new chat, or go back to an old one

- Select **New Chat** at the top right to start over.
- The chat history panel at the left of the chat lists your earlier chats in this project. Select one to reopen it, or use the search box there to find one by topic.

Deleting a chat from the history panel removes it for good. A chat you have here is also listed in the history on the main **Orion** page.

## Who can see your chats

Only you. Orion chats are private to the person who had them, even from the other people on the project and from the workspace Owner.

## What Orion does on a project

Orion is set up to test a prospect rather than agree with you. It leads with the evidence against a prospect as much as the evidence for it, says when the project's data cannot answer a question, and holds a number where the data puts it. That is deliberate.

## What you need to use it

Orion on a project needs the **Use AI** permission on your account and AI credits in the workspace. Credits are in the account menu under your picture at the top right, with **Buy more**. See [Buy AI credits](../orion-ai/buy-ai-credits.md).

pages.title: Rename a project
pages.body:
# Rename a project

Open the project, select its name in the middle of the bar at the top, type the new name, and press Enter. The name changes everywhere at once, and you can rename it again as often as you like.

## Rename it

1. Open the menu and select **Projects**.
2. Select the project's name to open it.
3. Select the project name in the middle of the bar at the top. It turns into a box with the text selected.
4. Type the new name.
5. Press Enter.

You can also rename it from the project name in the trail at the very top of the page, next to **Projects**. It works the same way.

## What happens next

The new name shows immediately, and the web address of the project changes to match it. A bookmark or link to the old address stops working, so bookmark the page again after renaming.

Nothing inside the project moves. The files, tasks, notes, and Orion chats all stay where they are.

## Cancel a rename

Press Esc while the box is open and the old name comes back. Selecting elsewhere on the page while the box is open saves the new name rather than cancelling it.

## Who sees it

Everyone the project is shared with, plus the workspace Owner. The new name is what they see the next time the page loads. Nobody is notified.

pages.title: Share a project with a coworker
pages.body:
# Share a project with a coworker

Open the project, select **Share**, then select the **+** button next to the person's name under **Add someone**. They can see and work in the project immediately, and only you, its creator, add and remove people.

## Who can see the project before you share it

Two people, and no more:

- You, because you created it.
- The workspace Owner, the one member whose **Status** reads **Owner** under **Settings**, then **Organization**, then **Members**.

Everyone else is locked out of the project, its files, its tasks, and anything Orion has learned about it, whatever their permissions. An Admin is no exception: only the Owner sees every project.

## Share it

1. Open the menu and select **Projects**.
2. Select the project's name.
3. Select **Share** at the top right.
4. Find the person under **Add someone**. Their email is shown under their name. Someone who has been invited joins this list once they have set up their login, so share it with them then.
5. Select the **+** button at the right of their row.
6. Select the **X** at the top right of the dialog to close it.

## What happens next

The person is added straight away. No email and no notification is sent, so tell them yourself. The project is in their **Projects** list the next time they open it.

The number beside the **Share** button counts the people the project is shared with.

## What a shared person can do

Everything you can do. There are no roles and no view-only option. Anyone you add can read, upload, rename, and delete the project's files, add and change tasks, write notes, chat with Orion about the project, and rename the project itself.

The one thing they cannot do is change who else is on it. The **Add someone** list and the remove buttons appear only for you. Everyone else opens the same dialog and sees only who is on the project.

Orion chats stay private. Each person sees only their own chats in the project, including you and the workspace Owner.

## Stop sharing

1. Open the project and select **Share**.
2. Select the **X** at the right of that person's row.

Access is cut off immediately. They lose the project, its files, and its tasks the next time the page loads. Nothing they added is deleted. You can add them back at any time the same way.

## What a shared person needs on their own account

Sharing puts them on the project. Their workspace permissions decide what opens. An admin sets these under **Settings**, then **Organization**:

1. Find the person in the **Members** table.
2. Select the button in their **Permissions** column.
3. Turn on **Projects** and **Files** to open the project and its documents.
4. Turn on **Personal agenda** or **Org agenda** to see the project's tasks.
5. Turn on **Use AI** to use Orion in the project.

See [Set what a coworker can see](../people-and-access/set-what-a-coworker-can-see.md).

## Notes are the exception

A note written on a project can be read by everyone in the workspace whose account has **View notes** or **Notes** turned on, whether or not the project is shared with them, and it shows up on the main **Notes** page. Keep anything sensitive out of notes. See [Take notes on a project](take-notes-on-a-project.md).

pages.title: Start a project
pages.body:
# Start a project

Open the menu, select **Projects**, select **New Project**, type a name, and select **Create project**. The new project is private to you: nobody else in the workspace can see it until you share it.

A project holds the files, tasks, notes, and Orion chats for one piece of work, such as a prospect you are evaluating or a workover you are planning.

## Create the project

1. Open the menu and select **Projects**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **New Project** at the top right.
3. Type a name in the **Name** box, for example "Spraberry Study".
4. Select **Create project**.

The project appears in the list right away, in name order, A to Z. The **Items** column counts the files in the project, and **Modified** shows the date you created it.

## Open the project

1. Open the menu and select **Projects**.
2. Select the project's name in the **Name** column. Selecting elsewhere in the row does not open it.

The project opens on the **Orion** tab. The tabs across the top left are **Orion**, **Tasks**, **Files**, and **Notes**. The buttons at the top right are **Share**, **New Chat**, **New Task**, **New Note**, and **Add File**, and they work from any tab.

## Who can see it

Only you and the workspace Owner. Other members cannot see a project you created, whatever their permissions, until you add them. See [Share a project with a coworker](share-a-project-with-a-coworker.md).

## Can this be undone

You can rename a project at any time. See [Rename a project](rename-a-project.md). A project cannot be deleted, so if you create one by mistake, rename it and reuse it.

## Next

- [Add files to a project](add-files-to-a-project.md)
- [Ask Orion about a project](ask-orion-about-a-project.md)
- [Track work on a project](track-work-on-a-project.md)

pages.title: Take notes on a project
pages.body:
# Take notes on a project

Open the project and select **New Note** at the top right. The note is filed to the project automatically, and it saves itself as you type.

Notes are for what you and your team know: what you saw in the field, what was said on a call, what you decided and why. Orion reads them when you ask it about the project.

## Write a note

1. Open the menu and select **Projects**.
2. Select the project's name.
3. Select **New Note** at the top right.
4. Type a title over the word **Untitled** at the top.
5. Type the note underneath.
6. Close the window when you are done.
