There is no save button. **Saving…** appears at the top right while it writes, then **Saved**. The note appears as a card on the **Notes** tab straight away.

## Open or change a note

1. Select the **Notes** tab.
2. Select the note's card.
3. Edit the title or the text. It saves as you go.

## Delete a note

Open the note and select the bin button at the top right, to the right of **Saved**. It deletes immediately, with no confirmation, and cannot be undone.

## File the same note somewhere else as well

Under the title are buttons for **Wells**, **Tanks**, **Meters**, **Batteries**, **Leases**, **People**, and **Projects**. Select one, then pick from the list, to file the same note on that well, lease, or person too. The **Projects** tag is what keeps the note on this project, so leave that one in place.

## Who can see it

This is the one part of a project that is not private. A note written on a project can be read by everyone in the workspace whose account has **View notes** or **Notes** turned on, whether or not the project is shared with them, and it shows up on the main **Notes** page. Keep anything you do not want the whole company reading out of notes.

Files, tasks, and Orion chats in a project stay private. See [Share a project with a coworker](share-a-project-with-a-coworker.md).

For everything else about notes, see [Write a note](../documents-and-notes/write-a-note.md).

pages.title: Track work on a project
pages.body:
# Track work on a project

Open the project and select **New Task** at the top right to add a job to the project's board. The board has four columns, **Backlog**, **Queue**, **Doing**, and **Done**, and you move a task by opening it and changing its **Status**.

## Add a task

1. Open the menu and select **Projects**.
2. Select the project's name.
3. Select **New Task** at the top right.
4. Type what needs doing in the **Title** box. This is the only box you have to fill in.
5. Fill in anything else you need: **Description**, **Assignee**, **Priority**, **Status**, **Deadline**, **Budget**, **Spend**.
6. Select **Add Task**.

The card appears in the column you chose under **Status**, and a new task starts in **Backlog**. Selecting **Cancel**, or closing the window, throws away what you typed.

## Move a task to another column

1. Select the **Tasks** tab.
2. Select the card.
3. Select the **Status** box and choose **Backlog**, **Queue**, **Doing**, or **Done**.
4. Select **Save**.

On a computer you can also drag a card from one column to another. On a phone or a tablet, use **Status**.

## Change or delete a task

1. Select the card on the **Tasks** tab.
2. Edit any box, then select **Save**.

To delete it, select **Delete** at the bottom left of the same window, then select **Delete** again to confirm. Deleting a task is permanent and cannot be undone.

## About the Assignee box

The box starts on **Unassigned**, and the list holds your own name and the contractors from your **People** page. Putting someone's name on a task is a label. It does not send them anything, and it does not give them access to the project. If they need to see the task, share the project with them: see [Share a project with a coworker](share-a-project-with-a-coworker.md).

## Budget and spend

Fill in **Budget** and **Spend** on a task and it becomes a budget line for the project. To see what the project has budgeted, spent, and has left, ask on the **Orion** tab, for example "what is left in this project's budget". Orion adds up the figures on the tasks. See [Ask Orion about a project](ask-orion-about-a-project.md).

## Where else these tasks show up

A task created in a project also appears on the **Agenda** page in the **Tasks** view, and on the calendar if you gave it a deadline. It shows there only for people who can already see the project. See [Move work across the task board](../agenda/move-work-across-the-task-board.md).

## Who can see it

Anyone the project is shared with, plus the workspace Owner. To open the project's tasks, a person also needs **Personal agenda** or **Org agenda** turned on. See [Set what a coworker can see](../people-and-access/set-what-a-coworker-can-see.md).

pages.title: Add an event to the calendar
pages.body:
# Add an event to the calendar

Open the menu, select **Agenda**, then select **New Event**. Fill in **Title** and **Date**, select **Add Event**, and the event appears on the calendar straight away.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Agenda**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **New Event** at the top right.
3. Type a name in **Title**.
4. Set **Date**. It starts on the day the calendar is showing, which is not always today, so check it.
5. Set **Start** and **End**, or tick **All day** instead.
6. Type the lease or the yard in **Location** if the job has one.
7. Select the **People** box and tick everyone who needs to be there.
8. Type any notes in **Description**.
9. Select **Add Event**.

**Add Event** turns on once the event has a title, a date, and either **All day** ticked or a start and an end with the end after the start.

Changing **Start** carries **End** along with it and keeps the event the same length. Set **End** afterwards to make the job longer or shorter.

## Who you can put on an event

The **People** box lists everyone on file, in sections: **Members**, **Employees**, **Contractors**, **Service providers**, **Royalty owners** and **Gatherers**. **Whole org** at the top of the list stands for everyone in the workspace.

This is a wider list than **Assignee** on a task, which offers only people with a login. See [Assign work to someone](assign-work-to-someone.md).

## What happens next

Everyone in your workspace with **Personal agenda** or **Org agenda** permission sees the event.

It shows on **Month** as a line with a blue dot beside it, and on **Week** as a blue block at its time. Both grids show the time and the title. Location, people and description show inside the event.

Select the event any time to reopen it, change it, and select **Save**.

The day before, whoever created the event gets a reminder. Tell the people named on it yourself.

**Month** and **Week** cover about two months back and four months ahead. An event dated further out is saved, and it appears on the grid as its date comes into range.

To remove an event, see [Delete an event or task](delete-an-event-or-task.md).

pages.title: Assign work to someone
pages.body:
# Assign work to someone

Open the task, choose a name in **Assignee**, and select **Save**. The name shows in the bottom right corner of the card on the **Tasks** board, and the person gets a notification that the task is theirs.

## Put a name on a task

1. Open the menu and select **Agenda**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **Tasks** at the top left.
3. Select the card you want to hand over.
4. Select the **Assignee** box.
5. Choose the person, or choose **Unassigned** to take the name off.
6. Select **Save**.

**Assignee** offers the people who have a login to your workspace, and each task takes one name. To add someone to that list, see [Invite a coworker](../people-and-access/invite-a-coworker.md).

## Assignee on a task, People on an event

A task is work someone signs in to move across the board, so **Assignee** offers people with a login.

The **People** box on a calendar event offers everyone on file: **Members**, **Employees**, **Contractors**, **Service providers**, **Royalty owners** and **Gatherers**, plus **Whole org**. Put a hauler or a workover crew on the schedule that way. See [Add an event to the calendar](add-an-event-to-the-calendar.md).

## What happens next

The name saves when you select **Save**, and everyone in your workspace who can open Agenda sees it on the card.

The person you named gets a notification. Tell the people named on a calendar event yourself: the reminder the day before goes to whoever created the event.

To show only one person's cards, see [See only one person's work](see-only-one-persons-work.md).

pages.title: Create a task
pages.body:
# Create a task

Open the menu, select **Agenda**, then select **New Task**. Type a **Title**, select **Add Task**, and the card lands in the **Backlog** column of the **Tasks** board.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Agenda**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **New Task** at the top right.
3. Type what needs doing in **Title**. This is the only box you have to fill in.
4. Add detail in **Description**.
5. Choose an **Assignee**, or leave it on **Unassigned**. See [Assign work to someone](assign-work-to-someone.md).
6. Choose a **Priority**: **Low**, **Medium** or **High**. It starts on **Medium**.
7. Choose a **Status**: **Backlog**, **Queue**, **Doing** or **Done**. It starts on **Backlog**.
8. Set a **Deadline** if the work is due by a date.
9. Fill in **Budget** and **Spend** to track money on this job.
10. Select **Add Task**.

Selecting **Cancel**, or closing the window, throws away what you typed.

## A deadline also puts the task on the calendar

A task with a **Deadline** shows in two places: as a card on the **Tasks** board, and as an entry marked with a flag on **Month** and **Week**.

Set the date first. The time box under **Deadline** opens once a date is there, and clearing the date clears the time with it. A deadline with a date and no time sits at 5:00 pm, which reads as due by the end of that day.

Selecting the flagged entry on the calendar opens the same task, so you can edit it from either place.

Deleting that flagged entry deletes the whole task. See [Delete an event or task](delete-an-event-or-task.md).

## What happens next

The card appears on the board straight away, and everyone in your workspace with **Personal agenda** or **Org agenda** permission sees it. To change a task, select its card, make the change, and select **Save**.

Naming someone in **Assignee** sends them a notification that the task is theirs.

Tasks you create here belong to no project. Tasks created on a project show on this board too. See [Track work on a project](../projects/track-work-on-a-project.md).

To move it along, see [Move work across the task board](move-work-across-the-task-board.md).

pages.title: Delete an event or a task
pages.body:
# Delete an event or a task

Select the trash icon on the entry, then select **Delete** in the box that asks you to confirm. The entry goes for everyone in your workspace, and deleting cannot be undone.

## Delete a calendar event

1. Open the menu and select **Agenda**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Find the event on **Month** or **Week**.
3. Select the trash icon on the event.
4. Select **Delete**.

You can also open the event, select **Delete** at the bottom left, and select **Delete** again to confirm.

To keep the event, select **Cancel**.

## Delete a task

1. Open the menu and select **Agenda**.
2. Select **Tasks** at the top left.
3. Select the card to open it.
4. Select **Delete** at the bottom left.
5. Select **Delete** again to confirm.

On a computer, resting the pointer on a card puts a trash icon in its top right corner. Selecting that icon goes straight to the confirmation.

## Deleting a deadline off the calendar deletes the whole task

A task with a deadline shows on **Month** and **Week** as an entry marked with a flag. That entry is the task itself.

Selecting its trash icon removes the task: the card, the description, the assignee and everything else. The box that asks you to confirm says so: "This permanently removes the task, not just its deadline. This can't be undone."

To take the date off and keep the work, open the task, select the **Deadline** box, and select the highlighted day a second time. Then select **Save**. The entry leaves the calendar and the card stays on the board.

## What happens next

The entry goes straight away, for everyone with **Personal agenda** or **Org agenda** permission. There is no undo and nowhere to recover it from, so type a new one to bring it back.

To make a new one, see [Add an event to the calendar](add-an-event-to-the-calendar.md) or [Create a task](create-a-task.md).

pages.title: Move work across the task board
pages.body:
# Move work across the task board

Open the task, change **Status**, and select **Save**. On a computer you can drag the card into another column instead.

The board has four columns, left to right: **Backlog**, **Queue**, **Doing** and **Done**. The number beside each heading is how many cards are in it.

## Change the status

1. Open the menu and select **Agenda**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **Tasks** at the top left.
3. Select the card you want to move.
4. Select the **Status** box.
5. Choose **Backlog**, **Queue**, **Doing** or **Done**.
6. Select **Save**.

This works on a phone, a tablet and a computer.

## Drag the card instead

On a computer with a mouse, hold the mouse button down on a card, drag it over another column, and let go. The column lights up while the card is over it.

## What happens next

The card moves as soon as you drop it or save, and the count at the top of each column updates. Everyone in your workspace with **Personal agenda** or **Org agenda** permission sees it in its new column.

To put a card back, move it again. There is no undo.

Moving a task leaves its deadline alone, so a task with a deadline stays on **Month** and **Week** after it reaches **Done**.

To make a new card, see [Create a task](create-a-task.md).

pages.title: See only one person's work
pages.body:
# See only one person's work

Open the menu, select **Agenda**, then select **All people** at the top right. Untick everyone except the person you want, and the board shows only their cards.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Agenda**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **All people** at the top right.
3. Untick the names you do not want to see. Your own name is at the top of the list, as **Me**.
4. Select outside the list to close it.

The button then names who is left: one person's name, or a count such as **3 people**.

To get everyone back, open the same list and select **Show everyone**.

## The filter covers tasks

Unticking a name takes their cards off the **Tasks** board and their flagged deadlines off **Month** and **Week**, so both views show the same set of work.

Calendar events stay on screen whatever you untick. An event carries a list of people rather than one owner, so the filter leaves it alone. See [Add an event to the calendar](add-an-event-to-the-calendar.md).

**Unassigned** sits at the bottom of the list when a task has no name on it. Untick it to put the unclaimed pile out of the way.

The list offers everyone with a login, plus any other name written on a task.

## What happens next

The filter changes your own screen only. Nobody else's Agenda changes, and nothing is deleted.

It goes back to **All people** when the page reloads.

To put a name on a task in the first place, see [Assign work to someone](assign-work-to-someone.md).

pages.title: Switch between Month, Week and Tasks
pages.body:
# Switch between Month, Week and Tasks

Select **Month**, **Week** or **Tasks** in the toggle at the top left of **Agenda**. **Month** opens first, unless you arrived from an alert about a task, which opens **Tasks**.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Agenda**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select **Month**, **Week** or **Tasks** at the top left.

## Which one to use

**Month** shows the whole month, up to three entries in a day. A busier day ends with a count of the rest, such as **+2 more**. Open **Week** to see those.

**Week** shows seven days, Sunday to Saturday, hour by hour, with a red line across today's column at the current time. It opens at 6:00 am, and you scroll up or down for the rest of the day. All-day events sit in a band above the hours.

**Tasks** shows the **Backlog**, **Queue**, **Doing** and **Done** columns, and every task whatever its deadline. See [Move work across the task board](move-work-across-the-task-board.md).

## Move to another month or week

Use the arrows either side of the date at the top. In **Month** they move a month at a time, in **Week** a week at a time. **Tasks** has no arrows.

**Month** lands you on the 1st of the month you move to. Switching to **Week** then opens the week holding that 1st, so read the dates across the top of the columns.

To get back to today, reload the page.

## What happens next

Switching views changes your own screen only, and leaves the events and tasks themselves alone.

Reloading the page brings the calendar back to today.

pages.title: Add or remove people from a group chat
pages.body:
# Add or remove people from a group chat

Open the group chat and select the people icon at the top right, the one with a number beside it. Everyone already in the chat is listed first and everyone else in your workspace below, and you add or remove them from that one list.

Any member of the group can do this. You do not have to be the person who started it.

## Add someone

1. Open the menu, select **Messages**, and open the group chat.
2. Select the people icon at the top right. The number beside it is how many people are in the chat, including you.
3. Find the person in the lower part of the list, under the dividing line. Type in **Search people…** if the list is long.
4. Select their row.

They join immediately and the chat appears in their **Messages** list. They can read everything already said in the chat, including messages sent before they were added. Anyone else looking at the chat sees the count go up without reloading.

To finish, select **Done**.

## Remove someone

1. Open the group chat and select the people icon at the top right.
2. Find the person in the upper part of the list, above the dividing line.
3. Select the **x** at the end of their row.

They are removed immediately and the chat disappears from their **Messages** list. They stop getting alerts from it. Nobody is told when a person is added or removed.

Add them back to undo it. They can then read what was said while they were gone.

## Taking yourself out

Ask someone else in the group to remove you. Your own row shows **You** and has no **x**.

## Direct messages

A one-to-one conversation has no people icon, and its membership stays as it is. To talk to a third person, start a group instead. See [Start a group chat](start-a-group-chat.md).

pages.title: Leave a comment on a well or lease
pages.body:
# Leave a comment on a well or lease

Open the well or lease, select the **Comments** tab, type in the box that reads **Add a comment**, and press Enter. The comment appears at the top of the thread and your coworkers see it without reloading.

Tanks, meters, batteries and saltwater disposal wells have the same **Comments** tab and it works the same way.

## Post a comment

1. Open the well or lease. Wells are under **Production** in the menu, leases under **Leases**.
2. Select **Comments** in the row of tabs.
3. Type in the box beside your picture, where it reads **Add a comment**.
4. Press Enter to post. To start a new line inside the same comment, hold Shift and press Enter. You can also select the round send button at the right of the box.

Your comment appears at the top of the list with your name and how long ago you wrote it.

Everyone who can see that well or lease gets an alert about it. On a well that is everyone with access to production, and on a lease it is everyone with access to leases. See [Choose which notifications you get](../your-account/choose-which-notifications-you-get.md).

To send it to one person in particular, name them in the comment. See [Mention a coworker so they get notified](mention-a-coworker-so-they-get-notified.md).

## Reply to a comment

1. Select **Reply** under the comment you are answering.
2. A box opens underneath with **@** and their name already typed in it. Leave that in place so they are notified.
3. Type your reply and press Enter.

Replies sit indented under the comment they answer. Answering a reply puts your answer beside it at the same depth rather than stepping further in, so a long back and forth never runs off the side of a phone screen.

A reply alerts the person you answered and nobody else.

To close the reply box without posting, press Esc or select **Reply** again.

## Like a comment

Select **Like** under it. The number beside the word goes up and the person who wrote it is alerted. Select **Like** again to take it back. They are alerted the first time only, so taking a like back leaves the first alert standing and liking again does not send a second one.

## Delete your own comment

Delete a comment from a computer:

1. Move the pointer over your comment. A small trash icon appears at the right of it.
2. Select the trash icon.

The comment is replaced with the words **Comment deleted** rather than disappearing, so any replies underneath still make sense. This cannot be undone, and the text is gone for everyone.

You can only delete comments you wrote. Nobody can delete yours, whatever their role.

## Comments and notes are different tabs

A note is a document you write and keep on the facility. A comment is a conversation. They have separate tabs, and posting in one does not put anything in the other.

pages.title: Mention a coworker so they get notified
pages.body:
# Mention a coworker so they get notified

In a comment box on a well, lease, tank, meter or battery, type **@** and start typing the person's name, then select them from the list that appears. They get an alert reading, for example, **Jane Doe mentioned you on Smith Lease**.

Use this when a comment needs one particular person to see it rather than whoever happens to look at the well.

## Name someone in a comment

1. Open the well or lease. Wells are under **Production** in the menu, leases under **Leases**.
2. Select **Comments** in the row of tabs.
3. Start typing your comment.
4. Type **@**. A short list of your coworkers appears above the box.
5. Keep typing to narrow the list, then select the person. You can also move through the list with the up and down arrow keys and press Enter to pick one, or press Esc to close the list.
6. Finish your comment and press Enter to post.

Their name shows in blue in the posted comment.

The alert takes them straight to the well or lease when they select it. It goes to their bell and their email. See [Choose which notifications you get](../your-account/choose-which-notifications-you-get.md).

## Pick the name from the list

A typed name reaches someone only when it matches their full name in WildcatIQ. **@Jane Doe** reaches Jane Doe, and **@Jane** does not. The list puts the full name in for you, so use it whenever you can.

## Who can be mentioned

Everyone currently in your workspace appears in the list. Somebody who was invited but has not signed in yet, and somebody who has been removed, are not in it.

A mention reaches people who can already open that page. On a lease, that means people with access to leases.

If two people in your workspace have the same name, both are alerted.

## Mentioning in a reply

When you select **Reply** under a comment, the reply box opens with the other person's name already in it. Leave it there. They are alerted once, as a mention.

## Once a comment is posted

Who was alerted is settled at the moment you post. There is no way to edit a comment, and deleting it afterwards leaves the alert standing. If you named the wrong person, post a new comment naming the right one.

## Mentions in Messages

Typing **@** and a name in **Messages** highlights the name in the sent message. Everyone in a conversation is already alerted about every message in it, so the highlight is there to catch the reader's eye. There is no name picker in the message box. See [Send a message to a coworker](send-a-message-to-a-coworker.md).

pages.title: Send a file in a message
pages.body:
# Send a file in a message

Open the conversation in **Messages**, select the paperclip beside the send button, choose the file, then send. You can send a file on its own, with no text.

## Attach and send

1. Open the menu, select **Messages**, and open the conversation.
2. Select the paperclip at the right of the message box, beside the send button.
3. Choose one or more files from your computer or phone. On a computer, hold Ctrl (or Command on a Mac) to pick several at once.
4. Each file appears as a chip above the message box, with its name on it. To take one back off, select the **x** on its chip.
5. To add more, select the paperclip again. The new files are added to the ones already there.
6. Type a message if you want one, then press Enter or select the blue send button.

The files upload and the message posts. Your files appear above your message bubble as chips with a paperclip and the file name.

Everyone in the conversation can open them. Nobody outside it can, and the files do not appear in **Files** or on any well or lease page.

## Open a file someone sent you

Select the chip with the file name on it. The file opens in a new browser tab, where you can save or print it.

File links last an hour. Open the conversation again for a fresh one.

## Editing and deleting

A sent message and its files stay as sent. There is no way to edit or delete them, so check the chips above the box before you send.

Next: [Leave a comment on a well or lease](leave-a-comment-on-a-well-or-lease.md).

pages.title: Send a message to a coworker
pages.body:
# Send a message to a coworker

Open the menu, select **Messages**, then select the **+** button at the top of the conversation list. Pick the person and select **Start chat**, then type in the box at the bottom and press Enter.

Everyone in your workspace can be messaged. There is no permission to turn on first.

## Start the conversation

1. Open the menu and select **Messages**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the **+** button at the right of the word **Messages**, at the top of the conversation list. If you have no conversations yet, select **New message** in the middle of the screen instead.
3. Type a few letters of the person's name in **Search people…**, or scroll the list.
4. Select their name. A check mark appears beside it and their name appears as a chip above the list.
5. Select **Start chat**.

The conversation opens straight away. Nobody is notified yet, because nothing has been said.

If you already have a conversation with that person, WildcatIQ opens the existing one rather than starting a second. One person, one thread.

## Send the message

1. Type in the box at the bottom that reads **Message** followed by their name.
2. Press Enter to send. To start a new line inside the same message, hold Shift and press Enter.

Your message appears on the right in blue. Theirs appear on the left with their name and picture. The time sits under the last message of a run.

The other person gets an alert on the bell in WildcatIQ, and on their phone if they have the app. Messages do not send email unless the person turns that on for themselves. See [Choose which notifications you get](../your-account/choose-which-notifications-you-get.md).

Only the people in the conversation can read it. Nobody else in the workspace can, not even an administrator.

## Editing, deleting and older messages

Once a message is sent it stays sent. There is no way to edit it and no way to delete it.

A conversation shows its most recent 200 messages.

Next: [Start a group chat](start-a-group-chat.md).

pages.title: Start a group chat
pages.body:
# Start a group chat

Open the menu and select **Messages**, then select the **+** button at the top of the conversation list. Pick two or more people and select **Start group**. Picking a second person is what makes it a group. One person is a direct message.

## Start it

1. Open the menu and select **Messages**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Select the **+** button at the right of the word **Messages**.
3. Type a name in **Search people…** and select each person you want. Each one you pick appears as a chip above the list.
4. To take someone back out, select the **x** on their chip.
5. Once you have picked a second person, a **Group name (optional)** box appears. Type a name for the chat, or leave it blank.
6. Select **Start group**. The button counts the people you picked, so picking three shows **Start group (3)**. You are in the chat as well.

The chat opens and everyone you picked is in it immediately. They are not notified until the first message is sent.

## If you leave the name blank

The chat is titled with everyone else's first names, like **Dana, Ray, Wes**. Each person sees the other members' names, not their own.

Name it later from a computer:

1. Open the group chat.
2. Move the pointer over the title at the top. A pencil appears beside it.
3. Select the pencil, type the name, and press Enter. Pressing Esc leaves the name as it was.
4. To go back to the list of first names, delete everything in the box and press Enter.

Everyone in the chat sees the new name. Any member can rename a group, not only the person who started it.

A direct message with one person is always titled with the other person's name.

## Two groups with the same people

Starting a group with people you already have a group with creates a second, separate group chat. That is on purpose, so a crew can run more than one conversation. Name each one so you can tell them apart.

## Leaving and deleting

A group chat has no delete, and you cannot take yourself out of one. To get out of a group, ask someone else in the chat to remove you. See [Add or remove people from a group chat](add-or-remove-people-from-a-group-chat.md).

Next: [Send a file in a message](send-a-file-in-a-message.md).

pages.title: Accept an invitation
pages.body:
# Accept an invitation

Open the email with the subject **You've been invited to Wildcat** and select **Accept invite**. Fill in your name, phone and a password, then select **Join team**.

The link is good for 7 days from the moment it was sent. There is nothing to install and nothing to pay.

## Join the workspace

1. Open the invitation email. If it is not in your inbox, check your spam folder.
2. Select **Accept invite**. If the button does not work, copy the link printed under it into your browser.
3. The page reads **Join your team**. Your address is already filled into **Email** and cannot be changed. The invitation is tied to that address.
4. Type your first name in **First name**.
5. Type your last name in **Last name**.
6. Type your mobile number in **Phone**. This one is optional.
7. Type a password in **Password**. Use at least 6 characters. Select the eye icon to see what you typed.
8. Select **Join team**.

You are signed in and land in the workspace. There is no email to confirm and no company setup to work through, because your employer has already done it.

Sign in from then on with the same email address and the password you just set.

## If you already use WildcatIQ

If that address already has a WildcatIQ account, the page says "This workspace is being added to the account you already have" and asks for nothing but the **Join team** button. Your password, your name and any other workspace you belong to are untouched.

After joining, you land on a screen listing your workspaces. Pick the one you want. Later you switch between them from the account menu behind your photo in the top right corner. See [Switch between workspaces](../getting-started/switch-between-workspaces.md).

## What you can see

Your admin chose which parts of WildcatIQ you can open, so your menu may be shorter than a coworker's. If something you need is missing, ask them to grant it. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).

## If the link does not work

The page shows **Invite unavailable** and one of these:

- "This invite link is invalid or has already been used." Someone has already joined with it, or the invite was cancelled.
- "This invite has already been accepted. Try signing in instead." Go to the sign-in page and use your email and password.
- "This invite has expired. Ask your admin to send a new one." Links last 7 days.

For the first and last, ask whoever invited you to send another. The new link replaces the old one, so use the newest email.

pages.title: Add a royalty owner
pages.body:
# Add a royalty owner

Open the menu and select **People**, under **Admin**. Select the **Person** button at the top right, choose **Owner**, fill in the form and select **Add Owner**.

Adding the owner records who they are. What they own is set separately, on the lease.

You need **Manage people** to add an owner. Ask an admin to switch the **People** area on for you.

## Add the owner

1. Open the menu and select **People**.
2. Select **Person** at the top right.
3. Select **Owner**. The form opens, titled **Add Owner**.
4. Type their name in **Name**. This is the only field you have to fill in. Use the name that goes on the check.
5. Fill in **Phone** and **Email**.
6. Type where their checks and statements go in **Mailing Address**.
7. Add anything else worth knowing in **Description**, such as who to call about a bad address.
8. Select **Add Owner**.

The screen switches to the **Owners** tab and the new row appears. Everyone who can open **People** sees it.

## Give them an interest

An owner added here holds nothing until you grant it. Interest belongs to a lease, and one owner can hold different interest in several, which is why the owner form has no place to enter a decimal or a well.

1. Open the lease in **Leases**.
2. Go to its **Interest** tab.
3. Add the owner and their interest there.

## Check what they hold

Select the owner's row in **People**. The **Edit Person** window opens wider than the others, with a **Leases** panel on the right listing every lease they hold an interest in, the interest type, how many wells, and the percentage.

That panel is read-only. Change interest on the lease, not here. Before any interest is granted it reads "No interest yet. Grant one from a lease's Interest tab."

The **Leases** column in the table is the short version of the same thing: how many leases they hold an interest in.

## Change or delete an owner

Select the row, edit the details, then select **Save**.

**Last Payment** in the table is not on the form. Use the lease and the revenue screens for what has actually been paid.

To delete, select the trash icon in the **Actions** column, then select **Delete** in the confirmation. That is permanent and cannot be undone, and it also removes the interest they held on every lease. The leases themselves are untouched.

pages.title: Add a vendor or purchaser
pages.body:
# Add a vendor or purchaser

Open the menu and select **People**, under **Admin**. Select the **Person** button at the top right, choose **Vendor** or **Purchaser**, fill in the form and select the button at the bottom of it.

A vendor is a company you buy services from. A purchaser is the company that hauls and buys your oil, which you pick on a tank when you call in a load.

You need **Manage people** to add either one. Ask an admin to switch the **People** area on for you.

## Add a vendor

1. Open the menu and select **People**.
2. Select **Person** at the top right.
3. Select **Vendor**. The form opens, titled **Add Vendor**.
4. Type the business name in **Company**. This is the only field you have to fill in.
5. Type what they do in **Service**, such as Trucking or Wireline. This is what the list groups them by, so keep the wording the same across vendors that do the same work.
6. Type the person you deal with in **Contact**.
7. Fill in **Phone** and **Email**.
8. Leave **Status** on **Active**, or select **Inactive**.
9. Add anything else worth knowing in **Description**.
10. Select **Add Vendor**.

The **Vendors** tab lists them under a heading for each **Service**, with the companies alphabetical inside each group. A vendor with no service typed sits in a group of its own.

## Add a purchaser

1. Open the menu and select **People**.
2. Select **Person** at the top right.
3. Select **Purchaser**. The form opens, titled **Add Purchaser**.
4. Type the company name in **Name**. This is the only field you have to fill in.
5. Fill in **Phone** and **Email**. Use the number your pumper actually calls to order a load.
6. Leave **Status** on **Active**, or select **Inactive**.
7. Add anything else worth knowing in **Description**.
8. Select **Add Purchaser**.

## What happens next

The new company is available immediately. On a tank's settings you pick one from the same list, under a field labelled **Gatherer**, and that is who a called-in load goes to. Everyone who can open **People** sees the record.

**Service** and **Description** are not columns in the vendor table. To see them, select the row.

## Change or delete one

Select any row to open **Edit Person**, change what you need, then select **Save**. Renaming a vendor's **Service** moves it into that group in the list.

To delete, select the trash icon in the **Actions** column, then select **Delete** in the confirmation. That is permanent and cannot be undone. For a purchaser you no longer use, set **Status** to **Inactive** instead, so the loads already recorded against them still make sense. The **Actions** column appears only for people who can manage people.

pages.title: Add an employee or contractor
pages.body:
# Add an employee or contractor

Open the menu and select **People**, under **Admin**. Select the **Person** button at the top right, choose **Employee** or **Contractor**, fill in the form and select the button at the bottom of it.

The new person appears in the list straight away. Everyone in your workspace who can open **People** sees them.

You need **Manage people** to add anyone. Ask an admin to switch the **People** area on for you. See [Set what a coworker can see](set-what-a-coworker-can-see.md).

## Which one to use

- **Employee**: someone on your payroll. Carries a salary and a payment schedule.
- **Contractor**: an individual you call out, such as a pumper or a roustabout. Contractors are people you work with who have no WildcatIQ login.

For a company you buy services from, use a vendor instead. See [Add a vendor or purchaser](add-a-vendor-or-purchaser.md).

## Add an employee

1. Open the menu and select **People**.
2. Select **Person** at the top right.
3. Select **Employee**. The form opens, titled **Add Employee**.
4. Type their name in **Name**. This is the only field you have to fill in.
5. Type their job in **Role**, such as Pumper or Bookkeeper.
6. Type their pay in **Salary (USD)**. Numbers only, no dollar sign.
7. Type how often they are paid in **Payment Schedule**, such as Monthly.
8. Fill in **Email** and **Phone**.
9. Leave **Status** on **Active**, or select **Inactive** for someone who has left.
10. Add anything else worth knowing in **Description**.
11. Select **Add Employee**.

## Add a contractor

1. Open the menu and select **People**.
2. Select **Person** at the top right.
3. Select **Contractor**. The form opens, titled **Add Contractor**.
4. Type their name in **Name**. This is the only field you have to fill in.
5. Type who they work for in **Company**, if anyone.
6. Type what they do in **Trade**, such as Pumping or Hot Oil.
7. Fill in **Phone** and **Email**.
8. Leave **Status** on **Active**, or select **Inactive**.
9. Add anything else worth knowing in **Description**.
10. Select **Add Contractor**.

## What happens next

The screen switches to the tab you added to and the new row appears at the top, then settles into alphabetical order.

A contractor becomes available on the Agenda right away, in the people picker on a calendar event, listed under **Contractors**. Tasks work differently: they can only be assigned to coworkers who sign in, so a contractor never appears in that list. To give someone tasks, invite them instead. See [Invite a coworker](invite-a-coworker.md).

**Salary**, **Payment Schedule** and **Description** are not columns in the table. To see them, select the row.

## Change or delete someone

Select any row to open **Edit Person**, change what you need, then select **Save**. **Person Type** is shown but cannot be changed. To move someone between employee and contractor, add them under the right type and delete the old record.

To delete, select the trash icon in the **Actions** column, then select **Delete** in the confirmation. That one is permanent and cannot be undone, so mark someone **Inactive** instead if you may want their history later. The **Actions** column appears only for people who can manage people.

pages.title: Invite a coworker
pages.body:
# Invite a coworker

Open **Settings**, select **Organization**, then select **Add member**. Type their name and email, grant at least one permission, and select **Invite**. WildcatIQ emails them the invite link straight away.

Only an admin sees the **Organization** tab. If your Settings screen shows just **Profile**, **Referral**, **Notifications** and **AI**, ask an admin to send the invite.

## Send the invite

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Organization** at the top of the page.
4. Select **Add member**.
5. Type their name in **Name**.
6. Type their work email in **Email**. This is the address the invite goes to, and the address they sign in with.
7. Select **Set permissions** and switch on what they should be able to do. See [Set what a coworker can see](set-what-a-coworker-can-see.md).
8. Select **Done** to close the permissions list.
9. Select **Invite**.

**Invite** turns on once you have typed an email address and granted at least one permission. Until then the line under the button reads "Grant at least one capability before inviting."

## What happens next

The invite email goes out the moment you select **Invite**. It is sent to the address you typed, with the subject **You've been invited to Wildcat** and a button reading **Accept invite**. The link is good for 7 days.

A line above the table with a green check reads "Invite sent to" and their address, and a new row appears with a **Pending** chip in the **Status** column.

The link is only ever in that email, so the invite has to reach the address you typed.

Nobody else in the workspace is notified. Other admins see the new row the next time they open Settings.

## If the email does not arrive

1. Ask them to check their spam folder first.
2. In the **Manage** column of their row, select the circular arrow icon (**Resend invite**).

A resend sends a brand new link and retires the old one, so tell them to use the newest email.

## Cancel an invite you should not have sent

In the **Manage** column of their **Pending** row, select the X icon (**Cancel invite**). The row goes and the emailed link stops working. There is no confirmation step, and the way back is to invite them again.

Once someone has accepted, the X is replaced by a trash icon. See [Remove a coworker](remove-a-coworker.md).

## If they already use WildcatIQ

Someone who already has a WildcatIQ account under that email is not asked to make a new one. Accepting adds your workspace to the account they have, and they pick between workspaces from the account menu. Their password, their name and their other workspaces are untouched.

Next: [Set what a coworker can see](set-what-a-coworker-can-see.md).

pages.title: Remove a coworker
pages.body:
# Remove a coworker

Open **Settings**, select **Organization**, then select the trash icon in that person's **Manage** column and confirm. They lose access immediately, and nothing they entered is deleted.

Removal can be undone. Removed people are listed under **Removed members** below the table, and one button puts them back.

## Remove them

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Organization** at the top of the page.
4. Find the person in the **Members** table.
5. Select the trash icon in their **Manage** column.
6. Read the confirmation. It is titled **Remove this member?**, with **Nothing is deleted.** underneath.
7. Select the button reading **Remove** and their name.

Select **Cancel** if you opened it by mistake. Nothing changes until you select the confirm button.

## What happens next

The next page they open shows a screen reading **Your access was removed** instead of the app. It tells them nothing was deleted and to ask an admin if it was a mistake.

Kept exactly as it was:

- their row, now listed under **Removed members**
- the permissions they held, so restoring them does not mean rebuilding a role
- every reading, note, file, ticket and record they entered

Only admins see any of this. Nobody else in the workspace is notified, and no email is sent to the person you removed.

If they belong to more than one WildcatIQ workspace, they keep the others. They only lose this one.

## The owner cannot be removed

The trash icon on the owner's row is greyed out and reads "The owner can't be removed". The owner's access comes from owning the workspace rather than from a membership row, so it is not switched off here. To hand the business over, contact support.

## They never accepted the invite

A row with a **Pending** chip has an X icon instead of a trash icon. Select it to cancel the invite. That one works differently: the row goes, the emailed link stops working, and the way back is to invite them again.

## Changed your mind

See [Restore someone you removed](restore-someone-you-removed.md).

pages.title: Restore someone you removed
pages.body:
# Restore someone you removed

Open **Settings**, select **Organization**, then select **Removed members** below the **Members** table. Find the person and select **Restore**.

They come back with the permissions they had before. Nothing was lost while they were out.

## Put them back

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Organization** at the top of the page.
4. Below the members table, select **Removed members**. The number beside it is how many people are in there.
5. Find the person. Each line shows their name, their email, and the date they were removed.
6. Select **Restore** at the right of their line.

Their row moves back into the **Members** table straight away, with the permissions they held before.

## What they need to do

Ask them to sign out and sign in again. That is what the **Your access was removed** screen tells them too.

If they never accepted the original invite, they go back to **Pending** and their original invite link still works. If it has expired, select the circular arrow icon in their **Manage** column to send a fresh one.

## If nobody is listed

The section reads "Nobody has been removed. When you remove someone they land here, and you can put them back." It is always shown, even when empty, so you can see before you act that removal can be undone.

## Someone you removed a long time ago

They stay in this list indefinitely. There is no time limit on restoring them.

You can also invite that address again from **Add member**. That reuses the same record and the same history, and sends them a fresh invite email. See [Invite a coworker](invite-a-coworker.md).

pages.title: Set what a coworker can see
pages.body:
# Set what a coworker can see

Open **Settings**, select **Organization**, then select the button in that person's **Permissions** column and switch areas on or off. Each switch saves the moment you flip it, so there is nothing to save at the end.

Only an admin can open the **Organization** tab and change permissions.

## Change someone's permissions

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Organization** at the top of the page.
4. Find the person in the **Members** table.
5. Select the button in their **Permissions** column. It is labelled with what they have now: **No access**, **Admin**, **Full access**, or a count such as "6 permissions".
6. Under **Access by area**, switch on each area they need.
7. Select **Done**.

The button label updates to the new summary. Their access changes the next time they load a page in WildcatIQ. They are not notified.

## The areas

| Area | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| **Skills** | Configure Orion skills. |
| **Files** | Open, upload, and manage files. |
| **Notes** | Create, tag, and manage notes. |
| **Wells** | Production, allocation, equipment, service, and creating wells. |
| **Disposal** | Saltwater disposal tanks, wells, and injection readings. |
| **Facilities** | The cross-substance flow map. |
| **Leases** | Leases, their assets, and owner interest. |
| **People** | Contractors, service providers, and royalty owners. |
| **Revenue** | Revenue and settlement statements. |
| **Invoices** | Vendor invoices, field tickets, and job cost. |
| **Projects** | View and manage projects. |
| **Inventory** | View and manage inventory. |
| **Agenda** | Tasks and calendar, personal and org-wide. |
| **AI** | Chat with Orion and scan documents. |
| **Reports** | The report hub. |
| **Analytics** | Analytics dashboards. |
| **Pricing** | Posted prices and projections. |

Switching an area on grants everything inside it. A pumper who should record readings but never see money gets **Wells**, **Disposal** and **AI**, and nothing under **Revenue** or **Invoices**.

**Messages** is not in the list. Everyone in the workspace can send and read their own messages.

## Give someone full access

Switch on **Admin** at the top of the list. That grants every permission below it, including inviting and removing members and opening billing. Every area switch locks on while **Admin** is on, because they already have all of it.

Switch **Admin** back off to return them to the areas you pick by hand.

## Split an area finer

1. Open the permissions list for that person.
2. Select **Advanced** to expand it.
3. Switch individual permissions on or off.

An area with only some of its permissions on shows a **Partial** chip beside its name.

Some switches are locked on purpose:

- A switch is locked **on** when another permission already grants it. **Notes** grants **View notes**, so **View notes** stays on while **Notes** is on.
- A switch is locked **off** until the permissions it needs are on. **View reports** needs **View well production** and **View revenue**, because a single report can carry both. **Reports** stays off in the area list until those two are granted.

## The owner

The **Permissions** column for the owner reads **Full access** with a shield, and there is no button to open. The owner has everything and cannot be edited here. That is also why the owner cannot be removed.

To take access away, see [Stop a coworker from seeing something](stop-a-coworker-from-seeing-something.md).

pages.title: Stop a coworker from seeing something
pages.body:
# Stop a coworker from seeing something

Open **Settings**, select **Organization**, then select the button in that person's **Permissions** column and switch the area off. The switch saves the instant you flip it, and they lose that screen the next time they load a page in WildcatIQ.

If you need them out of everything at once, remove them instead. Removal takes hold immediately, deletes nothing, and can be undone. See [Remove a coworker](remove-a-coworker.md).

Only an admin can open the **Organization** tab. If Settings shows you just **Profile**, **Referral**, **Notifications** and **AI**, ask whoever runs your workspace to do this for you.

## Take one area away

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Organization** at the top of the page.
4. Find the person in the **Members** table.
5. Select the button in their **Permissions** column.
6. Under **Access by area**, switch off the area you want to close.
7. Select **Done**.

The button in their row updates to the new summary. They are not notified, and no email goes out.

The money sits in three areas. **Revenue** covers revenue and settlement statements, **Invoices** covers vendor invoices, field tickets and job cost, and **Leases** covers leases, their assets, and owner interest. Switching **Revenue** off takes **Reports** with it, because a single report can carry revenue.

If **Admin** is switched on at the top of the list, that person has everything and every area switch below is locked on. Switch **Admin** off first, then switch on only the areas they keep.

## What they see afterwards

The link leaves their sidebar, and typing the address or opening an old bookmark gives them a page not found. Anything already on their screen stays there until they move to another page or refresh.

Orion uses that person's permissions, so it does not read an area you have switched off.

## Cut off everything at once

1. In their row, select the trash icon in the **Manage** column.
2. Read the confirmation. It is titled **Remove this member?** and says **Nothing is deleted.**
3. Select the button reading **Remove** and their name.

They lose access immediately, and the next page they open shows a screen reading **Your access was removed** instead of the app. Their record, their permissions and everything they entered all stay. Put them back at any time from **Removed members**, just below the table. See [Restore someone you removed](restore-someone-you-removed.md).

The workspace owner is the one exception. The trash icon on that row is greyed out and reads "The owner can't be removed".

## They have not accepted their invite yet

If their **Status** says **Pending**, they have never been in. Select the X icon in the **Manage** column to cancel the invite. The row goes and the emailed link stops working.

## Areas, not individual wells or files

Permissions work by area. Someone with **Wells** switched on sees every well in the workspace, and someone with **Files** switched on sees every file. To close one thing to one person, switch off the area it lives in, or remove them.

For every area and what it covers, see [Set what a coworker can see](set-what-a-coworker-can-see.md).

pages.title: Draw an area to search
pages.body:
# Draw an area to search

Use the three buttons stacked on the right edge of the map: **Box**, **Lasso** and **Ring**. Draw a shape and the map redraws to what is inside it. Drawing needs a mouse or a trackpad, because every shape is made by dragging.

Point at a button to see its name. The three buttons are there in all three modes.

## Draw a box

1. Select **Box** on the right edge of the map. The pointer becomes a crosshair.
2. Press and drag from one corner of the area to the opposite corner. A dashed outline follows the pointer.
3. Release. The outline turns solid and the map redraws to what is inside.

The tool switches itself off after one box, so the next drag moves the map again. A shape needs a real drag of at least a few pixels. Click without moving and the tool stays armed, ready for the next try.

## Draw a freehand shape

1. Select **Lasso**.
2. Press and drag around the area you want, as if drawing with a pencil.
3. Release to close the shape.

Recon smooths the line you drew, so the finished shape has fewer corners than your hand made. The tool switches itself off afterwards.

## Draw a ring around a well

The ring tool works two ways.

**A ring of a set radius, around wells you pick:**

1. Select **Ring**.
2. In the **Area** box at the bottom left, select a radius: **1 mi**, **2 mi**, **5 mi** or **10 mi**. It starts at 5 mi.
3. Select a well on the map. A ring of that radius appears around it.
4. Select more wells to add more rings. The tool stays armed, so keep clicking.
5. Select **Ring** again to put the tool away.

While **Ring** is armed, selecting a well makes a ring instead of opening the well's record. Put the tool away first if you want the record.

**A ring you size by hand:**

1. Select **Ring**.
2. Press on the centre point and drag outward. The ring grows as you drag, and the distance you drag is the radius.
3. Release.

Starting the drag on a well centres the ring exactly on that well rather than where you pressed. This way switches the tool off after one ring.

## See and edit what you have drawn

The **Area** box at the bottom left lists every shape: `Box · 4 corners`, `Shape · 12 points`, `Ring · 5 mi`. In Wells mode it also gives how many wells the shapes hold.

- To move a corner, drag one of the white handles on a box or freehand shape. The map redraws when you let go. Rings have no handles, because a ring is a centre and a radius.
- To remove one shape, select the **×** on its row.
- To remove all of them, select **Clear all**.

## How several shapes combine

Anything inside any one of your shapes is included. Shapes that overlap do not double-count wells.

## What an area means in each mode

A drawn area stays on the map when you switch mode, so you can draw once and ask the same place two questions. What it selects changes:

- **Wells**: the wells whose location falls inside the shape.
- **Permits**: the permits whose surface location falls inside the shape.
- **Operators**: operators whose **mailing address** falls inside the shape. Operator dots sit at a mailing address, so this picks companies based there. To find companies working in a place, use **Works in** instead. See [Switch between wells, permits and operators](switch-between-wells-permits-and-operators.md).

Nothing you draw is saved. It is gone when you reload the page, and nobody else sees it.

## Next

- [Narrow your search](narrow-your-search.md)
- [Switch between wells, permits and operators](switch-between-wells-permits-and-operators.md)

pages.title: Export a list of operators
pages.body:
# Export a list of operators

In Recon, set **Show** to **Operators**, select a numbered bubble on the map, and select **CSV** in the panel that opens. The file downloads to your device with one row per operator, including mailing address, phone and P-5 status.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Recon**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Set **Show** to **Operators**. See [Switch between wells, permits and operators](switch-between-wells-permits-and-operators.md).
3. Select a numbered violet bubble. A panel opens on the right, headed **Operators near Midland, TX** or similar, with the count underneath.
4. To keep only companies at a particular P-5 standing, change **Any activity** to the one you want, such as **Active** or **Delinquent**.
5. Check the count under the heading. That is what will be exported.
6. Select **CSV**.

The button reads **Exporting…** while it works, then the file downloads. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing in your workspace changes.

Selecting a single dot rather than a bubble opens that one operator's record instead. See [Look up an operator](look-up-an-operator.md). Export runs from the bubble's panel.

## What is in the file

One row per operator, in the order the panel shows them:

Operator number, Operator name, P-5 status, Last P-5 date, Phone, Address 1, Address 2, City, State, ZIP, Oil gatherer, Gas gatherer, Wells (total), Wells (active), Oil (bbl/mo), Gas (MCF/mo).

The file is named after the panel heading, such as `operators-near-midland-tx.csv`. When **Exclude plugged wells** is ticked under the gear button, `-active-only` is added to the name.

## What gets exported and what does not

- **Only the rows the panel is showing.** If **Any activity** is set to one standing, only those companies are in the file. The count under the heading reads **7 of 32** when that is happening.
- **Only the operators in the bubble you selected.** This is the bubble's list, not a statewide one and not everything matching your other filters.
- Address, phone and P-5 fields are fetched when you select **CSV**, so a large list takes a few seconds.

Every field comes from the Texas Railroad Commission's P-5 organisation reports. Oil and gas per month are the operator's own reported production over its last twelve filed months, divided by the months it actually filed. They are blank or zero for a company that has reported nothing.

## If something looks wrong

- **No numbered bubbles, only single dots.** You are zoomed in past the point where operators group together. Zoom out and the bubbles come back.
- **CSV is greyed out.** The list is empty. Set the filter back to **Any activity** to bring the rows back.
- **The file opens with odd characters in a spreadsheet.** Open it through your spreadsheet program's import option and choose UTF-8.

Related: [Find the people behind an operator](find-the-people-behind-an-operator.md).

pages.title: Find new drilling permits
pages.body:
# Find new drilling permits

In Recon, set **Show** to **Permits**. Every drilling permit the Texas Railroad Commission is currently sitting on is drawn in amber across the whole state, and selecting one opens its detail.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Recon**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Set **Show** to **Permits**. See [Switch between wells, permits and operators](switch-between-wells-permits-and-operators.md).
3. Read **Queue** in the filter bar. It says how many applications are pending statewide.
4. To narrow by what the operator filed for, select the purpose button, which reads **All purposes** until you change it, and tick the ones you want. Select **Show all purposes** to go back.
5. Select a dot. Its detail opens on the right.

A numbered bubble is a group of permits. Select it and the map zooms in.

## What the three colours mean

The key sits in the bottom left corner and counts what is on screen:

- **Pending**: filed and not yet acted on. Drawn amber, always shown, statewide. A permit filed for a horizontal well is drawn a darker amber.
- **Approved**: granted and not drilled.
- **Drilled**: granted, and the state's record shows the hole exists.

## Reading a permit

The badge at the top of the panel says where the permit stands:

- **12 days pending** counts from the day it was filed. Approved permits usually issue within one to eight days, so an application sitting much longer is in a hearing, in a mapping correction, or has been refused. The Commission publishes arrivals and does not announce refusals, so the badge reports the wait rather than the reason.
- **issued 5 days ago** counts from the day it was granted. That clock is not a wait.
- **drilled · issued 5 days ago** means the permit became a hole.

**API** is a link on a drilled permit, because that is the one with a wellbore behind it. On a pending application the API is a number the Commission assigned while working the paperwork, and about six in ten pending applications read **not yet assigned**. On a drilled permit, **Well** and **Production** show the hole's own name and what it has made.

**Position** says how the pin was placed. **RRC GIS** is the Commission's own mapping. **operator-reported** is the location the operator wrote on the form.

## What the map covers

The pending queue is complete for the whole state, and it is the reason to be on this screen. Two things about the other two colours are worth knowing:

- **Approved and drilled permits go back only so far.** They can be drawn only if they passed through the pending queue while WildcatIQ was watching it, because the Commission's approved records carry no coordinates. Anything granted before that window is not on this map.
- **Approved and drilled permits load for the part of the map you are looking at**, and refresh as you move. Pending ones are drawn statewide however far out you are.

A handful of pending applications report no usable location in any form. They are counted in **Queue** and not drawn.

To limit permits to one patch of ground, draw a shape around it. See [Draw an area to search](draw-an-area-to-search.md).

For one company's permits instead of a map, open the operator and select its **Permits** tab. See [Look up an operator](look-up-an-operator.md).

## If something looks wrong

- **The counts in the key change as you pan.** They count what is on screen, and **Approved** shows approved minus drilled.
- **A permit sitting pending for months.** That is real. See the badge note above for what it means.
- **A permit whose operator differs from the well's current operator.** That is often the trace of a sale or a takeover in progress. A well record flags it on the **Filings** tab.

Related: [Look up a well](look-up-a-well.md), [Look up a county or a field](look-up-a-county-or-field.md).

pages.title: Find the people behind an operator
pages.body:
# Find the people behind an operator

Type a name into **Person** in Recon's filter bar and select it. A panel opens listing every operator the Texas Railroad Commission has that person on, and the map narrows to those companies' wells.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Recon**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Type at least two letters of the name in **Person**. Results show how many operators the person is on and how many wells those add up to.
3. Select the name.

The panel opens on the right. The map now shows only the wells of the operators that person is on.

To go the other way, from a company to its people:

1. Open the operator. See [Look up an operator](look-up-an-operator.md).
2. On the **Summary** tab, find the **Officers & principals** panel. Its heading carries the count.
3. Select a name. The operator record closes and the person's panel opens beside the map.

A well record does the same on its **Principals** tab, which lists the officers of the operator running that well.

## What the panel shows

The heading is the person's name, with **Principal / officer** and their city and state underneath. Below it, **Affiliated operators** lists every company the Commission has them on, with their title and the company's P-5 standing.

Two dropdowns sit above the list:

- **Any activity** filters by P-5 standing: **Active**, **Active (extension)**, **Active (hearing)**, **Inactive**, **Delinquent**, **Revoked**.
- **Well count** sorts the list. Change it to **Oil (per mo)** or **Gas (per mo)** to rank by production, or **Name (A–Z)**.

When a filter is hiding rows, the heading reads **Affiliated operators (3 of 11)** so a short list reads as filtered rather than as a person with fewer companies than they have.

Select any operator in the list to open its full record.

## Where this comes from

Officers and principals are the people named on the operator's P-5 organisation report filed with the Texas Railroad Commission. That is the only source. WildcatIQ does not add names from anywhere else, so:

- A company that files no officers shows **None on file**.
- Two people with the same name are one entry, because the filings carry no way to tell them apart.
- A person who has left the company stays listed until the operator files a P-5 that drops them, and P-5 renewals are annual.

## If something looks wrong

- **"No operators with that activity."** The **Any activity** filter is set to a standing none of this person's companies hold. Set it back to **Any activity**.
- **"Could not load principal detail."** Close the panel and select the name again.
- **The map went nearly empty after picking a person.** That is the filter working. The map now shows only that person's operators. Clear the person with the small cross beside their name in **Person**. See [Narrow your search](narrow-your-search.md).

Related: [Look up an operator](look-up-an-operator.md), [Export a list of operators](export-a-list-of-operators.md).

pages.title: Find wells on the map
pages.body:
# Find wells on the map

Open the menu, select **Recon**, and the map opens on the whole of Texas with every well the Railroad Commission holds a location for. Zoom in until the blue numbered bubbles break apart into single wells, then select a well to open its record.

Recon draws the state's public record, not your own wells. Nothing you do on this map changes your workspace data, and nobody else sees what you have on screen.

## Open the map

1. Open the menu and select **Recon**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Wait while the page shows **Loading map** and then **Loading wells**. The state is around a million wells, so the first view takes a few seconds.

The map opens over satellite imagery, fitted to Texas.

## Move around

1. Drag the map to move it.
2. Select **+** and **−** in the bottom right corner to zoom in and out. The scroll wheel and a two-finger pinch do the same thing.
3. Select **Map** for a plain street map, or **Satellite** for aerial imagery.

Your basemap choice lasts until you leave the page.

## Read what is drawn

Blue numbered bubbles are groups of wells, not single wells. The number is how many wells are inside, and the bubble gets larger and darker as that number rises.

Single dots are single wells, coloured by what the hole is doing now:

- **Green**: producing or otherwise running.
- **Red**: stopped. Plugged, shut in, temporarily abandoned, abandoned, partially plugged, sealed, or filed as no production.
- **Blue**: injecting. Saltwater disposal, waterflood injection, storage, water supply and observation wells.

Red wins over blue, so a disposal well that has been shut in is drawn red.

## Get down to single wells

1. Select a blue bubble. The map eases in two and a half zoom levels on that spot.
2. Repeat until dots replace bubbles. Bubbles stop at about zoom 12, which is roughly a few miles across the screen.

## Look up one well

1. Select the dot to open [the well's full record](look-up-a-well.md).

On a computer you can rest the pointer on a dot first. A small label gives the well's name, its API number, and what it makes per month, for example `1,240 bbl/mo · 300 MCF/mo`. Wells with nothing filed show no rate.

The rate is that well's allocated production averaged over its last 12 filed months, so it is a monthly average and not today's rate.

## When the map looks empty

Zoom out. At close zoom you are seeing a few square miles, and dry stretches of Texas genuinely have nothing in them. If you have set filters, the map is showing only what matches them: see [Narrow your search](narrow-your-search.md).

## Next

- [Narrow your search](narrow-your-search.md)
