pages.title: Look up a county or a field
pages.body:
# Look up a county or a field

Ask Orion for the county or field by name. It answers from the same Texas Railroad Commission records Recon draws: production history, lifetime volumes, and who is producing there.

The main Recon map does not open county or field records. On the map, a county is a filter and a field name is a label.

## Ask Orion

1. Open the menu and select **Orion**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Type the question in plain English, for example `How active is Andrews County?` or `Show me production for the Spraberry Trend Area field`.

See [Ask Orion a question](../orion-ai/ask-orion-a-question.md). Orion's answers use your AI credits.

Field names are not unique. The Commission issues separate numbers for separate reservoirs that share a name, so Orion lists the candidates and asks which one you mean.

## The Market boards

Recon also has a Market view with ranked boards. Nothing in the menu links to it, so you reach it by typing the address:

1. Type `/recon/market` after your WildcatIQ address in the browser bar, and press Enter.
2. Scroll to **Top counties** or **Top fields**.
3. Select a row. The record opens over the page.

**Top operators** and **Top leases** on the same page open their own records the same way. The boards list the statewide leaders only, so a county or field outside the top ranks is not on them. Ask Orion for it by name instead.

You can also reach a field from a lease record opened on this page: on the lease's **Summary** tab, select the field name in the **Lease record** panel.

## What a county record shows

- **Summary**: **Wells** on an operator's current schedule, **Permits · 12 mo**, **Oil, lifetime**, **Gas, lifetime**, and the **Latest reported cycle** panel.
- **Production**: the county's monthly chart.
- **Leases**: the leases carrying the production, with oil and gas. Select one to open it.

**Permits · 12 mo** is the only forward-looking number on the screen. Everything else is a record of work already done. See [Find new drilling permits](find-new-drilling-permits.md).

## What a field record shows

- **Summary**: **Leases**, **Operators**, **Oil, lifetime**, **Gas, lifetime**, and the **Latest reported cycle** panel.
- **Production**: the field's monthly chart.
- **Operators**: who is producing in the field, with their lease counts and volumes. Select one to open the operator.

## Where the numbers come from

All of it is Texas Railroad Commission filings, added up by the Commission's own county and field rollups. A county that straddles two districts is summed back together here, so these are county totals rather than one district's share.

The chart's last few months are shaded and read low. The Commission publishes about three months behind, so those months are not yet reported rather than months nothing was produced.

## If something looks wrong

- **"No RRC record for this county."** or **"No RRC record for this field."** Nothing is published under that reference.
- **The county or field you want is not on the boards.** The boards list the statewide leaders only. Ask Orion for it by name, or reach the field through one of its leases.

Related: [Look up a lease](look-up-a-lease.md), [Look up an operator](look-up-an-operator.md).

pages.title: Look up a lease
pages.body:
# Look up a lease

Open a well or an operator in Recon, then select the lease name. The lease record opens with the production Texas actually publishes, because the lease is the level the state reports at.

## Steps

From a well:

1. Open the well. See [Look up a well](look-up-a-well.md).
2. On the **Summary** tab, select the lease name in the **Lease & field** panel.

From an operator:

1. Open the operator. See [Look up an operator](look-up-an-operator.md).
2. Select the **Leases** tab.
3. Select the lease name.

The **Completions** tab on a well and the **Activity** tab on an operator also list lease names, and both open the same record.

## What you get

- **Summary**: oil and gas per month, wells on the lease, **Reports not filed**, the **Lease record** panel, and the **Latest reported cycle** panel with that month's volumes and allowables.
- **Production**: the monthly chart with the filing strip under it.
- **Allowables**: one row per month with volume, allowable, oil in tank, gas lift injection, and whether a report was filed.
- **Disposition**: where the product went, by stream and month.
- **Counties**: the split for a lease that crosses a county line. This is the only correct county figure for a lease, since the lease record itself carries a district and not a county.
- **Wells**: every well completed on the lease, with **Oil (bbl/d)** and **Gas (MCF/d)**. Select a row to open the well.
- **Purchaser**: who takes the product, and the P-4 filing history. The tab is hidden when the state holds neither.
- **Map**: the lease's wells plotted.

Select **Summarise** in the **AI summary** panel on the Summary tab for a written version. It uses your AI credits.

## What a zero month means

Every volume here is what the operator filed with the Texas Railroad Commission. A zero month is one of three things, and the strip under the production chart tells you which:

- **filed**: the month was published and a production report was filed. A zero here means the lease made nothing.
- **no report filed**: the month was published and this lease filed nothing. It draws as zero, and it is not a shut-in. The **Reports not filed** tile on the Summary tab counts these, and the **Allowables** tab marks them **no** in the **Filed** column.
- **not yet reported**: the Commission has not published the month yet. It runs about three months behind. These months are shaded on the chart and read **pending** in the **Filed** column.

The decline figures on the Production tab ignore both kinds of zero, so a run of unfiled months does not read as a collapse.

## Badges on the header

- **Off schedule**: the lease is not on an operator's current schedule. Most leases in Texas carry this, so it is common and rarely worth acting on.
- **Severed**: rare, and worth reading. The Commission has severed the lease.

## If something looks wrong

- **"This lease is not in the RRC mirror."** The Commission publishes nothing under that lease reference.
- **The last months of the chart fall to nothing.** Check the strip. That is almost always the publishing lag.
- **The county figures do not match the well count.** A lease can cross county lines. The **Counties** tab is the split.
- **The Field name is plain text and will not open.** On the main Recon map the field name is a label, not a link. The **Field no.** and **Field type** rows beside it carry the rest of what the Commission holds under that name.

Related: [Look up a well](look-up-a-well.md), [Look up an operator](look-up-an-operator.md), [Look up a county or a field](look-up-a-county-or-field.md).

pages.title: Look up a well
pages.body:
# Look up a well

Open the menu, select **Recon**, and select the well's dot on the map. Its full record opens over the map, built from Texas Railroad Commission filings rather than from anything you have entered.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Recon**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Leave **Show** set to **Wells**.
3. Narrow the map to the right area. Pick the county under **County**, or type the company name under **Operator**. See [Narrow your search](narrow-your-search.md).
4. Zoom in until you see single dots. A numbered blue bubble is a group of wells: select it and the map zooms in on it. See [Find wells on the map](find-wells-on-the-map.md).
5. Select the well's dot.

On a computer, resting the pointer on a dot shows the well's name, its API number and its current rate without opening anything. On a phone, tap the dot.

## What you get

The record opens with tabs across the top. Which tabs appear depends on what the Commission holds for that well.

- **Summary**: status, total depth, completion date, operator, and the lease and field the well is on. The lease name and the operator name are links.
- **Production**: the monthly chart, with **Oil**, **Gas**, **Condensate** and **Casinghead** buttons and a **12M / 5Y / 10Y / All** selector. **W-10 tests on file** and **G-10 tests on file** list the well's own filed test rates underneath.
- **Injection**: appears only for a well that holds an injection or disposal permit. Shows the permitted daily volume, what the well is running at, and the permits themselves.
- **Status**, **Compliance**, **Filings**: dates, Rule 14(b)(2) reasons, and the paperwork on file. These three appear for a well on an operator's current schedule.
- **Completions**: every lease and field this same hole is completed on, including under previous operators.
- **Principals**: the officers listed on the operator's P-5. See [Find the people behind an operator](find-the-people-behind-an-operator.md).
- **Location**: surface and bottomhole coordinates on a satellite map, with the lateral drawn.

Select **Summarise** in the **AI summary** panel on the Summary tab to have Orion write the record out in a few sentences. It uses your AI credits, and it only restates figures already on the tab.

## Where the production number comes from

Texas publishes production **by lease**, never per well. So the Production tab's chart is titled one of two things, and the difference matters:

- **Lease production**: the whole lease's reported volume. Other wells on the same lease are in that number.
- **Allocated to this well**: this well's share of the lease, weighted by the W-10 and G-10 test rates on file. It is an estimate worked out from filed tests, not a meter reading.

Under the chart is a strip of small blocks, one per month, and a key:

- **filed**: the Commission published the month and the operator filed a production report.
- **no report filed**: the Commission published the month and this lease filed nothing. It reads as zero volume on the chart. That is not the same as a well being shut in. About 18 in every 100 lease-months statewide are like this.
- **not yet reported**: the Commission has not published that month yet. It runs about three months behind. Those months are shaded grey on the chart, and they read zero because the month has not been published.

The Injection tab covers a longer stretch. Injection volumes come from Form H-10, which runs about fourteen months behind, and the shaded tail on that chart marks the same thing.

## If something looks wrong

- **"This wellbore is not in the RRC mirror."** The map plots a slightly wider list of wellbores than the records database holds, so a dot can open with nothing behind it.
- **A "Historic record" badge, and no Status, Compliance or Filings tabs.** The well is not on any operator's current schedule. The Commission leaves status, compliance and filing columns blank on those rows, so those tabs are left out rather than shown empty.
- **No Production tab.** Either the well injects, so it takes no share of the lease's oil, or it sits on no current lease to read a series from.
- **The last few months read zero.** That is the filing lag. Check the strip under the chart.
- **"Currently inactive" disagrees with the chart.** Inactivity is the Commission's own clock on the wellbore. A well can be counted inactive and still sit on a lease that reports volume.

Related: [Look up a lease](look-up-a-lease.md), [Look up an operator](look-up-an-operator.md).

pages.title: Look up an operator
pages.body:
# Look up an operator

In Recon, set **Show** to **Operators** and select the company's dot. Its record opens with the P-5 filing, the officers, the leases, the wells split four ways, and every permit and completion it has filed.

## Steps

1. Open the menu and select **Recon**. See [Find the screen you need](../getting-started/find-your-way-around.md).
2. Set **Show** to **Operators**. See [Switch between wells, permits and operators](switch-between-wells-permits-and-operators.md).
3. Type the company name in **Name** and select it from the list. The record opens.
4. If you would rather find it on the map, select the company's violet dot. A numbered bubble is a group of operators: see [Export a list of operators](export-a-list-of-operators.md).

You can also reach an operator from anywhere its name appears: the **Operator** row on a well record, the operator on a lease, the operator on a drilling permit, or a pipeline on the map.

While **Show** is set to **Wells**, picking a company under **Operator** only filters the map. It does not open the record. Switch to **Operators** or **Permits** first if you want the record.

## What you get

- **Summary**: estimated revenue per month, oil and gas per month, well count, the **P-5 profile** panel (status, address, phone, last P-5 date, oil and gas gatherers, counties, lease count), and **Officers & principals**.
- **Leases**: every lease, richest first, with oil, gas and an estimated monthly value. Select one to open it.
- **Active wells**, **Inactive wells**, **Injection**, **Plugged wells**: the fleet split four ways. The four counts add up to the whole fleet. Select any row to open that well.
- **Permits**: granted drilling permits, newest issue first, with filed, issued and expiry dates. A struck-through expiry date means the permit lapsed.
- **Activity**: permits, completions and pluggings on one timeline, grouped by year. Select a year to open or close it.
- **Map**: the fleet plotted, with permits where the record carries a position.

**Summarise** is on well and lease records. An operator record does not carry one.

## Where the numbers come from

Everything is Texas Railroad Commission filings.

**Est. revenue · per month** is the trailing twelve months of whole-lease production on the leases this operator's wells sit on, priced at the oil and gas quotes shown in the tile hints. It is gross, before royalty, deducts and differentials, and it counts volume that other working-interest owners are paid for. It is a rough size, not this company's income.

The **Wells** tile says what share of producible wells are active. Injection and plugged wells are left out of that ratio, because neither could be producing.

On the well tabs, only active wells carry an estimate. Inactive, injection and plugged rows read a dash by rule. The estimate itself is each well's share of its lease's last filed month, split by the W-10 and G-10 tests on file.

## Lists that are cut short

Large operators file more than one read returns. The screen says so on the tab when that happens:

- **"Showing the N highest-producing of M leases."**
- **"Showing the N most recently issued of M permits."** The tab count is the true total.
- **"Well tabs cover the first N of M wellbores."**
- **"Estimates cover this operator's first 150 lease records"**, and wells past that show a dash.

## If something looks wrong

- **An "Incomplete" badge on a year in Activity.** Permits, completion reports and plugging reports reach the Commission months after the work. That year's count is a floor, not a total.
- **Production and revenue read zero for a company you know is producing.** The Commission publishes about three months behind, and a company that files late shows less. See [Look up a lease](look-up-a-lease.md) for how filed months and unpublished months are told apart.
- **A dash in an estimate column.** Either the well is not running, or its lease is past the estimate cap. The line above the **Active wells** table says which case is in force.
- **"Could not load operator detail."** Close the record and select the operator again.

Related: [Find the people behind an operator](find-the-people-behind-an-operator.md), [Export a list of operators](export-a-list-of-operators.md).

pages.title: Narrow your search
pages.body:
# Narrow your search

Use the filter bar across the top of the map. Everything you set there is combined, so the map redraws to the wells that match all of it at once.

Filters live in this browser tab only. They are not saved, nobody else sees them, and reloading the page clears every one of them.

## Set the basics

1. Make sure **Show** is set to **Wells**.
2. Under **Type**, select **All**, **Oil** or **Gas**. This is the schedule the well is filed under, not what comes out of it.
3. Under **Status**, select any of **Active**, **Inactive** and **Plugged**. Select more than one to see all of them together. Select **All** to clear the whole group.
4. Under **District**, select the RRC districts you want, or **All districts**.
5. Under **Well type**, select what the well is doing, for example **Producing**, **Shut in** or **Injection**. Select **All well types** to clear it.

The bubble counts follow the Status filter, so a bubble stops counting wells the filter has hidden.

## When the map shows a sample

Some filters make Recon run a database search instead of drawing the statewide layer, and that search returns at most **30,000 wells**. When more than that match, an amber **Showing a sample** badge appears in the filter bar.

The 30,000 wells you get are the lowest API numbers, which is county order rather than a spread across the state. Treat the map as a partial answer until the badge is gone, and add a county, district or operator to clear it.

These filters trigger the search: County, Operator, Person, Well type, Depth, Completed, Production, and any drawn area. Type, Status, District and **Exclude plugged wells** do not.

## Filter by county

1. Type a county name in the box labelled **County**.
2. Select the county from the list. It becomes a chip in the bar.
3. Repeat for as many counties as you want.

Several counties means either county, not both. The map flies to cover the counties you picked. Select the **×** on a chip to remove one.

## Filter by operator

1. Type at least two characters of the company name in the box labelled **Operator**.
2. Select the operator from the list.

In Wells mode this filters the map to that operator's wells and leaves the map readable. [Their record](look-up-an-operator.md) is still one click away on any of the dots, and the survey tracts their wells sit on are outlined in amber.

## Filter by person

1. Type at least two characters of a name in the box labelled **Person**.
2. Select the person from the list. The line underneath each result gives how many operators and wells are behind that name, which is how you tell two people with the same name apart.

A person is not attached to wells directly, so Recon resolves the name to every operator that person is listed on as an officer, filing agent or resident agent, and draws those wells. Their panel opens at the same time.

Setting a Person and an Operator together means that person's wells at that company only, so pick a company the person is listed on.

## Filter by depth, completion year or production

1. Select **Depth**, **Completed** or **Production** in the filter bar. The group opens in a row below the bar.
2. For **Depth ft** and for **Production**'s **Oil bbl/mo** and **Gas MCF/mo**, type a **Min**, a **Max**, or both. Leaving one empty leaves that end open.
3. For **Completed**, pick a year from the **From** list, the **To** list, or both.
4. For **Depth** and **Completed** you can drag the two handles over the bar chart instead. The chart shows how many wells sit at each value, and the count under it updates as you drag.
5. Select **Clear depth**, **Clear completed** or **Clear production** to reset that group. Each button appears once that group has a value set.

Two things to know before you trust these:

- **Completed** excludes wells with no completion date on file, which is about 8% of wellbores. The bar shows **excl. undated** while the filter is on.
- **Production** is oil in barrels and gas in MCF per month, allocated over the well's last 12 filed months. Wells with nothing on file are excluded once you set either end, because unfiled is not the same as zero.

A number showing on a group's button is how many ends of that group are currently set. When Orion sets one of these for you, the group opens itself so you can see what it did.

## Hide plugged wells everywhere

1. Select the gear icon at the right end of the filter bar.
2. Select **Exclude plugged wells**.

This applies in every mode and drops plugged wells from the counts as well as the map. It survives a mode switch. Select it again to turn it off.

## Clear what you have set

There is no single reset. Remove filters the way you set them: select the **×** on a chip, choose **All** or **All districts** or **All well types**, or use the group's own **Clear** button. Switching mode clears the filters that belong to the mode you left, and reloading the page clears everything.

If the map goes blank, nothing matched. Widen or remove the last filter you set.

## Next

- [Draw an area to search](draw-an-area-to-search.md)
- [Switch between wells, permits and operators](switch-between-wells-permits-and-operators.md)
- [Find wells on the map](find-wells-on-the-map.md)

pages.title: Switch between wells, permits and operators
pages.body:
# Switch between wells, permits and operators

Use the **Show** buttons at the far left of the filter bar: **Wells**, **Permits**, **Operators**. Each one draws a different record, so the rest of the filter bar changes with it.

Switching keeps your drawn area and your gear settings, and clears the filters that belonged to the mode you left. Any open well record closes.

## Wells

Select **Wells** under **Show**. You get every wellbore the Railroad Commission has a location for. Green is running, red has stopped, blue injects. Filter it with [the filter bar](narrow-your-search.md) or [a drawn area](draw-an-area-to-search.md).

## Permits

Select **Permits** under **Show**. You get drilling permits, in three states. The key at the bottom left names them and counts what is on screen:

- **Pending**: amber. An application the RRC has received and not yet acted on. Approvals usually issue within one to eight days, so one sitting much longer is in a hearing, in a mapping correction, or has been refused. Permits filed for a horizontal well are drawn a darker amber.
- **Approved**: dark. Granted, and no completion filed yet.
- **Drilled**: green. Granted, and a well has since been filed on it.

The bar shows **Queue** with the number of pending applications. That is the whole state's queue, at every zoom. Approved and drilled permits are loaded for the part of the state you are looking at and reload each time you move the map, so panning to a new area takes a moment to fill in.

To see only certain filings:

1. Select the purpose button in the bar, which reads **All purposes** until you change it.
2. Tick the purposes you want, for example a new drill or a re-enter. The number beside each one is how many permits of that kind are loaded.
3. Select **Show all purposes** to go back to the whole queue.

Select any permit dot to open its details on the right. See [Find new drilling permits](find-new-drilling-permits.md) for what those details hold.

## Operators

Select **Operators** under **Show**. You get one violet dot per operating company, sized by how many wells it operates. **The dots sit at the company's mailing address, not at its wells.** An operator drilling in Reeves County is usually pinned in Houston.

- On a computer, rest the pointer on a dot for the company name, its address, how many wells it operates, and its production and estimated revenue per month.
- Select a dot to open [that operator's record](look-up-an-operator.md).
- Select a cluster to list the operators inside it on the right.

The filters change to match:

- **Wells**: type a **Min** and **Max** number of wells operated.
- **Production**: oil and gas per month, as the operator itself reported over its last 12 months.
- **Revenue**: an estimated dollars per month. The small figure beside the boxes is the oil and gas price the estimate uses, and it is gross, before royalty and deductions.
- **Works in**: type a county to keep only operators with a wellbore there. Their dots stay at their mailing addresses, so the map does not gather into that county.
- **Name**: type to find one company. **Person** shows every company a named officer or agent is listed on.

## What survives a switch

Kept: your drawn area, and everything in the gear menu (**Exclude plugged wells**, **Survey lines**, **Pipelines**).

Cleared: the mode's own filters, the operator list panel, and any well record you had open.

Nothing here is saved. Reloading the page puts you back in **Wells** with no filters set.

## Next

- [Narrow your search](narrow-your-search.md)
- [Draw an area to search](draw-an-area-to-search.md)
- [Turn on survey lines and pipelines](turn-on-survey-lines-and-pipelines.md)

pages.title: Turn on survey lines and pipelines
pages.body:
# Turn on survey lines and pipelines

Both layers live in the gear icon at the right end of the filter bar. **Survey lines** are already on and appear once you zoom in far enough; **Pipelines** are off until you turn them on.

Neither setting is saved. They carry across a mode switch, and reloading the page puts them back to survey lines on, pipelines off.

## See the survey and abstract lines

1. Select the gear icon at the right end of the filter bar. The menu is headed **Map settings**.
2. Check that **Survey lines** is ticked. It is ticked when you arrive.
3. Close the menu and zoom in. The note beside the item reads **zoom 12+**, and that is when the grid starts drawing. Zoomed further out there are over 300,000 tracts in Texas and the grid would be a solid smear, so nothing is drawn.
4. Keep zooming for the abstract labels, for example `A-64`. Those need two more zoom levels than the lines.

The lines are amber over satellite imagery and darker amber over the plain map. They are survey and abstract tracts, which is how land is described on a lease. A tract is larger than the lease inside it, so treat the outline as the neighbourhood of a lease, not its boundary.

The grid loads for the part of the state you are looking at, so it fills in a moment after you stop moving the map.

## Draw the pipelines

1. Select the gear icon at the right end of the filter bar.
2. Select **Pipelines**.
3. Close the menu.

The lines are cyan over satellite imagery and teal over the plain map. Unlike the survey grid, they draw at every zoom, noted as **all zooms** in the menu. What changes with zoom is the size of pipe:

- Zoomed out across the state, only transmission-scale pipe, 16 inches and up.
- Closer in, 10 inch, then 6 inch, then 3 inch.
- From zoom 12, everything including gathering lines.

Dashed, dimmed lines are abandoned or revoked pipe. The state keeps those on file until the steel comes out of the ground, so they are drawn differently rather than hidden: do not plan a connection on one.

At most 4,000 segments are drawn at once, largest bore first, so a statewide view is the trunk network rather than every line in Texas.

## Look up a pipeline

1. On a computer, rest the pointer on a line. The label gives what it carries, its diameter, the operator, and the system name. A line with no size on file reads **size n/a**.
2. Select the line to open [that operator's record](look-up-an-operator.md). On a phone this is what a tap does, since there is no resting.

To turn the pipelines off again, select the gear icon and select **Pipelines** a second time.

## Next

- [Find wells on the map](find-wells-on-the-map.md)
- [Narrow your search](narrow-your-search.md)

pages.title: Change your email address
pages.body:
# Change your email address

WildcatIQ emails a confirmation link to the address you sign in with today, and your address changes when you open that link and type the new one there. So check the inbox you use now, not the new one.

## Step 1: ask for the link

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Profile** at the top of the page.
4. In the **Profile** card, select **Change email** beside your address.
5. Read the panel headed **Change your email**. It names the address the link is going to.
6. Select **Send me the link**.

The panel closes and a line under the **Email** box confirms the link went to your current address.

Your old address still signs you in until you finish, and nobody is notified.

## Step 2: open the email

1. Open the inbox for the address you sign in with now. Look in the spam folder if you do not see it.
2. Find the email **Confirm your WildcatIQ email change**.
3. Select **Choose a new email** in it.

The link is good for **1 hour** and works once. Open it on any device, including a phone that is not signed in to WildcatIQ.

## Step 3: type the new address

1. On the **Choose your new email** screen, type your new address in **New email**.
2. Type the same address again in **Confirm new email**. Copy and paste is turned off in this box on purpose, so type it out.
3. Select **Change my email**.

What you type becomes your sign-in address the moment you select **Change my email**, so read both boxes before you do.

The screen reads **Email updated**. Select **Back to settings** to return to WildcatIQ. On a device that is not signed in, sign in there with the new address.

### What happens next

- You sign in with the new address from now on. The old one no longer works.
- Your password does not change, and you stay signed in on every device.
- A message headed **Your WildcatIQ email address was changed** goes to your old address, so a change you did not make does not pass unnoticed.
- Your teammates are not emailed. Your new address shows on your row in the member list your workspace admin sees.

## If the link has expired

The screen reads **This link has expired** and **Your email address hasn't changed**.

1. Select **Send new link**. On a device signed in to WildcatIQ, a fresh link goes to your current address.
2. On a device that is not signed in, sign in there, then start again from **Settings**, **Profile**, **Change email**.

Asking for a new link cancels the old one, so always use the newest email.

## Common problems

**The email went to the wrong inbox.** It goes to the address on your account today, the one shown in the **Email** box in **Settings**. If you can no longer open that inbox, [contact support](../getting-help/contact-support.md).

**You pressed the button twice.** Only the newest link works. Open the most recent email.

**You typed the new address wrong.** Sign in with the address you typed and your usual password, then [contact support](../getting-help/contact-support.md) to have it corrected.

**You want to change a coworker's address.** Each person changes their own, from their own **Settings**.

pages.title: Change your password
pages.body:
# Change your password

Change your password in **Settings** under **Profile**, in the **Password** card. You need your current password to do it, so if you cannot remember it, see [Reset a password you forgot](reset-a-password-you-forgot.md) instead.

## Steps

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Profile** at the top of the page.
4. In the **Password** card, type the password you use now in **Current password**.
5. Type the new one in **New password**. Use at least 8 characters.
6. Type it again in **Confirm new password**.
7. Select **Change password**.

**Change password** stays greyed out until all three boxes have something in them. Once it goes through, the three boxes empty out and a line beside the button reads **Password changed**.

## What happens next

- Use the new password the next time you sign in.
- You stay signed in here, and on your phone and any other device, until those sessions run out on their own.
- An email headed **Your WildcatIQ password was changed** goes to your address, so a change you did not make does not pass unnoticed.
- No one else is notified, and your workspace admin cannot see your password.

There is no undo. To go back to the old password, change it again using the new one as the current password.

## Messages you might see

**That's not your current password.** The top box is wrong. What you typed in the two boxes below it is fine.

**Use at least 8 characters.** The new password is too short.

**Those two passwords don't match.** The second and third boxes differ. Retype both.

**That's already your password. Pick a different one.** The new password is the same as the current one.

pages.title: Choose which notifications you get
pages.body:
# Choose which notifications you get

Open **Settings**, select **Notifications**, and turn each switch on or off. Every switch saves the moment you touch it, and the choices are yours alone: nobody else's alerts change.

## Steps

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Notifications** at the top of the page.
4. Find the row you want in the **Notification** column. The **Description** column says when it fires.
5. Turn the switch on or off in the **Email**, **In-app** or **Mobile** column.

There is no save button. The switch moves and it is saved. Turn it back to undo it.

## What the three columns mean

- **Email**: a message to the address on your account.
- **In-app**: the bell inside WildcatIQ.
- **Mobile**: a push alert on your phone. It reaches you if the WildcatIQ app is installed on that phone and you are signed in to it.

Each column is separate. Turning off **Email** for a row leaves the bell and the phone alone.

## The rows you see

Everyone sees the personal rows: **Comments on wells**, **Comments on other facilities**, **Replies to your comments**, **Likes on your comments**, **Mentions**, **New production readings**, **Equipment status changes**, **Direct messages**, **Support replies**, **Your access changes**, **Tasks assigned to you**, **Task deadlines**, **Low inventory**, **Document processed** and **Calendar reminders**.

**New financial transactions** appears if you can see accounting. **Invitations accepted**, **Billing & payments** and **AI credits low** appear if you are a workspace admin. A row you do not see covers a part of WildcatIQ your account does not open.

## What is on before you change anything

Almost everything is on in all three columns. Four rows start differently:

- **Replies to your comments**, **Likes on your comments** and **Direct messages** arrive in the app and on your phone, with **Email** off. A chat gets read where it happens, so there is no email for every line.
- **Document processed** is off everywhere. Turn it on if you want to hear about every file that finishes.

## Reports emailed on a schedule

Those are not set here. Workspace admins set them on the **Reports** tab in **Settings**, and they apply to the whole workspace rather than to you.

pages.title: Manage your subscription and card
pages.body:
# Manage your subscription and card

Select **Billing** at the top of **Settings**. It opens your billing page at Stripe, our payment company, in a new browser tab.

Only workspace admins see the **Billing** tab.

## Steps

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Billing** at the top of the page.
4. Wait for the new tab to load. It shows your workspace's plan and payment details, and it is where you update a card, cancel, or restart a plan.
5. Make the change there. Stripe applies it as soon as you confirm it.
6. Close the Stripe tab and go back to the WildcatIQ tab when you are done.

**Billing** never becomes the selected tab in WildcatIQ, and the page underneath stays as it was. That is normal.

## What happens next

- Cancelling, restarting or changing a card takes effect at Stripe immediately, and WildcatIQ catches up within a few moments. Reload the WildcatIQ page to see it sooner.
- Card numbers are typed at Stripe and stored there. WildcatIQ never sees them.
- Other admins in the workspace can open the same billing page and see the same details. People without admin access cannot.

## If nothing opens

Your browser blocked the new tab. Allow pop-ups for WildcatIQ, or look for a blocked-pop-up notice in the address bar, then select **Billing** again.

If a message appears under the row of tabs instead, read it. **Billing is not configured.** means the workspace has no billing set up yet. Any other message is the reason Stripe could not be reached, and selecting **Billing** again is worth a try.

## If WildcatIQ is locked with a billing message

When a payment fails or a subscription lapses, WildcatIQ covers itself with a message and nothing else opens. The heading tells you which one it is: **Payment failed**, **Your subscription is cancelled**, or **This workspace has no subscription**.

1. Select **Go to billing**. It opens the same Stripe page.
2. Fix the payment or restart the plan there.
3. Come back to the WildcatIQ tab and select **I've reactivated, refresh**, or **I've subscribed, refresh** if there was no plan.

The lock lifts once the payment goes through. Managing billing needs admin access: anyone else who selects **Go to billing** is told to ask an admin to reactivate the subscription.

A fourth heading, **We couldn't confirm your subscription**, is ours to fix rather than yours. It offers **Try again**, and your plan is untouched.

## Related

[Start your plan and add a card](../getting-started/choose-a-plan-and-add-a-card.md) covers picking monthly or annual when you first sign up.

pages.title: Refer another operator
pages.body:
# Refer another operator

Open **Settings**, select **Referral**, and send someone your referral link. When they sign up through it and finish setting up their account, both workspaces get $1,500.00 in platform credit.

Every member of your workspace shares the same link, and the credit belongs to the workspace rather than to the person who sent it.

## Share your link

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Referral** at the top of the page.
4. Under **Your referral link**, select **Copy**. The button reads **Copied** for a moment.
5. Paste it into a text message or an email and send it.

Under it is **Your referral code**, six characters with its own **Copy** button. Use that when you are reading it out over the phone. The other person selects **Have a referral code?** on the sign-up screen, types it into **Referral code**, and gets the same result.

Anyone who opens your link lands on the WildcatIQ sign-up screen with your company already named on it, so they can see who referred them before they sign up.

## If there is no link yet

The card reads **No referral code yet. Reload this page to generate one.** Reload the page and the link appears.

## See what you have earned

Admins see a **Platform credit** section under the link.

1. Read **Current balance**. That is the credit the workspace holds today.
2. Select **Activity** to open the list of everything that added to the balance or spent it, newest first, with the date and amount on each row. Select it again to close it.

Platform credit comes off your next subscription invoice on its own, and you can spend it instead of a card when you buy AI credits. It is not paid out as cash.

If someone you referred does not finish their free trial, you lose any credit you still have from referring that person. Credit from your other referrals is untouched, and anything you already spent stays spent.

Members who are not admins see the link and the code but not the balance.

pages.title: Reset a password you forgot
pages.body:
# Reset a password you forgot

On the sign-in page, select **Forgot password?** next to the **Password** label, type your email address and select **Send reset link**. Open the emailed link and choose a new password.

If you are already signed in and just want a different password, see [Change your password](change-your-password.md) instead.

## Send yourself a reset link

1. Go to the WildcatIQ sign-in page.
2. Select **Forgot password?** to the right of the **Password** label. The heading changes to **Reset your password**.
3. Type your address in **Email**.
4. Select **Send reset link**.

The screen confirms a link is on its way and tells you to check your inbox and spam folder. The message reads the same whether or not there is an account for that address.

Select **Back to sign in** when you are done.

## Set the new password

1. Open the email and select the link. It is good for **1 hour** and works once.
2. The screen reads **Choose a new password** after a moment of checking.
3. Type the new password in **New password**. Use at least 8 characters.
4. Type it again in **Confirm new password**.
5. Select **Set new password**.

The screen reads **Password updated** and you are already signed in. Select **Continue to WildcatIQ**.

Your other devices stay signed in until their sessions run out on their own. An email headed **Your WildcatIQ password was changed** goes to your address.

## If you do not remember which email you used

1. On the **Reset your password** screen, find **Don't remember your email?** at the bottom and select **Look it up**.
2. Type your company as it appears on the account in **Company name**, or your number in **Or phone number**. One of the two is enough.
3. Select **Find my email**.
4. Look at the accounts found. Each shows a partly hidden address such as **ra\*\*\*n@gmail.com**, with the company under it. The first one is the closest match.
5. Select **Send link** on the right row.

The full address is never shown, and the reset link goes to it without you having to know it. If nothing matches, try the company name exactly as it appears on your account, or the phone number saved on your profile.

Select **Search again** to try different details.

## If the link has expired

The screen reads **This link has expired**. Select **Send a new link** and enter your address again. Reset links last an hour and work once, so always open the newest email.

## If you tried too many times

The message reads **Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.** That limit counts attempts from your internet connection, not from your account. Wait, then try again.

pages.title: Update your company details
pages.body:
# Update your company details

Your company name, address and RRC operator number are in **Settings** on the **Profile** tab, in the **Company** card. Only workspace admins see that card, and the fields save as you type.

## Change the RRC operator number

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Profile** at the top of the page.
4. In the **Company** card, type your six digit P-5 number in **RRC operator number**. Only digits go in, and it stops at six.
5. Select somewhere else on the page.

At the bottom of the card a line reads **Saving**, then **Saved**, and the name the Railroad Commission has under that number appears under the box. That name is your proof you typed the right six digits.

To unlink it, clear the box and select somewhere else.

### What happens next

- Wells already on your account stay exactly as they are. Changing this number does not import wells and does not remove any.
- **Sync with RRC** on a well or lease uses this number to find the right record in the state's files. A well with no API number on file is matched by name against the wells on this operator's P-5.
- Everyone in the workspace is affected, since there is one number for the company. Nobody is emailed.

### If the number is refused

The message reads **No operator is registered with the Railroad Commission under number** and the number you typed. Your old number stays linked, and what you typed stays in the box so you can correct it.

**Railroad Commission records are not available right now.** means the state's records are unreachable at that moment. Try again later.

## Change the company name or address

Only the person who created the workspace can change these two. If that is you:

1. In the **Company** card, type over **Company name**.
2. Type over **Company address**.
3. Select somewhere else on the page to save right away, or wait a moment for **Saved** to appear.

The company name is the workspace name your teammates see when they switch workspaces, so the change shows for everyone. To undo it, type the old name back in.

If you are an admin but did not create the workspace, ask the person who did. The **Organization** tab says who that is: their row in the **Members** table reads **Owner** in the **Status** column.

## If you do not see the Company card

You are not an admin of this workspace. Your own name, photo and phone are still yours to change on the same tab. See [Update your name and photo](update-your-name-and-photo.md).

pages.title: Update your name and photo
pages.body:
# Update your name and photo

Your name, photo and phone number live in **Settings** under **Profile**, and they save on their own as you type. Select your photo in the top right corner, then **Settings**, then **Profile**.

## Change your name or phone number

1. Select your photo in the top right corner.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Profile** at the top of the page.
4. In the **Profile** card, type over what is in **Name**.
5. Type your number in **Phone**. It formats itself as **(555) 555-5555** while you type.

There is no save button. A moment after you stop typing, a line at the bottom of the card reads **Saving**, then **Saved**. Selecting somewhere else on the page saves right away instead of waiting.

Your name and photo show on your comments, your messages and the member list your workspace admin sees, so everyone you work with sees the change. To undo it, type the old value back in.

## Add or change your photo

1. In the **Profile** card, select **Upload photo**. If you already have one, the button reads **Change photo** instead.
2. Pick a picture from your computer or phone. It needs to be a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF file, 5 MB or smaller.

The picture appears straight away and saves by itself, with no separate save step.

To swap it for a different picture, select **Change photo** again. There is no button that removes a photo and leaves you with none.

## The email box will not let you type

That is deliberate. Changing the address you sign in with needs to be confirmed by email first. See [Change your email address](change-your-email-address.md).

pages.title: A list will not finish loading
pages.body:
# A list will not finish loading

Reload the page. That clears nearly every stuck list.

On a phone, pull down on the page or use the reload button in the browser bar. On a computer, press F5, or Command and R together on a Mac.

## The Production tabs

The **Tanks**, **Meters** and **Batteries** tabs on the **Production** page load in the background while you look at **Wells**. If one is still spinning when you get there:

1. Reload the page.
2. Select the tab again.

Reload the same way after you change a tank, a meter or a battery on that page, so the row shows your change.

## A report is still building

Reports are built at the moment you open them, and a large one over a long period takes time. Give a report a minute before reloading. Reloading part way through starts the wait again.

## If reloading does not fix it

1. Check your internet connection. WildcatIQ needs a live connection for every screen, and a weak signal in the field shows up as a list that never arrives.
2. Check the workspace. Select your picture in the top right corner and read the name under **Workspace**. An empty list is sometimes a full list in a workspace you are not in. See [Switch between workspaces](../getting-started/switch-between-workspaces.md).
3. Check that the list is meant to have something in it. A table with nothing in it says so plainly, such as **No inventory to display.**, rather than spinning.
4. Try a different browser or another device, to tell a problem with this computer from a problem with your account.

If it is still spinning, [contact support](contact-support.md). Say which page, which tab, and roughly how long you waited.

pages.title: A screen or button is missing
pages.body:
# A screen or button is missing

Almost always this is permissions. WildcatIQ shows each account only what it is allowed to open, so a page you are not set up for is not in the menu and its address leads nowhere. Ask whoever set up your workspace to switch on the permission you need.

Your own permissions are not shown to you anywhere in WildcatIQ. Only the owner and the admins can see them, so this is a question you have to ask someone.

## Ask for the permission

1. Open the menu and select **Messages**, which everyone has. Message the person who set up your workspace and tell them which page or button you cannot find.
2. They open **Settings**, then the **Organization** tab, then **Members**.
3. They find your row and select the button in the **Permissions** column, which reads what you have now.
4. They switch on the area from the table below, under **Access by area**, then select **Done**. See [Set what a coworker can see](../people-and-access/set-what-a-coworker-can-see.md).
5. Reload the page in your browser. The new permission takes effect on your next page load. You do not need to sign out.

Each switch saves as they flip it, and you get a notification, **Your access changes**, whenever your permissions are changed.

## What to ask for

| Missing from the menu | Area to switch on |
| --- | --- |
| **Orion** | AI |
| **Dashboard** | Analytics |
| **Projects** | Projects |
| **Files** | Files |
| **Notes** | Notes |
| **Agenda** | Agenda |
| **Leases** | Leases |
| **Production** | Wells |
| **Disposal** | Disposal |
| **Facilities** | Facilities |
| **Inventory** | Inventory |
| **Revenue** | Revenue |
| **Invoices** | Invoices |
| **Prices** | Pricing |
| **People** | People |
| **Reports** | Reports |

**Messages** and **Recon** are in the menu for everyone. **Settings** and support are not in the menu at all: select your picture in the top right corner to reach them, and everyone has both.

**Reports** is the one that needs more than its own area. It only turns on once **View well production** and **View revenue** are both on, because a single report can carry production and money together.

## The page is there but a button is not

Looking and changing are separate permissions. Someone can be given the numbers without being given the ability to change them.

- No **Add**, **Allocation** or gear icon on an oil tank or a battery: **Manage oil production**.
- No **Add**, **Allocation** or gear icon on a gas meter: **Manage gas production**.
- No **Add** or gear icon on a saltwater tank: **Manage disposal**. Creating a saltwater well takes **Add injection wells**.
- No **Shot** in the **Add** menu on a well: **Manage well equipment**. No **Service**: **Manage well service**.
- No **Invoice** button on **Invoices**: **Manage invoices**.

These sit under **Advanced** in the same permissions panel, one switch each.

## Other reasons a screen goes missing

- **You are in a different workspace than you think.** Permissions are set per workspace, so the same account can be an owner in one and read-only in another. Select your picture in the top right and check the name under **Workspace**. See [Switch between workspaces](../getting-started/switch-between-workspaces.md).
- **The oil and gas prices vanished from the top bar.** That strip needs **View pricing**, and it shows only on a wide screen, so a phone or a tablet does not carry it.
- **Everything went at once and you were signed out.** You may have been taken out of the workspace, which takes effect immediately. Ask the owner. It can be undone, and your history comes back with you. See [Restore someone you removed](../people-and-access/restore-someone-you-removed.md).

If the right permission is on, you have reloaded, and the screen is still missing, [contact support](contact-support.md) and say which page you are trying to reach.

pages.title: An email did not arrive
pages.body:
# An email did not arrive

Look in the junk or spam folder first, then search the whole mailbox for `wildcatiq.ai`. Everything WildcatIQ sends comes from `WildcatIQ <noreply@wildcatiq.ai>`, so that one search finds all of it, wherever the mail program filed it.

Add that address to your contacts so later mail lands in the inbox.

## An invitation to join a workspace

The link is only ever sent by email. It is never shown on screen, so nobody can read it out to you over the phone.

1. Search the invited person's mailbox, junk folder included, for `wildcatiq.ai`. The subject is **You've been invited to Wildcat**.
2. If it is not there, an admin opens **Settings**, the **Organization** tab, then **Members**.
3. They find the row marked **Pending** and select the circular arrows button on it, **Resend invite**.

Points that catch people out:

- **An invite link lasts 7 days**, then stops working. Resending gives a fresh 7 days.
- **Resending cancels the previous link.** If the person has both emails, only the newest one works.
- **Each link works once.** Once they have signed up, the link is spent.
- **The address may be wrong.** Check the spelling in the **Email** column. To correct it, select the **x** on that row to cancel the invite, then invite them again with the right address.
- **A row showing Pending means the email went out.** WildcatIQ creates the invite only once the mail is away, so the admin sees an error on the spot instead.

See [Invite a coworker](../people-and-access/invite-a-coworker.md) and [Accept an invitation](../people-and-access/accept-an-invitation.md).

## A link to confirm an email change

**The link goes to your old address, not the new one.** WildcatIQ writes to the address currently on your account to check it is really you, and you choose the new address after you open the link.

1. Open the mailbox for the address shown in **Settings**, on the **Profile** tab, under **Email**.
2. Look for the subject **Confirm your WildcatIQ email change**.
3. **The link expires after one hour.** If yours is older, go back to **Settings**, **Profile**, select **Change email**, then **Send me the link**, and use the new mail.

Sending a new link cancels the previous one. Nothing about your account changes until you open a link and finish the change.

If you can no longer get into the old mailbox at all, [contact support](contact-support.md).

See [Change your email address](../your-account/change-your-email-address.md).

## A scheduled report

Scheduled reports arrive as one email per schedule. The subject is your company name followed by **Daily Reports**, **Weekly Reports** or **Monthly Reports**, so searching your mailbox for `Reports` alongside your company name finds them.

1. Open the menu and select **Reports**.
2. Select the gear icon beside the heading, which opens **Report delivery**.
3. Check that the switch for that report is on in the **Daily**, **Weekly** or **Monthly** column.
4. Check **Arrives at**. The hour and the timezone there apply to every scheduled report at once, and a report sent at 6 AM Central arrives in the small hours if you are reading it somewhere else.

Points that catch people out:

- **Not every report can be emailed.** A row whose **Section** reads **not emailable yet** has its switches greyed out.
- **The report goes to the address that was on your account when the switch was turned on.** Changing your email address later does not redirect reports that were already switched on. Ask support to re-point them.
- **A late report is tried again.** WildcatIQ retries a delayed report on the next pass, so give it a few hours before treating it as missing.
- **Setting up report delivery needs one of the management permissions.** See [A screen or button is missing](a-screen-or-button-is-missing.md).

See [Have reports emailed to you](../reports/have-reports-emailed-to-you.md).

## Notifications about replies, mentions and comments

These are separate from the mail above and each one can be switched off per person.

1. Open **Settings**, then the **Notifications** tab.
2. Find the row, such as **Support replies** or **Direct messages**.
3. Check the switch in the **Email** column.

Direct messages arrive on the bell and send email only once you switch the **Email** column on. See [Choose which notifications you get](../your-account/choose-which-notifications-you-get.md).

## If none of it arrives

A company mail server that blocks outside senders stops all of it at once. Ask whoever looks after your email to allow `noreply@wildcatiq.ai`, then [contact support](contact-support.md) and tell us which emails you are missing.

pages.title: Book a call with support
pages.body:
# Book a call with support

Select your picture in the top right corner, then **Chat with support**, then **Book a call**. Pick a day and time on the booking page that opens.

## Steps

1. Select your picture in the top right corner.
2. Select **Chat with support**.
3. Select **Book a call** at the top right, above the conversation.
4. A booking page opens in a new browser tab. Pick a day and time there, and confirm it.

## What happens next

The booking is handled on that page, not inside WildcatIQ. Your confirmation and any reminders come from the booking service, to the email address you type in there.

Nothing about the call is recorded in **Requests**, so a booked call leaves no trace in WildcatIQ. To change or cancel, use the links in the confirmation email the booking service sent you.

Your coworkers are not told that you booked a call.

## If you do not see Book a call

Ask for a call in the chat instead. Type the days and times that suit you and send it, and someone will arrange it with you. See [Contact support](contact-support.md).

pages.title: Contact support
pages.body:
# Contact support

Select your picture in the top right corner, then **Chat with support**. Type your message in the box and press Enter. A Wildcat representative answers you in the same window.

Support is open to everyone signed in to WildcatIQ. You do not need any special permission to use it.

## Steps

1. Select your picture in the top right corner.
2. Select **Chat with support**.
3. Type your message in the box marked **Message support…**. Say which well, lease or page you are looking at, what you expected to see, and what you saw instead.
4. To send a photo or a file with it, select the paperclip, then pick the file. The file appears as a small chip just above the line you type on. Select the **x** on the chip to take it off again.
5. Press Enter to send. Use Shift and Enter together if you want a new line instead.

## What happens next

Your message appears on the right side of the window with **Delivered** and how long ago it landed.

Under it, a note in a dashed box reads "Thanks for reaching out. We have your message, and a Wildcat representative will respond as soon as possible." That note is automatic. It is not a person answering, and it goes away as soon as a real reply arrives.

The reply lands in this same window. You also get a notification on the bell and by email. See [Track a support request](track-a-support-request.md).

Only you and Wildcat support can read your requests. Your coworkers cannot see them, and neither can the owner of your workspace. A file you attach stays with the conversation and does not appear on your **Files** page.

A sent message cannot be edited or taken back. Send a follow-up message instead.

## Other things you may notice

- **The send arrow is grey.** There is nothing to send yet. Type something, or attach a file.
- **You want to talk to someone instead of typing.** See [Book a call with support](book-a-call.md).

pages.title: Production numbers look wrong
pages.body:
# Production numbers look wrong

Three things account for nearly all of it: the last gauged day is deliberately left out, a well's share is set by its allocation split, and a well nobody has gauged shows the state's filed numbers instead of yours. Work down this page in order.

## The newest day is missing or reads low

This is how WildcatIQ is meant to work. A gauge is taken at a time of day, never at midnight, so the last day a tank covers is only a part of a day. Counting it would show a battery that looks like it quit, so WildcatIQ leaves that day out of the tables, the charts and the boxes at the top of the page.

The next gauge closes the day off and the day comes back with a full 24 hours behind it. Nothing is lost, and there is nothing to fix.

The day left out is the last day a gauge covers, which is not always today. If the last gauge on that tank was Tuesday morning, Tuesday is the day being held back.

See [Record a tank gauge](../daily-production-entry/record-a-tank-gauge.md).

## One well is wrong but the tank or battery total is right

A well does not measure itself. The tank or the battery is measured, and each well gets a share of it. If the total is right and the split is wrong, the split is what to look at.

- **The split percentages for that date.** Open the menu, select **Production**, then the **Batteries** tab, then the battery. Select **Allocation** and check the period covering the dates you are querying. Each period runs between a **From** and a **To** date, lists its wells with a percentage each, and has to add to 100%. A well that is not in the period gets nothing for those days. You need **Manage oil production** to see the **Allocation** button.
- **Downtime.** A well marked down for a day gets nothing for that day, and its percentage is handed to the wells on the battery that were online. That is why one well can jump the day a neighbour goes down. Open the well and check its **Downtime** tab. See [Record downtime or a shut-in](../daily-production-entry/record-downtime-or-a-shut-in.md).

Saltwater tanks carry their own split on the tank itself, and a gas meter carries its own on the meter. Those need **Manage disposal** and **Manage gas production**.

## The numbers are the state's, not yours

Where a well has nothing gauged or metered against it, WildcatIQ shows what the operator filed with the Texas Railroad Commission, so a page is never blank. On the lease **Production** tab those rows sit under the heading **Reported to the Railroad Commission · monthly average**, and they are greyed.

Texas runs two to three months behind, so the recent months look empty and the rate looks like it is dying off. A month the operator never filed shows a dash rather than a zero, because nobody reported it. Water never appears at all, because Texas publishes no produced-water volumes.

Once you enter gauges and meter readings for a well, your own figures take over.

## Money figures are estimates until a statement is posted

Every revenue figure outside a purchaser statement is your volume multiplied by a price estimate. Real money arrives when you post a settlement statement.

Open the menu and select **Dashboard**. On the production chart, the grey band at the right-hand end covers the months no statement has settled yet. Everything inside that band is priced rather than settled.

See [Post a statement to revenue](../finance/post-a-statement-to-revenue.md).

## Still wrong

- **Headline rates are averages.** The rate in the boxes at the top of a well or lease page is a 14-day average, so it does not match yesterday's single reading and is not meant to.
- **Compare against the source.** Open the tank or meter and read the raw entries. If the readings are right and the well is wrong, look at the split. If the readings are wrong, correct the reading. See [Correct or delete a gauge reading](../daily-production-entry/correct-or-delete-a-gauge-reading.md).
- **Two screens disagree about the same number.** That is worth reporting. [Contact support](contact-support.md) with the well or lease name, the dates, and both figures.

# Track a support request

Select your picture in the top right corner, then **Chat with support**. Every request you have sent is listed in the **Requests** panel, with the most recent activity at the top. Select one to read the whole conversation.

## Steps

1. Select your picture in the top right corner.
2. Select **Chat with support**.
3. In the **Requests** panel, select the request you want to read.
4. Read the conversation from the top. Your messages sit on the right. Replies from Wildcat sit on the left with the Wildcat mark beside them.

## What each row tells you

- **The heading** is the opening line of your first message, shortened to fit. It is filled in for you and cannot be changed. A request you have not sent anything on yet reads **New request**.
- **The time** on the right is how long ago the last message landed, such as `2d`.
- **The line underneath** is the newest message. `You:` in front of it means it was yours.
- **A dot** beside the heading means Wildcat has replied and you have not read it yet. It clears as soon as you open the request.

## How you find out about a reply

Replies arrive on the bell inside WildcatIQ and by email, from `WildcatIQ <noreply@wildcatiq.ai>`. This is switched on for you already, under **Support replies**. To change it, see [Choose which notifications you get](../your-account/choose-which-notifications-you-get.md).

If you have the support window open when a reply is sent, it appears straight away without reloading.

## Add to an old request

1. Select the request in the **Requests** panel.
2. Type in the box at the bottom and press Enter.

An old conversation still takes new messages, however long ago it started.

## Start a separate request

Select the **+** at the top of the **Requests** panel. Use a new request for an unrelated question, so the two do not get tangled together.

If you already have a request open that you never sent anything on, the **+** takes you back to that one rather than making another.

# WildcatIQ Privacy Policy

**Last edited:** September 28, 2026

## Overview

WildcatIQ ("we," "us," or "our") operates the website wildcatiq.ai, the web application at app.wildcatiq.ai, and the WildcatIQ mobile app for iOS and Android (collectively, the "Services"). This policy explains how we collect, use, share, and protect information when you use the Services.

By using the Services, you agree to the collection and use of information in accordance with this policy.

## Applicability

This policy applies to all WildcatIQ websites, applications, and support interactions. It does not cover third-party services you connect to or reach through the Services, such as Dropbox or our demo scheduling page, which have their own privacy policies.

## Information We Collect

**Account Information.** When you create an account, we collect your name, email address, password (stored in hashed form), phone number, company name and address, and an optional profile photo.

**User Information.** We collect information about users added to your organization, including names, email addresses, phone numbers, and permissions.

**Operational Data.** When you use the Services, you enter or upload well, lease, production, equipment, accounting, invoice, and regulatory data, along with documents, photos, notes, comments, and team messages. This can include information about people who are not users, such as employees, contractors, vendors, and royalty and working-interest owners. This data belongs to your company (see Data Ownership).

**AI Conversations.** When you use Orion, our AI assistant, we store your conversations. Orion also keeps notes about your preferences and working habits, which it updates automatically so it can help you better.

**Mobile App Permissions.** The mobile app may request access to your camera, photo library, microphone, Face ID or other biometrics, and notifications. These are used to scan documents, attach photos, dictate by voice, unlock the app, and send alerts. You can change any of these in your device settings. Biometric data stays on your device and is never sent to us. The app does not collect your location.

**Offline Data on Your Device.** So you can work without a connection, the mobile app stores a copy of your organization's data on your device. This copy stays on the device after you sign out. It is removed when a different person signs in on that device, when you are removed from the organization, or when you delete the app.

**Usage and Log Data.** Our hosting and authentication providers record technical information such as IP addresses, browser type, and access times. We also record IP addresses to prevent abuse of account recovery.

**Billing Information.** Payments are processed by Stripe. Your card details go directly to Stripe, and we do not store full card numbers.

**Cookies.** We use cookies only to keep you signed in and to make the Services work, such as remembering preferences and referral links. We do not use analytics or advertising cookies, and we do not use third-party analytics tools.

**Communications.** We keep records of support conversations and emails between you and us.

**Public Data.** The Services display publicly available records, such as Texas Railroad Commission operator and well data and county appraisal district mineral rolls, which may include names and mailing addresses.

## How We Use Your Information

We use the information we collect to:

- Provide, operate, and maintain the Services
- Set up your account, organization, and user permissions
- Process payments and manage subscriptions
- Send notifications by email, in the app, or by push notification, based on your settings
- Deliver scheduled reports to the recipients your organization chooses
- Power Orion and other AI features
- Prepare regulatory report files for you to review and file
- Provide customer support
- Improve the Services
- Detect and prevent fraud, abuse, and security issues
- Comply with legal obligations

## AI Features

WildcatIQ includes AI features that send your data to AI providers to process your requests. Orion and document scanning use Anthropic. Text extraction and search use Mistral AI. Image features use Google. Voice features use ElevenLabs. We do not store your voice recordings.

By default, uploaded documents are scanned by AI to suggest records, such as readings or invoices. Nothing is saved until a user approves it. Orion can also read team messages you have access to. Your organization's administrators can turn off document scanning and Orion's access to team messages.

We do not use your data to train AI models.

## How We Share Your Information

We do not sell your personal information. We share information only in the following circumstances:

**Within Your Organization.** Your organization's administrators control what each user can see and do, including access to operational data, user information, and billing. Facts you ask Orion to remember may be shared with other users in your organization.

**Service Providers.** We share information with vendors who help us run the Services, including:

- Hosting and infrastructure (Vercel, Supabase)
- Payment processing (Stripe)
- Email delivery (Brevo)
- AI processing (Anthropic, Mistral AI, Google, ElevenLabs)
- Push notifications (Expo, Apple, Google)
- Maps (Mapbox)

These providers may use your information only to provide services to us.

**At Your Direction.** If you connect Dropbox, send scheduled reports, or export data, information goes where you direct it.

**Legal Requirements.** We may disclose information if required by law, regulation, legal process, or governmental request.

**Business Transfers.** If we are involved in a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets, your information may be transferred as part of that transaction.

**With Your Consent.** We may share information for other purposes with your consent.

## Data Ownership

Your company owns its data, not WildcatIQ. Administrators control access to it and can export it from the Services.

If your information was entered by a WildcatIQ customer (for example, you are an employee, vendor, or royalty owner of one of our customers), that customer controls it. Please contact them with any requests about your information.

## Data Retention

We keep your data for as long as your account exists. Canceling your subscription ends access but does not delete your data, so you can come back. To have your account or data permanently deleted, contact us.

Some items you delete in the app are hidden rather than erased. You can contact us to have them permanently deleted.

## Security

We protect your information with measures including:

- Encryption of data in transit
- Encrypted storage through our hosting providers
- Database-level separation of each organization's data
- Role-based permissions set by your administrators
- Private storage for uploaded files
- Encrypted sign-in sessions and optional biometric unlock in the mobile app

The offline data on your mobile device relies on your device's own security, so protect your device with a passcode.

No method of transmission or storage is 100% secure. While we work hard to protect your information, we cannot guarantee absolute security.

## Your Rights and Choices

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to:

- Access the personal information we hold about you
- Correct inaccurate information
- Delete your personal information
- Receive a copy of your data
- Control notifications through your account settings

To exercise these rights, contact us at support@wildcatiq.ai or through your organization's administrator. We will not discriminate against you for exercising your rights.

**California and Texas Residents.** Residents of California, Texas, and other states with privacy laws have additional rights, including the right to know what personal information we collect and to request its deletion. We do not sell personal information or use it for targeted advertising.

## Children's Privacy

The Services are not directed to anyone under 16, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 16. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, contact us and we will delete it.

## International Data Transfers

The Services are operated in the United States, and your information is stored and processed there. If you use the Services from outside the United States, your information will be transferred to the United States.

## Changes to This Policy

We may update this policy from time to time. If we make material changes, we will notify you by email or through the Services before they take effect. Continued use of the Services after changes take effect means you accept the updated policy.

## Contact Us

If you have questions about this policy, contact us at:

- **Email:** support@wildcatiq.ai
- **Mail:** WildcatIQ, 5113 S. Harper, Suite 2C, Chicago, IL 60615

This policy is governed by the laws of the State of Illinois.
